## Summary
ImageEnhancementPanel band-ratio silently writes the full input band count with bands 2..N all zeros. Specifically, ImageEnhancementPanel band-ratio output carries the full input band count with bands 2..N all zeros — `bands = 1` is dead because writeGdalOutput writes the whole outputBands vector.

## Area
Core Remote Sensing / Georeferencing / Classification

## Type
correctness

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/dialogs/image_enhancement_panel.cpp:367-368,405-412,445` (ImageEnhancementPanel::onRun (method==2, ratioType==0 path))

## User impact
- Silent wrong output content (data integrity); consumers indexing bands get zeros; wasted file size; contradicts the standalone tool's contract

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (DLGA-4)**: Run a band ratio on any multi-band raster with more than 2 bands via the unified 影像增强 panel

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (DLGA-4)**: Single-band ratio GeoTIFF (the standalone BandRatioDialog correctly builds outputBands with outBandCount=1, band_ratio_dialog.cpp:176,185)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (DLGA-4)**: Output has the input band count; bands 2..N are silently all-zero floats; downstream band-aware operators see a bogus multi-band product

## Root cause
- **DLGA-4**: confirmed
  - *Callchain*: `影像增强 panel → type 波段比值, band1/band2 → 运行 → onRun → runGdalTask worker → ratio fills outputBands[0] only → writeGdalOutput writes all N vectors → user loads N-band TIFF where only band 1 holds the ratio`
  - *Code context*: `Line 367-368 allocate `std::vector<std::vector<float>> outputBands(bands); for (...) outputBands[b].resize(w * h);` (bands = input band count, zero-filled). Ratio branch lines 409-412: `int b1 = std::min(band1, bands); int b2 = std::min(band2, bands); ImageEnhancement::bandRatio( inputBands[b1-1].data(), inputBands[b2-1].data(), outputBands[0].data(), pixelCount); bands = 1;` — only outputBands[0] is written and the local `bands` assignment changes nothing about the vector. Line 445 then calls `writeGdalOutput( outPath, w, h, outputBands, geo.geoTransform, geo.projection, &error )`, and writeGdalOutput (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:505-551) creates the TIFF with `int bandCount = static_cast<int>(bands.size());` — i.e. ALL vectors, writing the untouched zero buffers as bands 2..N.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: No refutation. Verified at HEAD: image_enhancement_panel.cpp:367-368 allocates outputBands initialized to the INPUT band count (zero-filled); the band-ratio branch (:409-412) writes only outputBands[0] and executes the dead `bands = 1;` local reassignment; :445 calls writeGdalOutput which creates the TIFF with `int bandCount = static_cast<int>(bands.size())` (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:511) and writes every vector — bands 2..N are untouched zero buffers. Standalone BandRatioDialog does it correctly (outBandCount=1, band_ratio_dialog.cpp:176,185). Panel is compiled (src/app/CMakeLists.txt:184) and launched from openImageEnhancementPanel.
- **Review note**: None. Severity P2 retained: silent wrong band count in a product users rely on (data integrity).
- **Finding DLGA-4**: `Line 367-368 allocate `std::vector<std::vector<float>> outputBands(bands); for (...) outputBands[b].resize(w * h);` (bands = input band count, zero-filled). Ratio branch lines 409-412: `int b1 = std::min(band1, bands); int b2 = std::min(band2, bands); ImageEnhancement::bandRatio( inputBands[b1-1].data(), inputBands[b2-1].data(), outputBands[0].data(), pixelCount); bands = 1;` — only outputBands[0] is written and the local `bands` assignment changes nothing about the vector. Line 445 then calls `writeGdalOutput( outPath, w, h, outputBands, geo.geoTransform, geo.projection, &error )`, and writeGdalOutput (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:505-551) creates the TIFF with `int bandCount = static_cast<int>(bands.size());` — i.e. ALL vectors, writing the untouched zero buffers as bands 2..N.`

## Suggested fix
- Address the root cause directly with minimal, surgical changes adhering to project coding standards.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (DLGA-4).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #182 fixed band-combo population only; no prior issue on this write path.
- Finding DLGA-4: #182 fixed band-combo population in this panel (cac5da9469) but not the write path; no closed issue mentions the zero-band output; verified writeGdalOutput semantics at HEAD
title: [P2][correctness] ImageEnhancementPanel band-ratio silently writes the full input band count with bands 2..N all zeros

## Summary
SpectralLibraryDialog keeps matching/saving against the previously loaded library after the user Browse-picks a new file. Specifically, SpectralLibraryDialog keeps matching against the previously loaded library after the user picks a different library file — silently wrong match results.

## Area
Core Remote Sensing / Georeferencing / Classification

## Type
correctness

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/dialogs/spectral_library_dialog.cpp:131-137 (browseLibrary), 160-177 (runMatch skips reload), 244-252 (save writes stale library to the new path)` (SpectralLibraryDialog::browseLibrary / runMatch / saveCurrentToLibrary (m_libraryLoaded never invalidated))

## User impact
- Silently incorrect scientific matching results and library-file corruption (stale entries merged into the newly selected library)

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (DLGB-6)**: Load/match one spectral library, then browse to a different JSON and click 匹配 again

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (DLGB-6)**: Dialog reloads the library from the currently shown path (or warns) when the path changes

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (DLGB-6)**: Match scores, ranked table, and entry counts come from the old library; saving then writes old entries into the new file

## Root cause
- **DLGB-6**: confirmed
  - *Callchain*: `user loads library A (or matches once with A) -> Browse selects library B (text changes, no signal handled) -> 匹配 -> runMatch sees m_libraryLoaded==true -> matches against A -> status reports A's entry count; 保存当前谱到库 merges A's entries into file B`
  - *Code context*: `browseLibrary() only sets the edit text: 'm_libraryPathEdit->setText( path );'. runMatch() loads lazily exactly once: 'if ( !m_libraryLoaded ) { ... Library::load( path, &m_library, ... ) ... m_libraryLoaded = true; }' — after the first successful load, m_libraryLoaded stays true forever (no reset on text change/browse; the 'loadedPath' property written at line 147/175 is never read). saveCurrentToLibrary() then writes the stale in-memory m_library to the NEW path: 'const QString path = m_libraryPathEdit->text(); m_library.save( path, ... )'.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: No refutation found. browseLibrary() only does m_libraryPathEdit->setText(path) (:131-137); no textChanged signal is connected anywhere; runMatch() lazy-loads exactly once and m_libraryLoaded stays true forever (:160-177) even after the edit text changes; the 'loadedPath' dynamic property is written (:147,:175) but never read; saveCurrentToLibrary() appends to stale in-memory m_library and saves to the NEW path from the edit text (:244-247), merging old-library entries into the newly picked file.
- **Review note**: None. Severity P2 retained: silently wrong scientific match results plus library-file pollution (data-integrity), though it requires the two-step user flow (match once, then browse to another file).
- **Finding DLGB-6**: `browseLibrary() only sets the edit text: 'm_libraryPathEdit->setText( path );'. runMatch() loads lazily exactly once: 'if ( !m_libraryLoaded ) { ... Library::load( path, &m_library, ... ) ... m_libraryLoaded = true; }' — after the first successful load, m_libraryLoaded stays true forever (no reset on text change/browse; the 'loadedPath' property written at line 147/175 is never read). saveCurrentToLibrary() then writes the stale in-memory m_library to the NEW path: 'const QString path = m_libraryPathEdit->text(); m_library.save( path, ... )'.`

## Suggested fix
- Address the root cause directly with minimal, surgical changes adhering to project coding standards.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (DLGB-6).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

- Not in issues-closed.txt — spectral items (#213/#214/#256) are ROI-tool and curve-recompute, not library reload.
- Finding DLGB-6: Not in issues-closed.txt (spectral items there are #213/#214/#256 — ROI tool and curve recompute); verified at HEAD

## Summary
Closing a running non-modal SicnuAlgorithmDialog (window X, WA_DeleteOnClose) destroys mContext while the worker thread is inside runPrepared - worker-thread UAF (#220 sibling path). Specifically, Closing a running non-modal SicnuAlgorithmDialog via the window X button destroys the dialog while the worker thread is still inside runPrepared using the freed QgsProcessingContext (use-after-free).

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/dialogs/sicnu_algorithm_dialog.cpp:739-759 (contextPtr capture + runPrepared); 609-615 (isFinalized)` (SicnuAlgorithmDialog::runAlgorithm / SicnuProcessingRunState executor lambda / SicnuAlgorithmDialog::isFinalized)

## User impact
- Use-after-free on the GUI-adjacent worker thread: crash or silent memory corruption for any toolbox algorithm closed mid-run; window is the entire algorithm duration (seconds to minutes)

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (DLGB-1)**: Open any Processing Toolbox algorithm dialog (non-modal), press Run, then close the window with the X button while the algorithm is executing

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (DLGB-1)**: Dialog either refuses to close while the Task Center job is in flight, or the run state (context/feedback) is owned by the job so the worker never touches dialog-owned memory after destruction

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (DLGB-1)**: Dialog is destroyed mid-run; the worker thread continues runPrepared against freed QgsProcessingContext memory until the cancel hook (feedback->cancel()) happens to take effect; mContext is used pervasively by every QGIS algorithm

## Root cause
- **DLGB-1**: confirmed
  - *Callchain*: `menu qgis_algorithms:* -> QgisDesktopWindow::openProcessingAlgorithm (main_window_processing.cpp:115-134, sets WA_DeleteOnClose, show()) -> user clicks Run -> SicnuAlgorithmDialog::runAlgorithm -> GuiJobHandle::submitJob -> JobEngine worker thread -> state->algorithm->runPrepared(*contextPtr /* &mContext */, feedbackPtr) -> user clicks window X -> closeEvent accepted -> WA_DeleteOnClose -> ~SicnuAlgorithmDialog frees mContext/mRunState-order members -> worker still dereferences *contextPtr`
  - *Code context*: `runAlgorithm() captures raw pointers into dialog-owned members for the worker-thread executor: 'QgsProcessingContext *contextPtr = &mContext;' (line 739) and 'QgsProcessingFeedback *feedbackPtr = feedback;' (line 740); the worker executes 'state->results = state->algorithm->runPrepared( state->parameters, *contextPtr, feedbackPtr );' (lines 758-759). The only close-while-running guard is isFinalized() (returns false while mJobHandle.isRunning()), which the vendored base consults only to decide its own deleteLater(): QgsProcessingAlgorithmDialogBase::closeEvent (src/gui/processing/qgsprocessingalgorithmdialogbase.cpp:725-736) accepts the close event unconditionally and never ignores it while a Task Center job runs. The sole construction site sets WA_DeleteOnClose before show(): main_window_processing.cpp:129-133 'auto *dlg = new SicnuAlgorithmDialog(this); ... dlg->setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose); dlg->show();'. QWidget::close() honors WA_DeleteOnClose unconditionally (deleteLater), bypassing isFinalized().`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Refutation attempt failed at the strongest counter-argument (that the base closeEvent's isFinalized() guard prevents deletion). Empirically verified with a Qt 6.11 probe: a QDialog with WA_DeleteOnClose whose closeEvent is overridden to ACCEPT without calling deleteLater is still deleted by Qt itself after close()/X (destroyed signal emitted one event-loop turn later). So `QDialog::close()` + WA_DeleteOnClose bypasses QgsProcessingAlgorithmDialogBase::closeEvent's `if(!mAlgorithmTask && isFinalized()) deleteLater();` — that branch only governs the base's own extra deletion. SicnuAlgorithmDialog captures `contextPtr=&mContext` (value member, sicnu_algorithm_dialog.h:74) and `feedbackPtr` into the JobEngine executor (cpp:739-758) which runPrepared's on a std::thread pool worker (JobEngine::m_workers, job_engine.cpp:49-90). Main_window_processing.cpp:129-133 sets WA_DeleteOnClose + show(). Close mid-run => mContext freed while worker dereferences *contextPtr.
- **Review note**: None needed against the mechanism. One scope note: the worker only touches mContext until the cancel hook makes runPrepared return; but no guard bounds that window, so the UAF window spans the whole algorithm duration. #220's fix (5116f95a66) reordered members (mRunState shared_ptr before mJobHandle) and made ~GuiJobHandle cancel synchronously — that protects the mRunState readback but NOT the dialog-owned mContext.
- **Finding DLGB-1**: `runAlgorithm() captures raw pointers into dialog-owned members for the worker-thread executor: 'QgsProcessingContext *contextPtr = &mContext;' (line 739) and 'QgsProcessingFeedback *feedbackPtr = feedback;' (line 740); the worker executes 'state->results = state->algorithm->runPrepared( state->parameters, *contextPtr, feedbackPtr );' (lines 758-759). The only close-while-running guard is isFinalized() (returns false while mJobHandle.isRunning()), which the vendored base consults only to decide its own deleteLater(): QgsProcessingAlgorithmDialogBase::closeEvent (src/gui/processing/qgsprocessingalgorithmdialogbase.cpp:725-736) accepts the close event unconditionally and never ignores it while a Task Center job runs. QWidget::close() honors WA_DeleteOnClose unconditionally (deleteLater), bypassing isFinalized().`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure proper synchronization, atomic state transitions, clean thread termination, and avoidance of use-after-free or race conditions on worker/GUI threads.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (DLGB-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- Not a dup of #220 (which covered ~GuiJobHandle destructor re-entrancy + destroyed-mRunState callback); the X-close/WA_DeleteOnClose mid-run mContext path is genuinely the sibling branch #220's fix left open.

## Summary
Test-suite gates: 5 data-path tests fail for any out-of-tree build (exe-dir walk-up); test_gdal_thread_safety case 2 fails deterministically under per-case ctest; CI only builds in-tree. This issue aggregates 4 related finding(s): BUILD-6, TESTS-3, BUILD-7, TESTS-2. Specifically, Five data-driven tests resolve repo data via an exe-dir walk-up heuristic and fail for ANY out-of-tree build; CI only ever builds in-tree so the gate never sees it. Specifically, 5 ctest entries depend on source-tree-relative data resolution and fail on any out-of-tree build; test_paths.cpp only asserts tautological path properties so the suite cannot catch a wrong root. Specifically, test_gdal_thread_safety case 2 fails deterministically: GDALGetDriverByName before any GDALAllRegister in a per-case process.

## Area
Test Suite / Test Contracts & Invariants

## Type
tests/contract

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/framework/runtime_paths.h:20-30` (sicnu::processing::resolveRuntimeDataPath)
- `tests/test_toolbox_coverage.cpp:23-29 (test_generic_cli_manifest.cpp:43-48, test_pipeline_runner.cpp:388-396, and via provider init test_generic_cli_manifest.cpp:19-41)` (loadManifest / resolveDataPath call sites)
- `tests/test_gdal_thread_safety.cpp:63-73` (GdalDatasetWrapper concurrent open and read on distinct files)
- `tests/test_gdal_thread_safety.cpp:63-86` (TEST_CASE("GdalDatasetWrapper concurrent open and read on distinct files"))

## User impact
- Out-of-tree developers see 5 red tests that are green in CI, eroding trust in the toolbox-coverage gate (which README documents as a CI gate). Same root helper is the source of the installed-app data seam (BUILD-8).
- Suite cannot be run against out-of-tree/paranoid build layouts; masks layout regressions because test_paths.cpp's assertions hold for any root.
- Adds a permanent red test (1 of the 7 audit failures), masking real GDAL thread-safety regressions the suite is meant to catch.
- One of the 7 baseline failures; CI noise that misleads toward a nonexistent GDAL thread-safety regression. It is also the only suite coverage of concurrent GDAL open+read, so the intended concurrency contract currently has zero effective coverage.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (BUILD-6)**: Building in any directory outside the repository (normal CMake practice; note the walk-up also silently binds to any unrelated ancestor that happens to have a data/ directory)
- **Trigger (TESTS-3)**: cmake -S main -B <dir outside repo> && ctest: 5 entries fail. Any in-repo build passes.
- **Trigger (BUILD-7)**: Every ctest run on GDAL builds without implicit lazy driver registration (incl. 3.13; independent of build-tree location)
- **Trigger (TESTS-2)**: Any per-test-case run: ctest (all 1544 discovered this way), ctest -R, ctest --rerun-failed. Passes only when the binary is invoked without a filter (whole-binary runs).

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (BUILD-6)**: Tests locate shipped data via a compiled-in source dir or an installed-data fallback (like qgisRefResourcesDir's install-layout candidates)
- **Expected (TESTS-3)**: Tests locate shipped fixtures independent of build-tree placement (e.g. compiled-in CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR, as test_ui_task_center_contract.cpp already does via QStringLiteral(CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR)).
- **Expected (BUILD-7)**: GDALAllRegister() (or ensureGdalInit()) at the start of the test case, as the sibling case does
- **Expected (TESTS-2)**: Test registers GDAL drivers itself and validates concurrent open+read of distinct files.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (BUILD-6)**: 5 test cases fail deterministically in every out-of-tree build while passing in CI
- **Actual (TESTS-3)**: 5 deterministic failures on out-of-tree builds; CI presumably always builds in-tree so the constraint is invisible.
- **Actual (BUILD-7)**: Deterministic test failure in the suite's only concurrent-GDAL executable
- **Actual (TESTS-2)**: REQUIRE(driver != nullptr) fails deterministically under ctest; the 4 synthetic rasters are never created; the concurrency behavior the test exists to verify is never exercised.

- **BUILD-6**: confirmed

Test binaries live in <build>/tests, so this only finds the source root when the build dir is INSIDE the repo. The walk stopped at /home/kevin (an ancestor that happens to contain data/), yielding /home/kevin/data/tools/custom. Identical binaries pass from the in-tree build dirs (verified: main/build/tests/test_toolbox_coverage 'Toolbox manifest category coverage' → all passed) and fail from audit-build-d9c59e5b82/tests. Sibling tests already use compiled-in paths (e.g. test_pipeline_runner's own TEST_DATA_DIR="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/data" at tests/CMakeLists.txt:2781-2783; test_rpc_golden's GEOREF_TEST_DATA_DIR). These are NOT cwd-relative (the ctest WORKING_DIRECTORY is the build tests dir; resolution is executable-dir-relative) and they WOULD pass with an in-repo build: from <repo>/build/tests the walk stops at the repo root (CMakeLists.txt + data/ present) and data/processing/toolbox_manifest.json, data/tools/custom (5 JSONs), data/pipelines all exist in the repo. test_paths.cpp:24-39 'resolveDataPath produces correct paths' only asserts QFileInfo(path).isAbsolute() and path.endsWith(suffix) — both true for the wrong root '/' — so the path-resolution suite green-lights the broken layout. ## Summary
Build/deps: WITH_EPT option tested before declaration; install_deps.sh missing jsoncpp/qt6-declarative; vendored modes (SICNU_VENDOR_GDAL/SICNU_BUILD_OTB) cannot configure. This issue aggregates 3 related finding(s): BUILD-3, BUILD-4, BUILD-5. Specifically, WITH_EPT is tested before option() is declared: find_package(ZSTD) never runs; EPT decoder compiles/links against zstd by ambient luck. Specifically, install_deps.sh package lists cannot configure or compile the project (jsoncpp missing everywhere; qt6-declarative missing on 3 of 4 distros). Specifically, Vendored-dep modes cannot configure: SICNU_VENDOR_GDAL includes not-yet-built configs; SICNU_BUILD_OTB points at a partial/absent source tree and sets SICNU_HAS_OTB unconditionally.

## Area
Build System / Packaging / Installation

## Type
build/portability

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `CMakeLists.txt:81-84, 179-180` (WITH_EPT / ZSTD_LIBRARY)
- `scripts/install_deps.sh:39-125` (install_arch/install_ubuntu/install_fedora/install_macos)
- `CMakeLists.txt:59-74, 494-506` (SICNU_VENDOR_GDAL / SICNU_BUILD_OTB / SICNU_HAS_OTB)

## User impact
- Point-cloud EPT/COPC decode support (on by default) is un-declared as a dependency: breaks the documented Windows build tier, and on Linux any GDAL/Qt built without zstd turns into a link failure far from the root cause.
- The documented bootstrap path for every supported platform produces a broken environment; users must reverse-engineer the real dependency set from .github/workflows/ci.yml.
- README-documented SICNU_VENDOR_GDAL/SICNU_BUILD_OTB flows are unusable; a clean-clone OTB attempt leaves the user with an unrelated-looking CMake error about test_otb_smoke.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (BUILD-3)**: Any toolchain where zstd is not ambient: MSVC + vcpkg manifest mode (the Tier-3 Windows CI config) does not add vcpkg installed includes globally → `fatal error C1083: cannot open include file: 'zstd.h'` (and unresolved ZSTD_* at link even if the header were found)
- **Trigger (BUILD-4)**: Fresh machine following the README one-step dependency install on any supported distro
- **Trigger (BUILD-5)**: Any use of the two documented vendored-dependency switches on a fresh clone / this checkout

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (BUILD-3)**: option(WITH_EPT ...) declared before its first use (or the find_package moved below), so ZSTD_INCLUDE_DIR/ZSTD_LIBRARY are populated and qgis_core links an explicit zstd
- **Expected (BUILD-4)**: Lists include jsoncpp (+ qt6-declarative family) so the documented flow configures and compiles
- **Expected (BUILD-5)**: Vendor mode bootstraps (two-phase or guarded includes); OTB mode either builds or cleanly disables, and SICNU_HAS_OTB reflects reality

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (BUILD-3)**: zstd dependency silently absent from the build graph; compilation succeeds only on systems where zstd.h/libzstd are ambient
- **Actual (BUILD-4)**: Fresh-machine flow fails at configure (Qt components / version) and would fail at compile (jsoncpp) even then
- **Actual (BUILD-5)**: Both optional modes abort at configure; the OTB skip path additionally poisons the test configuration

## Root cause
- **BUILD-3**: confirmed
  - *Callchain*: `configure (line 81: WITH_EPT undefined → no find_package(ZSTD)) → qgis_core compiles qgseptdecoder.cpp with no zstd -I and links no zstd → resolves only via ambient system/Qt-GDAL transitive deps`
  - *Code context*: `CMakeLists.txt:81-84 `if(WITH_EPT) find_package(ZSTD REQUIRED) endif()` executes at line 81, but `option(WITH_EPT "" ON)` is declared later at line 180 — WITH_EPT is undefined at the point of the test, so the branch is dead and find_package(ZSTD) never runs (ZSTD_* absent from the audit build's CMakeCache). Downstream, src/core/CMakeLists.txt:2326 `include_directories(SYSTEM ${ZSTD_INCLUDE_DIR})` and :2811-2815 `if (WITH_EPT) target_link_libraries(qgis_core ${ZSTD_LIBRARY})` therefore inject empty values, while src/core/pointcloud/qgseptdecoder.cpp:20 `#include <zstd.h>` + :196-210 real ZSTD_* API calls are compiled whenever WITH_EPT OR WITH_COPC (both default ON at root lines 179-180). On Linux this only works accidentally: zstd.h is in the compiler default include path and libzstd.so.1 arrives transitively (ldd of built libqgis_core.so resolves via another linked lib; nm shows 4 undefined ZSTD_* refs). cmake/FindZSTD.cmake and the vcpkg.json `zstd` (windows) entry exist but are never used for this.`
- **BUILD-4**: confirmed

## Summary
RsSimpleSegmenter convolves NoData sentinels/NaN into valid pixels before quantization - OBIA quantize collapses scenes. Specifically, RsSimpleSegmenter convolves NoData sentinels/NaN into valid pixels before quantization - declared-NoData scenes collapse into 1-2 giant segments.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/analysis/segmentation/rs_simple_segmenter.cpp:218-320 (gaussianSmooth 252-260, quantize 286-318), segmentMultiBand path 135-164` (RsSimpleSegmenter::gaussianSmooth / RsSimpleSegmenter::quantize / RsSimpleSegmenter::segmentMultiBand)

## User impact
- Silent total quality collapse of the built-in segmenter whenever NoData touches data (rs:obia_classify then logs 'yielded few objects; falling back to grid' and silently degrades to grid cells; rs:obia_segment emits a 1-segment label map that flows into features/classify/polygonize).

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSHYP-1)**: Any input with NoData adjacent to valid data: declared -9999/-3.4e38/0 sentinel (extremely common: Landsat edges, clipped orthos, QUAC/calibration outputs) or NaN pixels when nothing is declared. Both rs:obia_segment and rs:obia_classify(segmentMethod=quantize) and the GUI fallback hit it.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSHYP-1)**: NoData pixels are excluded from the Gaussian kernel (or at least from the quantization min/max), so valid pixels spread across the full bins range and segments reflect image structure.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSHYP-1)**: Sentinel mixtures stretch vmin..vmax by ~40x, collapsing all valid pixels into bin 1: the connected-components stage yields 1-2 segments covering the whole scene. With NaN NoData (undeclared rasters) the kernel spreads NaN to the (2*half+1)^2 neighborhood per band, so quantize marks those VALID pixels bin 0 - the NoData mask dilates by the kernel radius in every band and the composite drops the union.

## Root cause
- **RSHYP-1**: confirmed (mechanism real; illustrative math corrected)
  - *Callchain*: `rs:obia_segment (src/operators/rs/rs_obia_segment_operator.cpp:117-128, nodata = band-1 declared value else NaN) and rs:obia_classify quantize path (src/operators/rs/rs_obia_classify_operator.cpp:203-211) -> RsSimpleSegmenter::segmentMultiBand; OBIA GUI fallback (src/app/obia/rs_obia_segmentation.cpp:100, nodata = declared value else -9999.0f when undeclared) -> segmentMultiBand`
  - *Code context*: `gaussianSmooth runs on the raw copy with no nodata masking: 'float val = 0.0f; for ( int k = 0; k < kernelSize; ++k ) { int cc = std::clamp( c + k - half, 0, w - 1 ); val += srcRow[cc] * kernel[k]; }' (lines 253-259). quantize() then computes vmin/vmax over the SMOOTHED data excluding only values that still exactly equal the sentinel: 'if ( v != nodata && !std::isnan( v ) ) { if ( v < vmin ) vmin = v; ... }' (lines 292-298). A valid pixel adjacent to NoData becomes a sentinel mixture (e.g. 0.6*DN + 0.4*(-9999) ~ -4000) which is != nodata, so it enters vmin/vmax. The post-hoc mask at lines 60-64/150/164 re-marks only ORIGINAL NoData pixels as bin 0 - it cannot repair the destroyed scale: 'const float scale = ( bins - 1 ) / ( vmax - vmin ); ... result[i] = 1 + static_cast<int>( ( data[i] - vmin ) * scale );' (lines 311-317). With DN 0-255, sentinel -9999, kernel 5, vmin ~ -4000..-9990 -> scale ~ 31/10000 -> every valid pixel lands in bin 1.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Refutation partially succeeds on the finding's OWN arithmetic, not on the defect. I simulated the exact gaussianSmooth (line-buffered separable, kernel 5) + quantize on a 300x300 structured 0-255 DN scene with -9999 border NoData: vmin lands ~-4493 (sentinel blended into valid pixels, since the mixture != sentinel and not NaN), scale=(bins-1)/(vmax-vmin) compresses valid pixels from 64 bins to 13 distinct bins, and connected-components segment count drops 24412 -> 175 (~140x). For reflectance-scale data (0-1 valid vs -9999 sentinel) ALL interior valid pixels land in a single bin (bins 17-31 only from contaminated boundary rings) — i.e. full collapse toward 1-2 giant segments. So the claimed 'collapse to 1-2 segments' holds in the reflectance/small-dynamic-range case and is a severe-but-not-total collapse for DN data; the finding's literal example ('vmin~-4000..-9990 -> every valid pixel lands in bin 1') is wrong — valid pixels land in the TOP bins (1 + (v - vmin)*scale), not bin 1. NaN-NoData case verified: smoothing dilates NaN to (2*half+1)^2 neighborhoods (6208 vs 5080 pixels at kernel 5), poisoning quantization of valid pixels. The #168 post-hoc raw-data re-mask (lines 60-64) only re-bins ORIGINAL nodata pixels to 0 and cannot repair the destroyed scale.
- **Review note**: Correct the evidence's arithmetic example (bins land near the top of the range, and collapse magnitude depends on sentinel/valid-range ratio); the mechanism, reachability (rs:obia_segment operator, rs:obia_classify quantize path, OBIA GUI fallback all pass declared/NaN nodata into segmentMultiBand), and impact (silent quality collapse; rs:obia_classify's <8-segment grid fallback) are all verified at HEAD.
- **Finding RSHYP-1**: `gaussianSmooth runs on the raw copy with no nodata masking: 'float val = 0.0f; for ( int k = 0; k < kernelSize; ++k ) { int cc = std::clamp( c + k - half, 0, w - 1 ); val += srcRow[cc] * kernel[k]; }' (lines 253-259). quantize() then computes vmin/vmax over the SMOOTHED data excluding only values that still exactly equal the sentinel: 'if ( v != nodata && !std::isnan( v ) ) { if ( v < vmin ) vmin = v; ... }' (lines 292-298). A valid pixel adjacent to NoData becomes a sentinel mixture (e.g. 0.6*DN + 0.4*(-9999) ~ -4000) which is != nodata, so it enters vmin/vmax. The post-hoc mask at lines 60-64/150/164 re-marks only ORIGINAL NoData pixels as bin 0 - it cannot repair the destroyed scale: 'const float scale = ( bins - 1 ) / ( vmax - vmin ); ... result[i] = 1 + static_cast<int>( ( data[i] - vmin ) * scale );' (lines 311-317). With DN 0-255, sentinel -9999, kernel 5, vmin ~ -4000..-9990 -> scale ~ 31/10000 -> every valid pixel lands in bin 1.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (RSHYP-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- Nothing prior covers the segmenter nodata bleed; #168 is a PR (19843d1b69) whose masking rework demonstrably left the smoothing bleed and vmin/vmax contamination in place (diff verified).
- Finding RSHYP-1: No closed issue covers the segmenter: #193/#190 (spatial filters/OpenCV pipeline NoData) and #200 (kmeans training NoData) are different modules. The nodata-masking rework in 19843d1b69 (#168, 'enhance ... nodata masking') only added the raw-data re-mask at lines 60-64/150-164 and left the smoothing bleed and vmin/vmax contamination in place - genuinely incomplete fix.
title: [P2][algorithm/numerics] RsSimpleSegmenter convolves NoData sentinels/NaN into valid pixels before quantization - OBIA quantize collapses scenes

## Summary
rs:endmember_extraction returns full per-pixel ppiCounts array in tool result (50-100 MB JSON on 25 MP). Specifically, rs:endmember_extraction returns the full per-pixel ppiCounts array (W*H JSON numbers) in the tool result.

## Area
Core Remote Sensing / Georeferencing / Classification

## Type
correctness

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/operators/rs/rs_endmember_extraction_operator.cpp:357-360` (RsEndmemberExtractionOperator::run)

## User impact
- MCP responses blow past transport/LLM context limits (agent tool calls become unusable or truncated mid-JSON); logger memory inflates by ~24 bytes/pixel per run; schema/outputs contract drift.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (OPS-5)**: rs:endmember_extraction on any real scene: a 25 MP Landsat tile returns a 25,000,000-element JSON array (~40-100 MB serialized); even a 1024x1024 teaching scene returns ~1M numbers.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (OPS-5)**: Per-pixel counts belong in a raster/sidecar, not the result map; result should carry endmembers, indices, and at most top-K counts.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (OPS-5)**: The full pixel-sized array is embedded in the operator result, the MCP tool response, the pipeline result payload, and the operation logger.

## Root cause
- **OPS-5**: confirmed
  - *Callchain*: `MCP execute_algorithm -> JobEngine 'processing:' executor -> RsOperatorAdapter::execute -> run(); the whole result becomes info.resultPayload and is returned verbatim by the MCP get_execution_result handler (src/agent/mcp_server.cpp:330-333); the GUI execute() path additionally stores a copy in the in-memory RSOperationLogger (rs_operation_logger.cpp:43-47).`
  - *Code context*: ``Json::Value countsJson(Json::arrayValue); for (int c : result.ppiCounts) countsJson.append(c); json["ppiCounts"] = countsJson;` — result.ppiCounts is std::vector<int> sized pixelCount (allocated at line 287). The schema outputs (lines 32-38) declare only endmembers/indices; ppiCounts is an undeclared, unbounded result key.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Attempted refutation failed. Verified at HEAD: run() allocates std::vector<int> counts(pixelCount) (rs_endmember_extraction_operator.cpp:103,287) and emits the whole pixel-sized array via json["ppiCounts"] (357-360). Result payload flows verbatim to MCP get_execution_result (src/agent/mcp_server.cpp:331-332 -> jsonValueToVariant) and to the in-memory RSOperationLogger; schema() declares only endmembers/indices so ppiCounts is an undeclared unbounded result key. A 25MP scene => 25M-int JSON array (~40-100MB). Confirmed empirically by code trace; no size cap anywhere.
- **Review note**: Impact estimate sound; exact serialized size depends on int JSON digits (~5-11 bytes/number), 40-100MB ballpark for 25MP plausible. Severity P2 retained (primary agent/MCP surface rendered unusable on any real scene; contract drift).
- **Finding OPS-5**: ``Json::Value countsJson(Json::arrayValue); for (int c : result.ppiCounts) countsJson.append(c); json["ppiCounts"] = countsJson;` — result.ppiCounts is std::vector<int> sized pixelCount (allocated at line 287). The schema outputs (lines 32-38) declare only endmembers/indices; ppiCounts is an undeclared, unbounded result key.`

## Suggested fix
- Address the root cause directly with minimal, surgical changes adhering to project coding standards.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (OPS-5).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- No prior issue on result-map size; #239 and #238 are unrelated catalog perf minors; verified against issues-closed.txt.
- Finding OPS-5: #239 (catalog perf minors) and #238 unrelated; no prior issue about result-map size. Verified at HEAD.

## Summary
gdal:retype/folder outputs: FolderDestination results never returned (#196 four-type gate misses folders). Specifically, gdal:retile OUTPUT_DIR (FolderDestination) is never inserted into results — processAlgorithm's output loop only handles raster/vector/sink/file destination types, so retile returns an empty results map on success (#196 class, folder case).

## Area
Processing Framework / GDAL & OTB Providers

## Type
processing/provider

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/providers/gdal_tools/gdal_tool_wrapper.cpp:103-141 (with src/processing/providers/gdal_tools/algorithms/gdal_retile.cpp:10-12)` (GdalToolWrapper::processAlgorithm)

## User impact
- gdal:retile outputs are invisible to the pipeline/asset layer (and to any consumer expecting the schema-promised OUTPUT_DIR), duplicating the #196 dropped-output failure mode for folder destinations

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (PROVG-6)**: Run gdal:retile successfully (tiles written under OUTPUT_DIR)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (PROVG-6)**: results["OUTPUT_DIR"] = resolved directory path so TaskCenter/OutputCommitter register the output and pipeline chaining works

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (PROVG-6)**: Empty results map; tiles exist on disk but no output path is returned/registered anywhere

## Root cause
- **PROVG-6**: CONFIRMED (P2; GdalToolWrapper::processAlgorithm (gdal_tool_wrapper.cpp:108-113) output collection loop only inspects RasterDestination, VectorDestination, FeatureSink, and FileDestination; algorithms using QgsProcessingParameterFolderDestination (such as gdal_retile.cpp:12 OUTPUT_DIR) have their outputs omitted, returning an empty results map)
  - *Callchain*: `Pipeline/dialog -> TaskCenter -> ProviderAlgorithmAdapter::execute -> GdalToolWrapper::processAlgorithm (results {}) -> postProcess -> OutputCommitter / $stepId.output placeholder resolution finds nothing`
  - *Code context*: `The results loop gates on `type == QgsProcessingParameterRasterDestination::typeName() || QgsProcessingParameterVectorDestination::typeName() || QgsProcessingParameterFeatureSink::typeName() || QgsProcessingParameterFileDestination::typeName()`; gdal_retile declares `addParameter(new QgsProcessingParameterFolderDestination("OUTPUT_DIR", ...))` whose typeName() is "folderDestination" (verified in qgsprocessingparameters.h:3957) — it matches none of the four, so `results` stays empty even on success. resolveDestinationParameters (lines 41-66) uses the same four-type gate. #196's stdout->FileDestination fallback likewise does not apply.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Inspected gdal_tool_wrapper.cpp line 108: FolderDestination type is absent from the if condition; results map remains empty on success.
- **Review note**: None. #196 fixed FileDestination outputs but missed FolderDestination.
- **Finding PROVG-6**: `The results loop gates on `type == QgsProcessingParameterRasterDestination::typeName() || QgsProcessingParameterVectorDestination::typeName() || QgsProcessingParameterFeatureSink::typeName() || QgsProcessingParameterFileDestination::typeName()`; gdal_retile declares `addParameter(new QgsProcessingParameterFolderDestination("OUTPUT_DIR", ...))` whose typeName() is "folderDestination" (verified in qgsprocessingparameters.h:3957) — it matches none of the four, so `results` stays empty even on success. resolveDestinationParameters (lines 41-66) uses the same four-type gate. #196's stdout->FileDestination fallback likewise does not apply.`

## Suggested fix
- Align parameter definitions, argument builders, and result harvesting with the QGIS/GDAL/OTB provider execution contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (PROVG-6).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #196 closed (FileDestination output drop fix); cite as [regression-check: #196 fix incomplete for folder destination].
- Finding PROVG-6: #196 fixed FileDestination drops (gdal_info/ogrinfo stdout write + results insert); the folder destination type was left out. Verified at HEAD.

## Summary
raster_merge_bands: cancel during read leaves blocks short - write loop OOB crash/UB. Specifically, raster_merge_bands: user cancellation during the read phase leaves blocks.size() < totalBands, then the write loop indexes blocks[b] out of bounds - UB/crash.

## Area
Error Handling / Exception Safety

## Type
error-handling

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/providers/qgis_algorithms/algorithms/raster/raster_merge_bands.cpp:66-82 vs 117-134` (RasterMergeBandsAlgorithm::processAlgorithm)

## User impact
- deterministic crash on a routine cancel path; #170 rewrote this algorithm but did not make the cancel path safe

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (PROVO-2)**: Start Merge Raster Bands on a multi-band/multi-layer input and press Cancel during the 'Merging raster bands...' read phase

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (PROVO-2)**: cancellation returns a partial/empty result safely (return {} like raster_calculator.cpp:88-89 does)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (PROVO-2)**: out-of-bounds std::vector operator[] then member call on an uninitialized unique_ptr - segmentation fault / memory corruption

## Root cause
- **PROVO-2**: CONFIRMED (P2; RasterMergeBandsAlgorithm::processAlgorithm (raster_merge_bands.cpp:71-82, 117-124) inner loop breaks on feedback->isCanceled() during band reading, leaving blocks.size() < totalBands; execution falls through to GDAL output creation and accesses blocks[b] up to totalBands, causing out-of-bounds memory access / UB / crash on cancel)
  - *Callchain*: `QgisAlgorithmsProvider::loadAlgorithms -> run raster_merge_bands -> processAlgorithm -> user clicks Cancel while bands are being read -> blocks.size()==currentBand < totalBands -> blocks[b] reads past end of std::vector<std::unique_ptr<QgsRasterBlock>> -> dereference of garbage pointer in hasNoDataValue()/bits()`

## Summary
Image fusion skips the entire PixelSizeMismatch verdict - mirrored/south-up/rotated inputs accepted and silently flipped. Specifically, image_fusion skips the whole PixelSizeMismatch verdict to allow heterogeneous resolution — which also skips the #191 mirrored/south-up orientation and rotation blocks, so mirrored or rotated MS inputs fuse silently flipped/misplaced.

## Area
Data Model / Raster Grids / NoData & CRS

## Type
data/crs-nodata-metadata

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/image_fusion.cpp (consumer) + src/data/raster_grid_compat.cpp (verdict producer, fed by src/processing/gdal/gdal_grid_compat.cpp):image_fusion.cpp:716-727; raster_grid_compat.cpp:151-173` (ImageFusion::process / sicnu::data::compareGrids)

## User impact
- Silently wrong fusion output — the exact mirrored-grid defect class #191 was fixed for, re-entering through the fusion consumer

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (PROVG-5)**: Fuse a pan raster with an MS raster stored south-up/mirrored (old ERDAS/Landsat-style) or carrying rotation terms; |pixel sizes| equal (mirror case)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (PROVG-5)**: Mirrored/rotated inputs are rejected with the #191 rectify message (orientation and rotation are not fixable by read-time resampling); only genuine |size| differences are tolerated for resampling

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (PROVG-5)**: Mirror/rotation/size are conflated into one verdict the fusion path skips; mirrored MS content is fused vertically flipped, rotated content is read through axis-aligned window math and misplaced

## Root cause
- **PROVG-5**: CONFIRMED (P2; ImageFusion::runStreamingFusion (image_fusion.cpp:714-727) skips the entire GridCompatVerdict::PixelSizeMismatch issue to allow differing pan/MS resolution, but compareGrids (raster_grid_compat.cpp:151-172) groups axis orientation (mirrored/south-up) and rotation under PixelSizeMismatch, thus silently bypassing #191 orientation safety checks in fusion)
  - *Callchain*: `rs:image_fusion / pan-sharpening dialog -> AlgorithmEngine -> ImageFusion::process -> compareGrids(gridFromDataset(pan), gridFromDataset(ms)) -> tile loop fusing flipped/misplaced MS`
  - *Code context*: `Fusion preflight: `for (issue : gridReport.issues) { if (issue.verdict == PixelSizeMismatch) { continue; } if (issue.blocking) return false; }`. compareGrids emits axisOrientationMismatch ('gt[1]*gt[1b] <= 0 || gt[5]*gt[5b] <= 0', i.e. #191's mirrored/south-up detector), rotation (gt[2]/gt[4] != 0) AND plain size differences all under the single verdict GridCompatVerdict::PixelSizeMismatch with an early return — so for any heterogeneous pair the ONLY grid gate fusion applies is CRS equality. The comment at image_fusion.cpp:779-781 even asserts 'compareGrids allows PixelSizeMismatch (non-blocking)', which is false — it is blocking; the consumer bypasses it. For a mirrored MS with equal |pixel size|, scaleX/scaleY are 1.0 -> resampleMs=false -> identity readBandWindow reads the south-up raster as if north-up.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Examined raster_grid_compat.cpp: axisOrientationMismatch and rotated emit GridCompatVerdict::PixelSizeMismatch. In image_fusion.cpp:716, if (issue.verdict == PixelSizeMismatch) continue; skips all of them.
- **Review note**: None. Skips entire verdict instead of checking only scalar pixel size difference.
- **Finding PROVG-5**: `Fusion preflight: `for (issue : gridReport.issues) { if (issue.verdict == PixelSizeMismatch) { continue; } if (issue.blocking) return false; }`. compareGrids emits axisOrientationMismatch ('gt[1]*gt[1b] <= 0 || gt[5]*gt[5b] <= 0', i.e. #191's mirrored/south-up detector), rotation (gt[2]/gt[4] != 0) AND plain size differences all under the single verdict GridCompatVerdict::PixelSizeMismatch with an early return — so for any heterogeneous pair the ONLY grid gate fusion applies is CRS equality. The comment at image_fusion.cpp:779-781 even asserts 'compareGrids allows PixelSizeMismatch (non-blocking)', which is false — it is blocking; the consumer bypasses it. For a mirrored MS with equal |pixel size|, scaleX/scaleY are 1.0 -> resampleMs=false -> identity readBandWindow reads the south-up raster as if north-up.`

## Suggested fix
- Validate grid compatibility rigorously, propagate NoData masks across all processing steps, and preserve CRS/metadata on output datasets.

## Summary
readBandWindowScaled out-of-raster padding contract false on current GDAL - RasterIO overwrites prefill with 0/band-NoData. Specifically, readBandWindowScaled's out-of-raster padding contract is false on current GDAL — RasterIO overwrites the pre-filled nodata with 0 (or the band's own NoData), so heterogeneous pan/MS fusion edge tiles read fake zero data.

## Area
Processing Framework / GDAL & OTB Providers

## Type
processing/provider

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/gdal/gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:294-308` (GdalDatasetWrapper::readBandWindowScaled)

## User impact
- Silent data corruption along the right/bottom edges of pansharpened/heterogeneous fusion outputs; fake zeros propagate into downstream statistics and classification

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (PROVG-4)**: Heterogeneous-resolution fusion (pan res != MS res). The MS window msW = ceil((xOff+tw)*scaleX) - msXOff rounds past the MS edge on the last tile column/row whenever width*scale is non-integer; extents of pan/MS are also unchecked for heterogeneous pairs because compareGrids early-returns at PixelSizeMismatch and image_fusion skips that verdict (see PROVG-5)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (PROVG-4)**: Out-of-raster buffer region contains the caller-supplied nodata so the fusion kernel masks it (kernel checks msData[i] == nodata || isnan)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (PROVG-4)**: Region contains 0 for MS bands without declared NoData — a valid DN — so edge pixels are fused as real zero-reflectance data (or the MS band's own sentinel, which != the fusion nodata)

## Root cause
- **PROVG-4**: CONFIRMED (P2; GdalDatasetWrapper::readBandWindowScaled (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:294-308) pre-fills buffer with NoData and assumes GDALRasterIO will leave out-of-raster padding untouched; GDALRasterIO returns CE_Failure whenever xOff+srcWidth > rasterWidth or yOff+srcHeight > rasterHeight, failing edge tile reads in pan/MS fusion)
  - *Callchain*: `AlgorithmEngine -> ImageFusion::process tile loop (src/processing/algorithms/image_fusion.cpp:803-814 readMsWindow -> msDataset.readBandWindowScaled(band, msXOff, msYOff, msW, msH, buf, tw, th, nodata)) -> GdalDatasetWrapper::readBandWindowScaled -> GDALRasterIO`
  - *Code context*: `Comment claims 'GDAL resamples the source window into the buffer and handles a window that extends past the raster edge by only filling the valid intersection, leaving the rest of the buffer at its pre-filled value', implemented as std::fill(buffer, buffer + bufWidth*bufHeight, nodata) followed by GDALRasterIO(band, GF_Read, xOff, yOff, srcWidth, srcHeight, ...) with the UNCLAMPED window (negative offsets allowed by the line-301 guard). Empirically verified on the linked GDAL 3.13.2 via `gdal_translate -srcwin -1 -1 6 6`: out-of-source pixels come back as 0 when the band declares no NoData, and as the band's declared NoData when it does — the caller's pre-fill is clobbered in both cases.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Verified GDAL C API specification for GDALRasterIO: requesting an access window extending beyond raster dimensions returns CE_Failure with CPLE_IllegalArg.
- **Review note**: None. Contract assumption vs GDAL C API contract confirmed.
- **Finding PROVG-4**: `Comment claims 'GDAL resamples the source window into the buffer and handles a window that extends past the raster edge by only filling the valid intersection, leaving the rest of the buffer at its pre-filled value', implemented as std::fill(buffer, buffer + bufWidth*bufHeight, nodata) followed by GDALRasterIO(band, GF_Read, xOff, yOff, srcWidth, srcHeight, ...) with the UNCLAMPED window (negative offsets allowed by the line-301 guard). Empirically verified on the linked GDAL 3.13.2 via `gdal_translate -srcwin -1 -1 6 6`: out-of-source pixels come back as 0 when the band declares no NoData, and as the band's declared NoData when it does — the caller's pre-fill is clobbered in both cases.`

## Suggested fix
- Align parameter definitions, argument builders, and result harvesting with the QGIS/GDAL/OTB provider execution contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (PROVG-4).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests

- issues-closed.txt scanned; no closed issue on readBandWindowScaled boundary handling.
- Finding PROVG-4: #174 is the apply_mask window bug (operators, different symbol); #202 covers output NoData declaration. No prior issue or sibling-agent finding covers readBandWindowScaled fill semantics. Verified at HEAD.
title: [P2][processing/provider] readBandWindowScaled out-of-raster padding contract false on current GDAL - RasterIO overwrites prefill with 0/band-NoData

## Summary
Lee speckle filter interprets noiseVariance as absolute while siblings use relative CV^2 - Lee is a no-op with dialog defaults. Specifically, Lee speckle filter treats noiseVariance as absolute data-unit variance while the sibling filters treat the same parameter as relative CV^2 - Lee is a no-op on DN-scale SAR.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/image_enhancement.cpp:681-686` (ImageEnhancement::leeFilter)

## User impact
- The default speckle method silently does nothing on typical SAR data while the parameter tooltip says it is the speckle variance; inconsistent semantics across the four filters also makes cross-filter comparisons meaningless.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSALGO-6)**: Lee filter with the documented relative noise-variance parameter on non-normalized SAR amplitude/backscatter data (DN in hundreds-thousands)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSALGO-6)**: weight = clSq/(clSq + cuSq) with clSq = localVar/mean^2 (relative, consistent with enhanced Lee/Kuan/Gamma-MAP)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSALGO-6)**: weight = localVar/(localVar + cuSq) ~= 1 -> filter is an identity operation; users see zero speckle reduction

## Root cause
- **RSALGO-6**: CONFIRMED (P2; ImageEnhancement::leeFilter (image_enhancement.cpp:684) computes weight = localVar / (localVar + noiseVariance), treating noiseVariance as absolute variance in DN^2, whereas enhancedLeeFilter (line 724) and standard SAR filtering treat noiseVariance as relative speckle variance Cu^2 = 1/ENL ~ 0.25; on SAR data where localVar >> 1, weight is ~1.0, rendering the default Lee filter an identity no-op)
  - *Callchain*: `speckle_filter_dialog.cpp:128 and image_enhancement_panel.cpp:432 -> ImageEnhancement::leeFilter`
  - *Code context*: `leeFilter: `float weight = localVar / (localVar + noiseVariance); out = mean + weight*(pixel - mean);` - localVar is in data units squared. enhancedLeeFilter:724 computes `cu = sqrt(noiseVariance)` and compares against `cl = sqrt(localVar)/mean` (a coefficient of variation) -> treats noiseVariance as relative CV^2; kuanFilter:906-909 and gammaMapFilter:975 likewise use `cuSq = noiseVariance` against `clSq = localVar/(mean*mean)`. Both GUI callers feed a relative-scale parameter: speckle_filter_dialog.cpp:58 default 1.0 (range 0.001-10) and image_enhancement_panel.cpp:236 default 0.1 (range 0.001-1.0). For SAR amplitude DN with mean ~1000, speckle CV^2=0.1: localVar ~ 1e5, weight = 1e5/(1e5+0.1) ~= 1.0 -> output == input (no despeckling), whereas the correct relative form gives weight = clSq/(clSq+cuSq) ~ 0.5.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Examined math: in Lee (1980) multiplicative model, weight is (localVar - mean^2 * Cu^2) / (localVar * (1 + Cu^2)). Adding noiseVariance to the denominator as an absolute quantity has wrong dimensions (DN^2 vs dimensionless).
- **Review note**: None. Parameter semantics mismatch between sibling filters confirmed.
- **Finding RSALGO-6**: `leeFilter: `float weight = localVar / (localVar + noiseVariance); out = mean + weight*(pixel - mean);` - localVar is in data units squared. enhancedLeeFilter:724 computes `cu = sqrt(noiseVariance)` and compares against `cl = sqrt(localVar)/mean` (a coefficient of variation) -> treats noiseVariance as relative CV^2; kuanFilter:906-909 and gammaMapFilter:975 likewise use `cuSq = noiseVariance` against `clSq = localVar/(mean*mean)`. Both GUI callers feed a relative-scale parameter: speckle_filter_dialog.cpp:58 default 1.0 (range 0.001-10) and image_enhancement_panel.cpp:236 default 0.1 (range 0.001-1.0). For SAR amplitude DN with mean ~1000, speckle CV^2=0.1: localVar ~ 1e5, weight = 1e5/(1e5+0.1) ~= 1.0 -> output == input (no despeckling), whereas the correct relative form gives weight = clSq/(clSq+cuSq) ~ 0.5.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (RSALGO-6).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- issues-closed.txt scanned; no closed issue on Lee filter variance units.
- Finding RSALGO-6: #183 was the stretch-preset off-by-one (image_enhancement.cpp switch mapping, fixed); no closed issue covers speckle filter numerics. Verified current HEAD formula unchanged.
title: [P2][algorithm/numerics] Lee speckle filter interprets noiseVariance as absolute while siblings use relative CV^2 - Lee is a no-op with dialog defaults

## Summary
Atmospheric correction NoData handling incomplete across paths: QUAC percentiles over sentinels; provider adapter feeds NoData as data. This issue aggregates 2 related finding(s): RSALGO-5, PROVO-5. Specifically, QUAC statistics computed over raw DN including declared NoData sentinels - the #190 NoData fix covered only the single-band DOS path. Specifically, atmospheric_correction provider adapter feeds NoData pixels in as data and writes output with no NoData declared - #192 fix missed this file.

## Area
Data Model / Raster Grids / NoData & CRS

## Type
data/crs-nodata-metadata

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/atmospheric_correction.cpp:308-381, 261-306` (AtmosphericCorrection::processFileMultiBand / quac / percentile)
- `src/processing/providers/qgis_algorithms/algorithms/remote_sensing/atmospheric_correction_algorithm.cpp:93-99, 140-147` (AtmosphericCorrectionAlgorithm::processAlgorithm)

## User impact
- QUAC output radiometry wrong on every scene with NoData; magnitude scales with the fraction of fill pixels (a 30% border-filled scene shifts dark[b] entirely to the sentinel).
- numerically wrong atmospheric correction and NoData-contract violation (#192/#202 class); fix incomplete

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSALGO-5)**: QUAC on any raster declaring a numeric NoData sentinel (0, -9999, fill values) - the common case for clipped scenes
- **Trigger (PROVO-5)**: any input raster with NoData pixels (scene edges, nodata=0) using DOS1/DOS2/DN-to-radiance

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSALGO-5)**: NoData pixels excluded from the 1st/99th percentile statistics and mapped to NoData in the output (as the DOS path does post-#190)
- **Expected (PROVO-5)**: NoData masked to NaN and output NoData declared (as the #192 fix did for band math / spectral index / raster_ndvi)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSALGO-5)**: Sentinel values dominate the dark percentile, skewing per-band gains; sentinels are output as clipped reflectance values
- **Actual (PROVO-5)**: NoData DNs are 'corrected' as valid pixels, DOS haze level biased toward the sentinel value, downstream treats nodata as reflectance

## Root cause
- **RSALGO-5**: CONFIRMED (P2; AtmosphericCorrection::processFileMultiBand (atmospheric_correction.cpp:339) reads raw DNs into memory without masking band NoData sentinels before calling quac(), corrupting 1st and 99th percentile statistics on scenes with fill values)
  - *Callchain*: `rs:atmospheric_correction(method=quac) (rs_atmospheric_correction_operator.cpp:237-245) -> AtmosphericCorrection::processFileMultiBand -> quac -> percentile`
  - *Code context*: `processFileMultiBand reads bands with `srcDataset.readBandData(b + 1, dnBands[b].data(), ...)` and never calls bandNoDataValue(); quac then takes `percentile(..., 1.0f)` / `percentile(..., 99.0f)` where the percentile helper partitions out only NaN (`return !std::isnan(v)`). A scene with nodata=0 or -9999 puts the sentinel at the 1st percentile: dark[b] = sentinel, meanDark contaminated, refRange = meanBright - meanDark inflated, gain = 0.5*refRange/(range*meanBright) wrong for every band. Also the sentinel pixels themselves are 'corrected' into clipped [0,1] values instead of passed through as NoData. The sibling single-band path processFile() masks `!isfinite(v) || abs(v - bandNoData) < 1e-4f -> NaN` before statistics (lines 424-430, added in 0169bd7eac for #190/#193) - the multi-band QUAC path was not given the same treatment.`
- **PROVO-5**: CONFIRMED (P2; AtmosphericCorrectionAlgorithm::processAlgorithm (atmospheric_correction_algorithm.cpp:89-147) reads raw block values without checking isNoData(), computes dark level over sentinels, and writes output without setting NoData on outProvider)
  - *Callchain*: `qgis_algorithms:rs_atmospheric_correction -> processAlgorithm -> provider->block(1,...) including NoData -> AtmosphericCorrection::dos1/dos2 findMin corrupted -> Float32 GeoTIFF with no NoData metadata`
  - *Code context*: `Read loop: 'for (size_t i=0;i<totalPixels;++i) { int row=i/nCols; int col=i%nCols; dnData[i]=static_cast<float>(inBlock->value(row,col)); }' - no inBlock->isNoData(i) check, unlike the sibling adapters fixed for #192 (band_math_algorithm.cpp:100-101 and spectral_index_algorithm.cpp:61-62 map NoData to NaN). Output block writes result values unconditionally and never calls outProvider->setNoDataValue / setIsNoData. Downstream, AtmosphericCorrection::dos1 computes findMin() over all pixels (src/processing/algorithms/atmospheric_correction.cpp:25-35), so sentinel NoData (typically 0) becomes the dark-object minimum and corrupts the haze estimate for every pixel.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Inspected atmospheric_correction.cpp: QUAC path percentile() filters std::isnan but not declared band NoData values. Inspected atmospheric_correction_algorithm.cpp: block->value(row, col) is unfiltered; outProvider never receives setNoDataValue.
- **Review note**: None. #190/#192 fixed NoData masking in DOS streaming and band math, but missed QUAC multi-band and the QGIS algorithm provider adapter.
- **Finding RSALGO-5**: `processFileMultiBand reads bands with `srcDataset.readBandData(b + 1, dnBands[b].data(), ...)` and never calls bandNoDataValue(); quac then takes `percentile(..., 1.0f)` / `percentile(..., 99.0f)` where the percentile helper partitions out only NaN (`return !std::isnan(v)`). A scene with nodata=0 or -9999 puts the sentinel at the 1st percentile: dark[b] = sentinel, meanDark contaminated, refRange = meanBright - meanDark inflated, gain = 0.5*refRange/(range*meanBright) wrong for every band. Also the sentinel pixels themselves are 'corrected' into clipped [0,1] values instead of passed through as NoData. The sibling single-band path processFile() masks `!isfinite(v) || abs(v - bandNoData) < 1e-4f -> NaN` before statistics (lines 424-430, added in 0169bd7eac for #190/#193) - the multi-band QUAC path was not given the same treatment.`
- **Finding PROVO-5**: `Read loop: 'for (size_t i=0;i<totalPixels;++i) { int row=i/nCols; int col=i%nCols; dnData[i]=static_cast<float>(inBlock->value(row,col)); }' - no inBlock->isNoData(i) check, unlike the sibling adapters fixed for #192 (band_math_algorithm.cpp:100-101 and spectral_index_algorithm.cpp:61-62 map NoData to NaN). Output block writes result values unconditionally and never calls outProvider->setNoDataValue / setIsNoData. Downstream, AtmosphericCorrection::dos1 computes findMin() over all pixels (src/processing/algorithms/atmospheric_correction.cpp:25-35), so sentinel NoData (typically 0) becomes the dark-object minimum and corrupts the haze estimate for every pixel.`

## Suggested fix

- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## References / Dedupe
- #129 closed (added QUAC method), #190/#192 closed (NoData fixes on OpenCV/indices); cite as [regression-check: #190/#192 fix incomplete].
- Finding RSALGO-5: #190 (commit 0169bd7eac) patched atmospheric_correction.cpp only in the single-band processFile/streaming path; QUAC multi-band path verified still unmasked at HEAD.

## Summary
IHS pan-sharpening forward/inverse transforms inconsistent - colors distorted even with no pan substitution. Specifically, IHS pan-sharpening forward/inverse transforms are mathematically inconsistent - colors distorted even with no pan substitution.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/image_fusion.cpp:407-473 (ihsFusion), 1004-1023 (streaming IHS in processNativeFusion)` (ImageFusion::ihsFusion / ImageFusion::processNativeFusion(method=ihs))

## User impact
- Fused products systematically lose spectral fidelity - wrong colors in the primary visual pan-sharpening method; any downstream classification on fused output inherits the distortion.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSALGO-3)**: Any IHS pan-sharpening run (method=ihs) on multispectral imagery

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSALGO-3)**: Forward/inverse IHS pair consistent: substituting I'=I reproduces the input RGB exactly (within FP)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSALGO-3)**: Hue mirrored (G/B swapped) and chroma shrunk ~3x: saturated colors desaturate and shift even before the pan detail is injected

## Root cause
- **RSALGO-3**: CONFIRMED (P2; ImageFusion::ihsFusion (image_fusion.cpp:407-473) forward transform defines saturation as S = 1 - min(R,G,B)/I from cylindrical HSI model, while inverse transform reconstructs chromatic components using c1 = I*sat*cos(hue) and c2 = I*sat*sin(hue), mixing cylindrical saturation with linear Cartesian chromaticity; inverse formula also swaps signs of sqrt(3)/2*c2 on G and B; result distorts colors even when Pan is identical to Intensity, e.g. (100, 50, 0) reconstructs as (93.3, 6.7, 50.0))
  - *Callchain*: `rs:image_fusion / RsFusionMethodOperator (src/operators/rs/rs_fusion_aliases.cpp:108) -> ImageFusion::processNativeFusion('ihs') lines 991-1023; in-memory ihsFusion has the same math at 412-473`
  - *Code context*: `Forward: `float c1 = red - 0.5f*(green+blue); float c2 = (green-blue)*sqrt(3)/2; H=atan2(c2,c1); S=1-min/I`. Inverse: `newC1 = newI*sat*cos(hue); newC2 = newI*sat*sin(hue); r=newI+newC1; g=newI-0.5*newC1-sqrt(3)/2*newC2; b=newI-0.5*newC1+sqrt(3)/2*newC2`. The inverse does not invert the forward basis: correct inverse of c1=(2r-g-b)/2, c2=(g-b)*sqrt(3)/2 with chroma C=sqrt(c1^2+c2^2) is r=I+(2/3)c1', g=I-c1'/3+c2'/sqrt(3), b=I-c1'/3-c2'/sqrt(3) where |c'|=C; the code instead sets |c'| = I*S (3x too small for the /2-basis, e.g. pure red C=1 vs I*S=1/3) and flips the c2 sign. Round-trip with NO pan change (I'=I): pure red (1,0,0) -> (0.667, 0.167, 0.167); pure green (0,1,0) -> (0.167, 0.167, 0.667) - green becomes blue. A consistent pair exists in the same tree (ImageEnhancement::rgbToIhs/ihsToRgb uses u=(2R-G-B)/sqrt(6), v=(G-B)/sqrt(2), chroma=3*S*I and round-trips exactly) but is not used here.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Verified algebraic and numerical roundtrip: without Pan substitution (pan = (R+G+B)/3), RGB -> IHS -> RGB should be an identity transform. Instead, (100,50,0) yields (93.3, 6.7, 50.0), reversing G and B channels.
- **Review note**: None. Empirically proven with numerical simulation.
- **Finding RSALGO-3**: `Forward: `float c1 = red - 0.5f*(green+blue); float c2 = (green-blue)*sqrt(3)/2; H=atan2(c2,c1); S=1-min/I`. Inverse: `newC1 = newI*sat*cos(hue); newC2 = newI*sat*sin(hue); r=newI+newC1; g=newI-0.5*newC1-sqrt(3)/2*newC2; b=newI-0.5*newC1+sqrt(3)/2*newC2`. The inverse does not invert the forward basis: correct inverse of c1=(2r-g-b)/2, c2=(g-b)*sqrt(3)/2 with chroma C=sqrt(c1^2+c2^2) is r=I+(2/3)c1', g=I-c1'/3+c2'/sqrt(3), b=I-c1'/3-c2'/sqrt(3) where |c'|=C; the code instead sets |c'| = I*S (3x too small for the /2-basis, e.g. pure red C=1 vs I*S=1/3) and flips the c2 sign. Round-trip with NO pan change (I'=I): pure red (1,0,0) -> (0.667, 0.167, 0.167); pure green (0,1,0) -> (0.167, 0.167, 0.667) - green becomes blue. A consistent pair exists in the same tree (ImageEnhancement::rgbToIhs/ihsToRgb uses u=(2R-G-B)/sqrt(6), v=(G-B)/sqrt(2), chroma=3*S*I and round-trips exactly) but is not used here.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Summary
Terrain aspect returns mirrored angle and hillshade mixes azimuth conventions - lighting/aspect wrong except default sun azimuth. Specifically, Terrain aspect returns a mirrored angle (270deg - true compass azimuth) and hillshade mixes azimuth conventions, so lighting is wrong for any sun azimuth except 135/315.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/terrain_analysis.cpp:186-190, 274-278` (TerrainAnalysis::aspect / TerrainAnalysis::hillshade)

## User impact
- Aspect rasters are systematically mirrored (N<->W, E<->S quadrants swapped) - wrong input for landform classification, solar exposure, hydrology. Hillshade renders with wrong light direction for any non-default azimuth; quantitative shade masks wrong.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSALGO-1)**: rs:terrain_analysis with product=aspect (any DEM) or product=hillshade with sunAzimuth outside {135,315} (e.g. 0/45/90/180/225/270 for time-of-day analysis)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSALGO-1)**: aspect = compass azimuth of downhill direction (0=N, 90=E, e.g. east-facing slope -> 90); hillshade term cos(az_compass - aspect_compass)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSALGO-1)**: aspect = 270deg - true azimuth (east-facing -> 180, south-facing -> 90); hillshade lighting rotated/mirrored for azimuths other than 135/315 (default 315 accidentally correct, hiding the bug)

## Root cause
- **RSALGO-1**: CONFIRMED (P2; TerrainAnalysis::aspect (terrain_analysis.cpp:188) computes std::atan2(-dzdy, dzdx) * 180 / M_PI, returning polar angle from East rather than compass azimuth clockwise from North (Horn 1981 / GDAL convention), systematically mirroring and swapping quadrants; test_terrain.cpp:94-127 encodes the inverted formula into test expectations; hillshade (lines 230, 275-278) mixes azRad in compass azimuth with aspectRad in polar angle, rendering correct lighting only at default 315/135 deg)
  - *Callchain*: `RsTerrainAnalysisOperator::run (src/operators/rs/rs_terrain_analysis_operator.cpp:146-149) -> TerrainAnalysis::aspect / TerrainAnalysis::hillshade -> processNativeFusion-style output write`
  - *Code context*: `aspect: `float angle = std::atan2( -dzdy, dzdx ) * toDeg; if ( angle < 0 ) angle += 360.0f;` with dzdx = east-west gradient, dzdy = south-north gradient. atan2(-dzdy, dzdx) is the CCW-from-East math angle of the UPHILL gradient, not the documented compass azimuth of the downhill direction (header: 'aspect in degrees [0, 360), clockwise from north'; GDAL/ESRI convention: azimuth = 90 - atan2(dzdy,-dzdx) mapped to [0,360)). Verify: east-facing slope (dzdx<0, dzdy=0) -> code outputs 180 (South) where GDAL/ESRI output 90 (East); output = 270deg - trueAzimuth for all cases. hillshade: `aspectRad = std::atan2( -dzdy, dzdx )` then `hs = cosZen*cos(slopeRad) + sinZen*sin(slopeRad)*cos(azRad - aspectRad)` mixes azRad (compass, CW-from-north) with aspectRad (CCW-from-East math angle) in one cos difference. Correct term is cos(az - aspect_compass) = cos(az - 270 + m); the code computes cos(az - m) - equal only for az=135/315. Example: sun azimuth 0 (north) on a south-facing slope: correct term = cos(0-180) = -1 (fully shadowed); code computes cos(0-90) = 0 (mid-gray).`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Examined math: dzdx is dZ/dEast, -dzdy is dZ/dNorth. Compass azimuth is atan2(dZ/dEast, dZ/dNorth) or atan2(-dzdx, dzdy). atan2(-dzdy, dzdx) yields 270 - azimuth. In hillshade, cos(azRad - aspectRad) subtracts compass azimuth from polar angle.
- **Review note**: None. Rigorously verified via GDAL gdaldem conventions and test_terrain analysis.
- **Finding RSALGO-1**: `aspect: `float angle = std::atan2( -dzdy, dzdx ) * toDeg; if ( angle < 0 ) angle += 360.0f;` with dzdx = east-west gradient, dzdy = south-north gradient. atan2(-dzdy, dzdx) is the CCW-from-East math angle of the UPHILL gradient, not the documented compass azimuth of the downhill direction (header: 'aspect in degrees [0, 360), clockwise from north'; GDAL/ESRI convention: azimuth = 90 - atan2(dzdy,-dzdx) mapped to [0,360)). Verify: east-facing slope (dzdx<0, dzdy=0) -> code outputs 180 (South) where GDAL/ESRI output 90 (East); output = 270deg - trueAzimuth for all cases. hillshade: `aspectRad = std::atan2( -dzdy, dzdx )` then `hs = cosZen*cos(slopeRad) + sinZen*sin(slopeRad)*cos(azRad - aspectRad)` mixes azRad (compass, CW-from-north) with aspectRad (CCW-from-East math angle) in one cos difference. Correct term is cos(az - aspect_compass) = cos(az - 270 + m); the code computes cos(az - m) - equal only for az=135/315. Example: sun azimuth 0 (north) on a south-facing slope: correct term = cos(0-180) = -1 (fully shadowed); code computes cos(0-90) = 0 (mid-gray).`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (RSALGO-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #203 closed (addressed cellSize geotransform); trigonometric azimuth coordinate conventions were not addressed.
- Finding RSALGO-1: #203 (terrain cellSize from geotransform) fixed only the 30.0 default; aspect/hillshade convention never covered in issues-closed.txt (233 lines read). No commit in `git log -20 -- src/processing/algorithms/` touches the aspect math.

performance/cpu

  - *Callchain*: `QgisDesktopWindow::layerProperties (src/app/main_window_layers.cpp:242) -> ActiveViewHost::showLayerProperties (src/app/active_view_host.cpp:411-416) -> QgsVectorLayerProperties ctor -> full-layer scan.`

## Summary
OBIA window runs full-scene feature extraction synchronously on the GUI thread on every spin change; per-polygon OGR_G_Contains loop on import. Specifically, OBIA window runs full-scene multi-band feature extraction synchronously on the GUI thread on every View-L spinbox change, and a per-pixel OGR point-in-polygon loop on Import ROI.

## Area
Performance / CPU & Main Thread Responsiveness

## Type
performance/cpu

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/obia/rs_obia_main_window.cpp:950-965 (setActiveLevelMap, call to RsSegmentFeatures::extract at 957); 1155-1166 (onActiveLevelChanged); 1442-1630 (importRoiLabels per-pixel loop 1558-1575)` (RsObiaMainWindow::setActiveLevelMap / onActiveLevelChanged / importRoiLabels)

## User impact
- Repeated GUI freezes during normal OBIA level inspection; distinguishes from closed #214/#218/#256 which covered the classification ROI tools and contrast widgets, not the OBIA hierarchy window

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (SHELLB-3)**: After a 2-level hierarchy on a large scene, click the View L spinbox up/down; or import a training polygon covering a large area

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (SHELLB-3)**: Level switch re-indexes asynchronously (or reuses cached per-level stats — the hierarchy task already computed level-0 stats)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (SHELLB-3)**: UI freezes for the duration of a full-scene multi-band read+scan (seconds to tens of seconds on realistic scenes)

## Root cause
- **SHELLB-3**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `View L spinbox valueChanged -> onActiveLevelChanged -> setActiveLevelMap -> RsSegmentFeatures::extract (full-scene GDAL read + full pixel scan on GUI thread); Import ROI button -> importRoiLabels -> per-pixel OGR_G_Contains loop on GUI thread`
  - *Code context*: ``mSegStats = RsSegmentFeatures::extract( mRasterPath, mSegMap, allBandIndices() );` executes directly in the slot. RsSegmentFeatures::extract (src/analysis/segmentation/rs_segment_features.cpp:14-70) opens the raster and reads EVERY requested band into a w*h float buffer (line 48-61: `bandData[b].resize(nPixels); GDALRasterIO(... GF_Read, 0,0,w,h ...)`) then scans every pixel. This runs on the GUI thread each time the user flips the View L spinbox (connected at line 172-173 to onActiveLevelChanged). Same class of defect: importRoiLabels loops `for r... for c...` over each training polygon's envelope calling OGR_G_Contains per pixel center (1559-1572) synchronously — a 10kx10k envelope is 1e8 GEOS point-in-polygon tests.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: View L spinbox valueChanged -> onActiveLevelChanged -> setActiveLevelMap -> 'mSegStats = RsSegmentFeatures::extract(mRasterPath, mSegMap, allBandIndices())' (rs_obia_main_window.cpp:957). RsSegmentFeatures::extract (rs_segment_features.cpp:14-70) GDALOpens the raster and per band GDALRasterIOs the FULL w*h plane into float buffers, then scans every pixel — on the GUI thread. The spin range grows to hierarchy levelCount after a hierarchy completes (lines 979-981), so the trigger is a real user path. importRoiLabels (toolbar action at :203) loops each training polygon's envelope over rows x cols with per-pixel OGR_G_Contains/Intersects synchronously (:1558-1575), and then re-invokes setActiveLevelMap(clsLevel) at :1580 (another full re-extract).
