## Summary
Batch processing still runs every item synchronously on the GUI thread; processEvents re-entrancy lets the file list mutate mid-iteration (UAF). This issue aggregates 3 related finding(s): DLGB-12, DLGA-3, DLGB-11. Specifically, Batch processing still executes every item synchronously on the GUI thread — #184 only gained inter-item cancellation; each item freezes the UI for its full duration. Specifically, Batch dialog #184 fix regression: full QApplication::processEvents() (user input re-enabled) lets Add/Remove mutate m_inputFiles while the loop holds a QString reference across the processEvents window — dangling reference/UAF and index-shift file mixups. Specifically, Batch dialog output-directory handling gaps: typed-but-nonexistent directory is neither created nor pre-validated, and same-basename inputs from different folders silently overwrite each other.

## Area
Performance / CPU & Main Thread Responsiveness

## Type
performance/cpu

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/dialogs/batch_processing_dialog.cpp:408-454 (sequential loop), 416 (processEvents between items), 760 (adapter->execute), 810 (alg->run)` (BatchProcessingDialog::onRun / runBatchItem)
- `src/app/dialogs/batch_processing_dialog.cpp:408-430` (BatchProcessingDialog::onRun)
- `src/app/dialogs/batch_processing_dialog.cpp:363-371 (dir emptiness check only), 424-426 (output naming), 408-454 (loop)` (BatchProcessingDialog::onRun (#217 fix verification))

## User impact
- Multi-minute UI freezes (the original #184 P1 symptom) persist whenever any single item is slow; unsafe shared-instance run can interleave with toolbox runs of the same algorithm
- Crash or corrupted batch run (wrong input processed under wrong output name) triggered by ordinary UI interaction the #184 fix deliberately re-enabled; regression introduced by the fix commit
- Failed batches with confusing per-item errors; silent loss of earlier batch outputs on name collision

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (DLGB-12)**: Batch any real rasters; each item runs seconds-to-minutes with the UI frozen
- **Trigger (DLGA-3)**: During a batch run, click 添加文件… or 移除选中 in the still-enabled file-list buttons while an item is between the processEvents window and runBatchItem
- **Trigger (DLGB-11)**: Type a new directory path into 输出目录, or batch two files with identical basenames

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (DLGB-12)**: Per-item submission through the Task Center/JobEngine seam (as the single-shot dialogs do), enabling true mid-item cancel
- **Expected (DLGA-3)**: Either user-input events excluded (as before #184) or the file list guarded/disabled during the run; inputFile should be a copy (QString, not const QString&)
- **Expected (DLGB-11)**: mkpath (or upfront existence validation) and unique per-file output naming / collision warning

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (DLGB-12)**: GUI frozen for the duration of every item; cancel takes effect only at the next item boundary; shared registry instance mutated per run
- **Actual (DLGA-3)**: List mutation during the live reference yields use-after-free reads of freed QString data (or at minimum wrong file→output mapping from index shifts); Add can also silently extend a running batch
- **Actual (DLGB-11)**: All items fail with generic algorithm write errors when the dir is missing; basename collisions silently destroy earlier results

## Root cause
- **DLGB-12**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `运行批量 -> onRun loop -> runBatchItem -> adapter->execute / alg->run (blocking, GUI thread) -> QApplication::processEvents() only between items`
  - *Code context*: `The loop calls runBatchItem directly on the GUI thread: RS path 'const Json::Value result = adapter->execute(params);' (line 760) and QGIS path 'const QVariantMap results = alg->run(params, context, &feedback);' (line 810). 'QApplication::processEvents();' appears only at line 416 (before each item) so cancel/progress are processed BETWEEN items only; during an item the GUI is fully blocked. Additionally the QGIS path runs the shared REGISTRY algorithm instance ('QgsApplication::processingRegistry()->algorithmById(algorithmId)') rather than the create()/clone() copy that qgsprocessingalgorithm.h:425-430 requires ('not safe to call on algorithms directly retrieved from QgsProcessingRegistry').`
- **DLGA-3**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `运行批量 click → onRun loop iteration i → const QString &inputFile = m_inputFiles[i] → processEvents() → nested dispatch of 添加文件…/移除选中 click → m_inputFiles.append/removeAt (buffer realloc or element destruction) → processEvents returns → QFileInfo(inputFile) / runBatchItem(..., inputFile, ...) read the destroyed QString`
  - *Code context*: `Lines 414-424: `const QString &inputFile = m_inputFiles[i]; m_statusLabel->setText(...); QApplication::processEvents(); if ( m_canceled ) {...} ... QString baseName = QFileInfo( inputFile ).completeBaseName(); ... runBatchItem( algorithmId, inputFile, outputPath, &itemError, overrides );`. The reference into the QStringList is held ACROSS the processEvents() call. Commit cac5da9469 (#184) replaced the previous `QApplication::processEvents(QEventLoop::ExcludeUserInputEvents)` (whose comment said 'Keep UI responsive without re-entering user-input handlers') with plain processEvents(), so during each item the user can click 添加文件… (onAddFiles appends → QList reallocation moves/destroys every QString element) or 移除选中 (onRemoveSelected → m_inputFiles.removeAt(row) destroys/overwrites the referenced element). After the nested event dispatch returns, line 424/430 read/pass the dangling reference. Also, index-based iteration over a mutated list skips/duplicates files and mislabels outputs.`
- **DLGB-11**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `set a typed (nonexistent) output dir, or add two same-named files from different directories -> 运行批量 -> per-item writes fail / second overwrites first -> summary reports 'N failed' or false success with half the data`
  - *Code context*: `The #217 fix itself is present (m_outputDirEdit->text() is now read: textChanged wiring at 257-259 and the fallback read at 363-365). But: (1) the directory is never created or checked for existence — no QDir().mkpath(m_outputDir) / QFileInfo::exists anywhere; every runBatchItem then fails with a per-item error after processing the whole list. (2) Output name is '<completeBaseName>_processed<ext>' with no collision policy: '/a/img.tif' and '/b/img.tif' both map to outDir/img_processed.tif; the second item silently overwrites the first's result. (3) Skip/fail policy and summary reporting ARE implemented (fail-continue loop 428-451, counts + first-8-error box 468-482).`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: m_inputFiles is QStringList (=QList<QString>, header line 107). onRun loop: line 414 binds 'const QString &inputFile = m_inputFiles[i]', line 416 calls plain QApplication::processEvents() (commit cac5da9469 #184 replaced QEventLoop::ExcludeUserInputEvents with the full version), then lines 424/430 read inputFile -> live reference across a window in which the Add (append -> possible QList node-array realloc invalidating every QString element ref) and Remove (removeAt destroys the element and shifts the array) buttons are still enabled (only m_runButton toggles; addFilesBtn/removeBtn never disabled, no setEnabled on them anywhere in the file). Index shift also mislabels outputs. DLGB-12: runBatchItem runs synchronously: RS path adapter->execute (line 760) and QGIS path 'QVariantMap results = alg->run(params, context, &feedback)' (line 810) on the GUI thread; processEvents only between items so the GUI is frozen for an item's whole duration — the original #184 P1 freeze persists, only inter-item cancel was added. The QGIS path also runs the shared registry instance directly (QgsApplication::processingRegistry()->algorithmById), which the vendored contract forbids: qgsprocessingalgorithm.h:412-414 'this method modifies the algorithm instance, so it is not safe to call ... a new instance ... created with clone() and prepare()/runPrepared()'. DLGB-11: #217 fix (8f57fbbd79 reads m_outputDirEdit text via textChanged + onRun fallback) is present, but onRun never mkpath()-s or pre-validates the typed dir and output naming is '<completeBaseName>_processed<ext>' with no collision policy, so same-basename inputs from different folders silently overwrite.
- **Review note**: None; member severities as assigned (DLGB-12 P2, DLGA-3 P2, DLGB-11 P3).
- **Finding DLGB-12**: `The loop calls runBatchItem directly on the GUI thread: RS path 'const Json::Value result = adapter->execute(params);' (line 760) and QGIS path 'const QVariantMap results = alg->run(params, context, &feedback);' (line 810). 'QApplication::processEvents();' appears only at line 416 (before each item) so cancel/progress are processed BETWEEN items only; during an item the GUI is fully blocked. Additionally the QGIS path runs the shared REGISTRY algorithm instance ('QgsApplication::processingRegistry()->algorithmById(algorithmId)') rather than the create()/clone() copy that qgsprocessingalgorithm.h:425-430 requires ('not safe to call on algorithms directly retrieved from QgsProcessingRegistry').`
- **Finding DLGA-3**: `Lines 414-424: `const QString &inputFile = m_inputFiles[i]; m_statusLabel->setText(...); QApplication::processEvents(); if ( m_canceled ) {...} ... QString baseName = QFileInfo( inputFile ).completeBaseName(); ... runBatchItem( algorithmId, inputFile, outputPath, &itemError, overrides );`. The reference into the QStringList is held ACROSS the processEvents() call. Commit cac5da9469 (#184) replaced the previous `QApplication::processEvents(QEventLoop::ExcludeUserInputEvents)` (whose comment said 'Keep UI responsive without re-entering user-input handlers') with plain processEvents(), so during each item the user can click 添加文件… (onAddFiles appends → QList reallocation moves/destroys every QString element) or 移除选中 (onRemoveSelected → m_inputFiles.removeAt(row) destroys/overwrites the referenced element). After the nested event dispatch returns, line 424/430 read/pass the dangling reference. Also, index-based iteration over a mutated list skips/duplicates files and mislabels outputs.`
- **Finding DLGB-11**: `The #217 fix itself is present (m_outputDirEdit->text() is now read: textChanged wiring at 257-259 and the fallback read at 363-365). But: (1) the directory is never created or checked for existence — no QDir().mkpath(m_outputDir) / QFileInfo::exists anywhere; every runBatchItem then fails with a per-item error after processing the whole list. (2) Output name is '<completeBaseName>_processed<ext>' with no collision policy: '/a/img.tif' and '/b/img.tif' both map to outDir/img_processed.tif; the second item silently overwrites the first's result. (3) Skip/fail policy and summary reporting ARE implemented (fail-continue loop 428-451, counts + first-8-error box 468-482).`

## Suggested fix
- Address the root cause directly with minimal, surgical changes adhering to project coding standards.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (DLGB-12, DLGA-3, DLGB-11).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #184 (CLOSED) added cancel only — the synchronous-per-item freeze is its original symptom, incompletely addressed; DLGA-3 is a NEW regression introduced by the same #184 commit. #217 (CLOSED) fixed the text-not-read bug; the remaining dir/collision gaps are completeness. Not duplicative as live issues.
- Finding DLGB-12: #184 (P1, closed by cac5da9469) — that fix added the cancel toggle and inter-item processEvents; verified current HEAD still runs items synchronously, so the core freeze is unfixed
- Finding DLGA-3: Not a dupe of #184 (which reported the sync freeze/no-cancel that cac5da9469 addressed); this is a NEW defect introduced by that same commit's processEvents change — verified at HEAD the call is plain QApplication::processEvents() and the reference spans it
- Finding DLGB-11: #217 (fixed in 8f57fbbd79 — text is now read; verified) but completeness gaps remain at HEAD; not covered elsewhere

## Summary
Ribbon Workflow tab renders empty (layout() on QScrollArea is null) - #215 fixed signals sit in unreachable branches. Specifically, Ribbon 流程 (Workflow) tab renders empty — pageW->layout() on a QScrollArea is always null, so all five workflow buttons are never created and the closed #215 fix lives in unreachable dead code.

## Area
GUI / Application Shell / Dialogs

## Type
ui/interaction

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/shell/ribbon_controller.cpp:1024-1084 (key line 1026); makeTabPage 151-175; pageLayoutOf 177-187` (RibbonController::createRibbonBar / RibbonController::makeTabPage)

## User impact
- Whole feature surface of the workflow ribbon tab is dead; #215 is effectively unresolved at HEAD despite being closed; users can only run/stop workflows from the pipeline editor dock toolbar

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (SHELLB-1)**: Open the app, click the 流程 tab in the ribbon

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (SHELLB-1)**: Two groups (流程编辑 / 流程控制) with five large buttons as coded

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (SHELLB-1)**: Blank tab page; workflow run/stop controls missing from the ribbon

## Root cause
- **SHELLB-1**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `user clicks 流程 tab (stack index created by addTab at line 1083) -> QStackedWidget shows the empty QScrollArea page; no button exists, so PipelineEditorDock::runFullWorkflowRequested/stopWorkflowRequested can never be triggered from the ribbon (they remain reachable only from the dock's own toolbar, pipeline_editor_dock.cpp:64-68)`
  - *Code context*: `All other tabs do `QHBoxLayout *pl = pageLayoutOf( pageW );` which digs the layout out of the scroll area's inner page widget (`sa->widget()->layout()`). The 流程 tab instead does `auto *pLayout = qobject_cast<QHBoxLayout *>( pageW->layout() );` where pageW is the QScrollArea returned by makeTabPage() (makeTabPage only sets a layout on the inner `page` widget, never on `scroll` itself; it even stashes the page pointer in the "pageWidget" dynamic property because the scroll area's layout() is null). QWidget::layout() on a bare QScrollArea returns nullptr, so pLayout == nullptr; addGroup(pLayout,...) then early-returns a default GroupHost{widget=nullptr, toolsLayout=nullptr} and every `if ( auto *btn = addToolButton( editGrp, ...) )` block is skipped — 新建流程, 打开流程, 流程编辑器, 运行全流程, 停止运行 are never instantiated. Consequently the #215 fix (commit 8f57fbbd79, emit dock->runFullWorkflowRequested()/stopWorkflowRequested()) edited lambdas inside these unreachable `if` blocks and did not actually restore the controls.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: All 11 sibling tabs obtain the layout through pageLayoutOf(pageW) which handles QScrollArea by drilling to sa->widget()->layout(); the 流程 tab alone does qobject_cast<QHBoxLayout*>(pageW->layout()) on the QScrollArea (line 1026) -> nullptr. addGroup(null) returns GroupHost{widget=nullptr, toolsLayout=nullptr}; addToolButton returns nullptr when toolsLayout is null (line 235-237) so every 'if (auto *btn=...)' block is skipped — all five buttons are never created and addTab(流程) adds an empty page. #215's fix commit 8f57fbbd79 modified the runFullWorkflowRequested/stopWorkflowRequested lambdas INSIDE those unreachable branches (git show confirms the hunk is contained in 'if (auto *btn = addToolButton(execGrp,...))'), so the fix is dead code — the Dock toolbar remains the only functioning surface. Ribbon is always built (main_window_docks.cpp:621-622); stack->setCurrentIndex(kMapTab=3) leaves 流程 at a later index but reachable by click.
- **Review note**: None (lines 151-187, 1024-1084 accurate; makeTabPage sets a layout only on the inner page widget, never on the QScrollArea, and stashes the page via the 'pageWidget' dynamic property precisely because the scroll area's layout() is null).
- **Finding SHELLB-1**: `All other tabs do `QHBoxLayout *pl = pageLayoutOf( pageW );` which digs the layout out of the scroll area's inner page widget (`sa->widget()->layout()`). The 流程 tab instead does `auto *pLayout = qobject_cast<QHBoxLayout *>( pageW->layout() );` where pageW is the QScrollArea returned by makeTabPage() (makeTabPage only sets a layout on the inner `page` widget, never on `scroll` itself; it even stashes the page pointer in the "pageWidget" dynamic property because the scroll area's layout() is null). QWidget::layout() on a bare QScrollArea returns nullptr, so pLayout == nullptr; addGroup(pLayout,...) then early-returns a default GroupHost{widget=nullptr, toolsLayout=nullptr} and every `if ( auto *btn = addToolButton( editGrp, ...) )` block is skipped — 新建流程, 打开流程, 流程编辑器, 运行全流程, 停止运行 are never instantiated. Consequently the #215 fix (commit 8f57fbbd79, emit dock->runFullWorkflowRequested()/stopWorkflowRequested()) edited lambdas inside these unreachable `if` blocks and did not actually restore the controls.`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure widgets are fully initialized or stubbed safely, signals/slots are correctly connected to backend results, and UI elements do not block the main event loop.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (SHELLB-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #215 (CLOSED) is the same feature (empty stop lambda / run only raises dock); its fix is verified unreachable, so C32 is an incomplete-fix reopen with new evidence. #236/#238 unrelated.
- Finding SHELLB-1: #215 claimed fixed in 8f57fbbd79; verified at HEAD d9c59e5b that the fixed lambdas sit inside addToolButton()==nullptr branches and are unreachable. Not tracked by #236/#238.

## Summary
QgsLayoutDesignerDialog WA_DeleteOnClose + destructor deleteLater on dangling mWindow - heap UAF at exit. Specifically, QgsLayoutDesignerDialog destructor calls mWindow->deleteLater() on a dangling raw pointer — use-after-free after the layout window is closed (WA_DeleteOnClose) and the app exits.

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/layout/qgslayoutdesignerdialog.cpp:64-73, 100; src/app/main_window_project.cpp:67-70` (QgsLayoutDesignerDialog::~QgsLayoutDesignerDialog / QgisDesktopWindow::newLayout)

## User impact
- Crash on application exit for any session that opened and closed a layout designer; on ASan builds it aborts the process

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (SHELLA-5)**: Open New Layout once, close the layout designer window, then quit the application (or anything else that destroys the main window, e.g. tests)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (SHELLA-5)**: mWindow tracked via QPointer (or destroyed via deleteLater before the attribute applies); destructor is a no-op after the window was already closed

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (SHELLA-5)**: Deterministic use-after-free on exit: the null-check guard passes on the dangling pointer and deleteLater() is invoked on a destroyed QObject (crash/ASan heap-use-after-free at teardown)

## Root cause
- **SHELLA-5**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `工程->新建布局 -> newLayout creates designer (child of main window) + WA_DeleteOnClose mWindow -> user closes layout window -> mWindow destroyed (pointer dangles) -> app quit -> ~QgisDesktopWindow destroys child designer -> ~QgsLayoutDesignerDialog -> mWindow->deleteLater() on freed object`
  - *Code context*: `main_window_project.cpp:67-68 sets `designer->window()->setAttribute( Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose );` where window() returns the parentless `mWindow` (qgslayoutdesignerdialog.h:44 `QWidget *window() override { return mWindow; }`, member declared as raw `QMainWindow *mWindow = nullptr;` at .h:100). When the user closes the layout window, WA_DeleteOnClose destroys mWindow via deleteLater, but the raw member is NOT nulled. The destructor then runs at app teardown (designer is a QObject child of the main window): qgslayoutdesignerdialog.cpp:69-71 `if (mWindow) { mWindow->deleteLater(); ... }` — the comment says 'guard with a null check', but a deleted QWidget leaves the pointer non-null, so the branch executes `deleteLater()` on freed memory (heap-use-after-free in QObject::deleteLater -> d-ptr read). close() at :141-143 has the same dangling pattern.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: main_window_project.cpp:67-68: designer->window()->setAttribute(Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose) then show(); window() returns parentless mWindow (new QMainWindow(nullptr,Qt::Window) in ctor). Wa_DeleteOnClose makes close() schedule deleteLater on mWindow; the raw member is never nulled on close, so when ~QgisLayoutDesignerDialog runs (designer is a QObject child of the main window, so it is destroyed at main-window teardown) the 'if (mWindow) mWindow->deleteLater()' branch executes on a freed QObject -> UAF (deleteLater reads the d-ptr). The code comment even acknowledges the WA_DeleteOnClose hazard but the described 'null-check guard' cannot work because the pointer is not nulled on deletion. close() at :140-143 shares the dangling pattern. Reachability: Project menu '新建布局' -> newLayout (main_window_menus.cpp:148-149).
- **Review note**: None (verified qgslayoutdesignerdialog.cpp:64-73,100 + header raw member line 100 + main_window_project.cpp:67-70).
- **Finding SHELLA-5**: `main_window_project.cpp:67-68 sets `designer->window()->setAttribute( Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose );` where window() returns the parentless `mWindow` (qgslayoutdesignerdialog.h:44 `QWidget *window() override { return mWindow; }`, member declared as raw `QMainWindow *mWindow = nullptr;` at .h:100). When the user closes the layout window, WA_DeleteOnClose destroys mWindow via deleteLater, but the raw member is NOT nulled. The destructor then runs at app teardown (designer is a QObject child of the main window): qgslayoutdesignerdialog.cpp:69-71 `if (mWindow) { mWindow->deleteLater(); ... }` — the comment says 'guard with a null check', but a deleted QWidget leaves the pointer non-null, so the branch executes `deleteLater()` on freed memory (heap-use-after-free in QObject::deleteLater -> d-ptr read). close() at :141-143 has the same dangling pattern.`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure proper synchronization, atomic state transitions, clean thread termination, and avoidance of use-after-free or race conditions on worker/GUI threads.

## Summary
MeasureTool caches QgsDistanceArea CRS/ellipsoid at construction - measurements wrong after project CRS change. Specifically, MeasureTool caches QgsDistanceArea source CRS/ellipsoid once at startup — every later measurement is computed in the wrong CRS after a project CRS change or project open.

## Area
Data Model / Raster Grids / NoData & CRS

## Type
data/crs-nodata-metadata

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/map_tools/measure_tool.cpp:15-34, 128-142` (MeasureTool::MeasureTool / MeasureTool::finishMeasurement)

## User impact
- Silently wrong measurement numbers for every measurement taken after any CRS change/project load — quantitative results a remote-sensing user relies on are garbage with no error signal

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (SHELLA-4)**: Start the app (project CRS = startup default), then open a saved .qgs whose CRS is different or change 工程 CRS via the status-bar selector, then measure any distance/area

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (SHELLA-4)**: Distance/area computed with sourceCrs = current canvas destinationCrs (QGIS's measure tool reconfigures QgsDistanceArea on crs changes), giving geodesic values for the visible map

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (SHELLA-4)**: The stale startup CRS is used; e.g. UTM (metre) coordinates interpreted as the startup 4326 CRS produce wildly wrong ellipsoidal lengths; unit label (mDistanceArea.lengthUnits()) also reflects the stale CRS

## Root cause
- **SHELLA-4**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `视图->测距/测面 -> MeasureTool (constructed at app start) -> clicks append map-CRS points -> finishMeasurement -> QgsDistanceArea::measureLine (sourceCrs = stale startup CRS)`
  - *Code context*: `measure_tool.cpp:31-33 (constructor): `QgsProject *project = QgsProject::instance(); mDistanceArea.setSourceCrs( project->crs(), project->transformContext() ); mDistanceArea.setEllipsoid( project->ellipsoid() );` — the tools are constructed exactly once in MapToolManager::setupTools() during app startup (map_tool_manager.cpp:109-110) and nothing ever reconfigures mDistanceArea (no connection to QgsProject::crsChanged anywhere in the file; QgsProject::read() and QgisDesktopWindow::onCrsChanged both change project CRS without touching the tool). finishMeasurement then calls `mDistanceArea.measureLine( mPoints )` / `measurePolygon( mPoints )` where mPoints are map (canvas destination CRS) coordinates. If destinationCrs differs from the CRS captured at startup, coordinates are interpreted in the wrong CRS.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: MeasureTool ctor sets mDistanceArea.setSourceCrs(project->crs()) and setEllipsoid once. mPoints are canvas/click coordinates in the canvas destination CRS; QgsDistanceArea::measureLine/measurePolygon interpret them in the cached source CRS. Nothing reconfigures the tool on project CRS change: no crsChanged connection in measure_tool.cpp/map_tool_manager.cpp (grep only the two ctor sets); the CRS-change paths (onCrsChanged main_window_connections.cpp:357-361 sets project CRS + canvas destinationCrs + refresh; setProjectCrs main_window_processing.cpp:533-534) never touch MeasureTool. After a CRS change or project open with a different CRS, every subsequent measurement uses the stale startup CRS. QGIS reference behavior (qgsmeasuretool re-wires QgsDistanceArea on crs changes) is absent here.
- **Review note**: None (lines 15-34, 128-142 accurate; the two tools are constructed once each in MapToolManager::setupTools(), main_window.cpp:337).
- **Finding SHELLA-4**: `measure_tool.cpp:31-33 (constructor): `QgsProject *project = QgsProject::instance(); mDistanceArea.setSourceCrs( project->crs(), project->transformContext() ); mDistanceArea.setEllipsoid( project->ellipsoid() );` — the tools are constructed exactly once in MapToolManager::setupTools() during app startup (map_tool_manager.cpp:109-110) and nothing ever reconfigures mDistanceArea (no connection to QgsProject::crsChanged anywhere in the file; QgsProject::read() and QgisDesktopWindow::onCrsChanged both change project CRS without touching the tool). finishMeasurement then calls `mDistanceArea.measureLine( mPoints )` / `measurePolygon( mPoints )` where mPoints are map (canvas destination CRS) coordinates. If destinationCrs differs from the CRS captured at startup, coordinates are interpreted in the wrong CRS.`

## Suggested fix
- Validate grid compatibility rigorously, propagate NoData masks across all processing steps, and preserve CRS/metadata on output datasets.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (SHELLA-4).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- No closed issue mentions MeasureTool or QgsDistanceArea (#214 was the ROI spectrum GDAL scan — different file/symptom). Not covered.
- Finding SHELLA-4: No closed issue mentions MeasureTool or QgsDistanceArea (#214 was ROI spectrum GDAL scans, different file/symptom). Verified mDistanceArea is never re-set at HEAD

## Summary
CRS preset table maps CGCS2000/Xian1980 labels to wrong EPSG codes (39-deg zone shift; Xian off-by-one). Specifically, CRS preset table maps labels to wrong EPSG codes — all 9 CGCS2000 entries point at CM 114-138E zones and the Xian 1980 series is off by one (zone 13 selects Hong Kong 1980).

## Area
Data Model / Raster Grids / NoData & CRS

## Type
data/crs-nodata-metadata

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/crs_presets.cpp:22-30, 46-56` ((anonymous) presets())

## User impact
- Silent gross georeferencing corruption: a layer assigned a 'matching' preset CRS gets misplaced by tens of degrees / wrong datum; project CRS mispairs with UTM data, cascading into the SHELLA-1-style extent errors and reprojection failures. China-region workflows are the app's primary audience and these are 22 of 37 presets

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (SHELLA-3)**: Pick any 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree GK Zone 25..33' or 'Xian 1980 / GK Zone 13..23' preset to set the project or layer CRS

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (SHELLA-3)**: Zone 25 -> EPSG:4513 (CM 75E), Xian Zone 13 -> EPSG:2327; the applied CRS matches the label

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (SHELLA-3)**: Zone 25 -> EPSG:4547 = CM 114E (39 degrees off); Xian Zone 13 -> EPSG:2326 = Hong Kong 1980 Grid System (different datum); the rest of both series are one zone off

## Root cause
- **SHELLA-3**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `设置->CRS 预设 / 图层->设置工程 CRS -> CrsPresetDialog -> selectedEpsg -> QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem::fromEpsgId(4547) -> QgsProject::setCrs / layer->setCrs`
  - *Code context*: `crs_presets.cpp:22-30 declares `{ "CGCS2000 / 3-degree GK Zone 25", 4547 }` .. `{ ".. Zone 33", 4555 }`, and :46-56 `{ "Xian 1980 / GK Zone 13", 2326 }` .. `{ ".. Zone 23", 2336 }`. Verified against the local PROJ database: EPSG:4547 = 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree Gauss-Kruger CM 114E' (zone 25's central meridian is 75E — the correct zone-number series is 4513-4521; e.g. projinfo EPSG:4513 = 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree Gauss-Kruger zone 25'); EPSG:2326 = 'Hong Kong 1980 Grid System' (a different datum/ellipsoid), while Xian 1980 GK zone 13 is EPSG:2327 (2336 = zone 22, 2337 = zone 23). So 'Zone 13' applies Hong Kong 1980 and every other Xian entry is shifted one zone; every CGCS2000 preset is shifted ~39 degrees of longitude. Consumers: QgisDesktopWindow::setProjectCrs / setLayerCrsFromPreset (main_window_layers.cpp:259-278, main_window_processing.cpp:547-574) call QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem::fromEpsgId with these codes.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: crs_presets.cpp:22-30 maps 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree GK Zone 25..33' -> 4547..4555. projinfo EPSG:4547 = 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree Gauss-Kruger CM 114E' (lon_0=114); the zone-series labels correspond to EPSG:4513-4521 ('CGCS2000 / 3-degree Gauss-Kruger zone 25..33', lon_0=75 for zone 25) — a 39-degree CM shift for all 9 entries. crs_presets.cpp:46-56 maps 'Xian 1980 / GK Zone 13..23' -> 2326..2336; projinfo EPSG:2326 = 'Hong Kong 1980 Grid System' (ellps=intl, lat_0=22.3121, lon_0=114.1785), EPSG:2327 = 'Xian 1980 / Gauss-Kruger zone 13' (lon_0=75), EPSG:2336 = zone 22, EPSG:2337 = zone 23 — the series is off by one (Zone 13 = HK 1980), 2336 belongs to Zone 22 not 23. Beijing 1954 series 21413-21423 checked and is CORRECT (21413=zone 13 CM 75E, 21423=zone 23 CM 135E, ellps=krass), consistent with the finding flagging only the CGCS2000 and Xian series. Consumers verified: Crspreset selection -> QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem::fromEpsgId (main_window_layers.cpp:267; dialog path crs_preset_dialog.cpp).
- **Review note**: None. projinfo (system PROJ, /usr/sbin/projinfo) directly verified every claimed mapping.
- **Finding SHELLA-3**: `crs_presets.cpp:22-30 declares `{ "CGCS2000 / 3-degree GK Zone 25", 4547 }` .. `{ ".. Zone 33", 4555 }`, and :46-56 `{ "Xian 1980 / GK Zone 13", 2326 }` .. `{ ".. Zone 23", 2336 }`. Verified against the local PROJ database: EPSG:4547 = 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree Gauss-Kruger CM 114E' (zone 25's central meridian is 75E — the correct zone-number series is 4513-4521; e.g. projinfo EPSG:4513 = 'CGCS2000 / 3-degree Gauss-Kruger zone 25'); EPSG:2326 = 'Hong Kong 1980 Grid System' (a different datum/ellipsoid), while Xian 1980 GK zone 13 is EPSG:2327 (2336 = zone 22, 2337 = zone 23). So 'Zone 13' applies Hong Kong 1980 and every other Xian entry is shifted one zone; every CGCS2000 preset is shifted ~39 degrees of longitude. Consumers: QgisDesktopWindow::setProjectCrs / setLayerCrsFromPreset (main_window_layers.cpp:259-278, main_window_processing.cpp:547-574) call QgsCoordinateReferenceSystem::fromEpsgId with these codes.`

- Validate grid compatibility rigorously, propagate NoData masks across all processing steps, and preserve CRS/metadata on output datasets.

- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.

## Summary
Zoom-to-layer/first-layer framing feeds layer extents to the canvas without CRS reprojection. Specifically, Layer extents are fed to QgsMapCanvas::setExtent without CRS reprojection — zoom-to-layer and first-layer framing put the view in the wrong place whenever layer CRS != project CRS.

## Area
GUI / Application Shell / Dialogs

## Type
ui/interaction

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/active_view_host.cpp:261-263, 320-322, 477-488; src/app/main_window_view.cpp:434-442` (ActiveViewHost::displayAsset / ActiveViewHost::openSource / ActiveViewHost::zoomToLayer / QgisDesktopWindow::zoomToLayer)

## User impact
- Blank or misplaced map view after loading CRS-mismatched data — the most common remote-sensing workflow (mixed CRS scenes). User must manually zoom-to-full-extent to recover; first-run experience appears broken

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (SHELLA-1)**: Load a raster whose CRS differs from the project CRS (e.g. UTM GeoTIFF into the default 4326/3857 project, or open a saved project with another CRS and add a new layer), then use Zoom to Layer, Zoom to Native Resolution, or add the first layer to an empty view

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (SHELLA-1)**: Extent is transformed layer-CRS -> canvas destinationCrs (QgsCoordinateTransform with project transform context, as QGIS does) before setExtent

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (SHELLA-1)**: Raw layer-CRS numbers are used as destination-CRS coordinates; e.g. a UTM layer's 300000..700000 m range is interpreted as degrees -> canvas frames a bogus extent tens of degrees away, rendering a blank/garbage view. First-layer framing (openSource/displayAsset) and the layer-menu/context-menu Zoom to Layer are all affected

## Root cause
- **SHELLA-1**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `layer-tree ctx menu Zoom to Layer -> LayerTreeMenuProvider -> ActiveViewHost::zoomToLayer -> QgsMapCanvas::setExtent(layer->extent()); or file open -> QgisDesktopWindow::addRasterLayer -> ActiveViewHost::openRasterPath -> openSource -> targetCanvas->setExtent(layer->extent()) when canvas empty; or View menu 缩放到图层 -> QgisDesktopWindow::zoomToLayer`
  - *Code context*: `active_view_host.cpp:262 `targetCanvas->setExtent( layer->extent() );` (displayAsset), :322 same in openSource, :486 `m_mapCanvas->setExtent( target->extent() );` (zoomToLayer); main_window_view.cpp:438 `m_mapCanvas->setExtent(selected.first()->extent());`. QgsMapLayer::extent() is in the LAYER CRS; QgsMapCanvas::setExtent expects destination(project)-CRS coordinates (QGIS's own QgisApp::zoomToLayerExtent wraps it in QgsCoordinateTransform). No QgsCoordinateTransform exists anywhere in these two files (grep QgsCoordinateTransform src/app/active_view_host.cpp main_window_view.cpp = 0 hits). zoomToNativeResolution (active_view_host.cpp:490-515) additionally multiplies rasterUnitsPerPixel (layer-CRS units) by canvas pixel size and setExtent()s the result — same CRS class error.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: QgsMapLayer::extent() is in layer CRS; QgsMapCanvas::setExtent -> QgsMapSettings::setExtent stores the rectangle in destination/output CRS. Reference QGIS confirms the transform step: refs/qgis/src/gui/layertree/qgslayertreeviewdefaultactions.cpp:438 'layerExtent = canvas->mapSettings().layerExtentToOutputExtent( layer, layerExtent );' before combining and zooming. No QgsCoordinateTransform / layerExtentToOutputExtent in active_view_host.cpp or main_window_view.cpp (grep = 0). Destination CRS tracks the project CRS (main_window_processing.cpp:533-534, main_window_connections.cpp:357-361 onCrsChanged), so any layer whose CRS != project CRS gets its raw extent interpreted as destination coordinates (UTM metres read as degrees -> bogus framing). No lower-layer guard exists (display manager adds layers with their own CRS).
- **Review note**: None (all four cited sites verified: active_view_host.cpp:262, 322, 486, main_window_view.cpp:438; zoomToNativeResolution 490-515 also reuses layer-CRS extents).
- **Finding SHELLA-1**: `active_view_host.cpp:262 `targetCanvas->setExtent( layer->extent() );` (displayAsset), :322 same in openSource, :486 `m_mapCanvas->setExtent( target->extent() );` (zoomToLayer); main_window_view.cpp:438 `m_mapCanvas->setExtent(selected.first()->extent());`. QgsMapLayer::extent() is in the LAYER CRS; QgsMapCanvas::setExtent expects destination(project)-CRS coordinates (QGIS's own QgisApp::zoomToLayerExtent wraps it in QgsCoordinateTransform). No QgsCoordinateTransform exists anywhere in these two files (grep QgsCoordinateTransform src/app/active_view_host.cpp main_window_view.cpp = 0 hits). zoomToNativeResolution (active_view_host.cpp:490-515) additionally multiplies rasterUnitsPerPixel (layer-CRS units) by canvas pixel size and setExtent()s the result — same CRS class error.`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure widgets are fully initialized or stubbed safely, signals/slots are correctly connected to backend results, and UI elements do not block the main event loop.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (SHELLA-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #236 (CLOSED) covered which canvas receives first-layer setExtent (87575ea7ec targeted targetCanvas rerouting without adding a transform); the CRS-transform gap in these files is new. #195/#194 cover operator-layer CRS issues, not canvas extent framing.
- Finding SHELLA-1: #236 fixed only WHICH canvas receives setExtent (secondary-view first-layer framing) — commit 87575ea7ec diff shows targetCanvas rerouting with no transform added. Not #195/#194 (operator-layer CRS issues). No open/closed issue covers canvas extent CRS transform in these files
title: [P2][ui/interaction] Zoom-to-layer/first-layer framing feeds layer extents to the canvas without CRS reprojection

## Summary
Python IPC lifecycle: sendRequestSync timeout leaves UAF-capturing callback registered; worker-crash reset crosses two plugins onto one IPC stream. This issue aggregates 2 related finding(s): DATAPY-2, DATAPY-3. Specifically, PythonIpcServer::sendRequestSync worker-thread path: after wait-timeout the still-queued lambda writes through dangling stack references (UAF). Specifically, Worker crash resets WorkerNode::isBusy without notifying the owning adapter — one pool node can end up serving two plugins with crossed IPC dispatch.

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/python/isolated/python_ipc_server.cpp:294-326` (PythonIpcServer::sendRequestSync)
- `src/python/isolated/python_worker_process_pool.cpp:223-268` (PythonWorkerProcessPool::handleWorkerCrash / PythonPluginAdapter::initialize)

## User impact
- Deterministic crash/UB on the main thread in the delayed-main-thread scenario; the same shape of defect was fixed for sendRequestAndAwait (#233) but this remaining path was not.
- Crossed IPC streams after a crash-restart: duplicate plugin menu entries, responses attributed to the wrong plugin, and premature node release allowing a third consumer. This is the residual ownership defect left after #233's bridge-dangling fix (QPointer re-bind, python_plugin_adapter.cpp:118-123).

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (DATAPY-2)**: Worker-thread sendRequestSync whose home thread does not service the event loop within timeoutMs+1000 ms (timeout is 300 s for py: execution).
- **Trigger (DATAPY-3)**: Worker crash while a Python plugin is loaded, followed by loading another Python plugin (pool default size 2 makes node reuse likely).

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (DATAPY-2)**: Timeout returns cleanly and the deferred invocation is invalidated (shared context + erased callback), mirroring the sendRequestAndAwait fix at lines 240-264.
- **Expected (DATAPY-3)**: The crashed node's owner either loses the node (adapter marked dead / plugin reloaded) or the node stays reserved; exactly one bridge per IPC server.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (DATAPY-2)**: The queued lambda survives with dangling references; late execution is use-after-free on QWaitCondition/QMutex/QJsonObject and the caller's stack (crash or silent memory corruption).
- **Actual (DATAPY-3)**: Two AppInterfaceBridges receive the same PythonIpcServer::messageReceived: daemon requests like ui.add_plugin_menu are dispatched twice (duplicate QActions, racing responses), and either adapter's releaseWorker(m_workerNode) clears isBusy while the other still uses the node — the busy-flag protocol is broken.

## Root cause
- **DATAPY-2**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `py: algorithm on a JobEngine worker (src/processing/framework/python_algorithm_adapter execute → AppInterfaceBridge handler, src/python/isolated/app_interface_bridge.cpp:353-354 `ipc->sendRequestSync("processing.execute_algorithm", req, execResult, execIsError, 300000)`) → sendRequestSync worker branch → main thread blocked >301 s (long synchronous GUI/GDAL work; this app has documented classes of multi-minute main-thread stalls, e.g. #184/#218) → worker times out and unwinds → queued lambda eventually executes on the main thread → UAF.`
  - *Code context*: `The worker-thread branch queues a lambda capturing `&result, &isError, ... &status, &done, &mutex, &waitCond` BY REFERENCE (lines 301-313) onto the server's home thread, then blocks: `if ( !waitCond.wait( &mutex, timeoutMs + 1000 ) ) { return AwaitStatus::Timeout; }` (319-322). On timeout the worker returns immediately and destroys those stack objects; nothing cancels or fences the queued lambda. When the main thread later runs it, it executes `status = weakServer->sendRequestAndAwait(...); result/isError writes; waitCond.wakeAll();` on destroyed objects.`
- **DATAPY-3**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `Plugin A loaded on node N (acquireWorker → isBusy=true) → daemon segfaults (there is even a `crash_test` RPC, worker_daemon.py:492-495) → handleWorkerCrash(N) → isBusy=false, new server+worker → workerRestarted re-binds A's bridge to the new server → user loads Plugin B → acquireWorker returns the SAME node N → B's bridge also binds to N's server (bindIpcServer connects messageReceived) → both bridges dispatch every daemon→C++ request.`
  - *Code context*: `handleWorkerCrash rebuilds the node and unconditionally does `node->isBusy = false;` (line 261) while the PythonPluginAdapter that owns the node still holds m_workerNode (src/python/isolated/python_plugin_adapter.h:82) and re-binds its bridge on restart (python_plugin_adapter.cpp:118-123). acquireWorker hands the node out again purely on `!node->isBusy && ... node->server->hasClient()` (pool lines 72-78). Nothing re-marks the node busy for the first adapter, and no adapter-side invalidation exists (the adapter listens only to workerRestarted, never to workerCrashed).`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: DATAPY-2: sendRequestSync (python_ipc_server.cpp:294-326) worker branch queues a lambda capturing &result,&isError,&status,&done,&mutex,&waitCond BY REFERENCE onto the home thread, then waitCond.wait(timeoutMs+1000). On timeout the function returns and the frame dies; nothing erases/invalidates the queued lambda (compare the sendRequestAndAwait fix at 240-268 that uses shared AwaitContext and m_callbacks.erase). Worker path is real: python_plugin_host.cpp:21-43 runs py: jobs on JobEngine worker threads and app_interface_bridge.cpp:353-354 calls ipc->sendRequestSync("processing.execute_algorithm",...,300000). #233 (8093059751) fixed only sendRequestAndAwait's stack-capturing callback; #210 (5116f95a66) rewrote sendRequestSync to the current deferral but did not solve late-run of the captured lambda. DATAPY-3: handleWorkerCrash (python_worker_process_pool.cpp:223-268) unconditionally sets node->isBusy=false after replacing server+worker (line ~261); the owning PythonPluginAdapter listens only to workerRestarted (re-bind, python_plugin_adapter.cpp:119-123), never workerCrashed; acquireWorker (72-78) hands the node out on !isBusy && hasClient, so a second plugin can bind a second AppInterfaceBridge to the same PythonIpcServer -> both receive every daemon message.
- **Review note**: None; note both are edge-window defects (DATAPY-2 needs the main thread blocked >300 s while a py: RPC waits; DATAPY-3 needs a worker crash while a plugin is loaded and then a second plugin load on the same pool node). Keep P2 as latent UAF/crossed-IPC-stream.
- **Finding DATAPY-2**: `The worker-thread branch queues a lambda capturing `&result, &isError, ... &status, &done, &mutex, &waitCond` BY REFERENCE (lines 301-313) onto the server's home thread, then blocks: `if ( !waitCond.wait( &mutex, timeoutMs + 1000 ) ) { return AwaitStatus::Timeout; }` (319-322). On timeout the worker returns immediately and destroys those stack objects; nothing cancels or fences the queued lambda. When the main thread later runs it, it executes `status = weakServer->sendRequestAndAwait(...); result/isError writes; waitCond.wakeAll();` on destroyed objects.`
- **Finding DATAPY-3**: `handleWorkerCrash rebuilds the node and unconditionally does `node->isBusy = false;` (line 261) while the PythonPluginAdapter that owns the node still holds m_workerNode (src/python/isolated/python_plugin_adapter.h:82) and re-binds its bridge on restart (python_plugin_adapter.cpp:118-123). acquireWorker hands the node out again purely on `!node->isBusy && ... node->server->hasClient()` (pool lines 72-78). Nothing re-marks the node busy for the first adapter, and no adapter-side invalidation exists (the adapter listens only to workerRestarted, never to workerCrashed).`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure proper synchronization, atomic state transitions, clean thread termination, and avoidance of use-after-free or race conditions on worker/GUI threads.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (DATAPY-2, DATAPY-3).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #210 (CLOSED) was the worker-thread socket/UAF and is addressed by the current deferral design; #233 (CLOSED) fixed sendRequestAndAwait callback lifetime and adapter-dangling after unloadAll — distinct from the residual sendRequestSync queue-lifetime and the crash busy-flag reset. Not covered elsewhere (grep isBusy/crash in issues-closed = JobEngine/TaskCenter only).
- Finding DATAPY-2: #210 (fixed) covered sendRequestSync driving the socket from workers; #233 (fixed) covered sendRequestAndAwait's stack-capturing callback timeout. This is the distinct worker-branch queue-lifetime defect — verified still present at HEAD d9c59e5b.

## Summary
DataManager relocate/commitEdit/promote rebuild snapshots without parentCollectionId - collection membership silently dropped, double-adoption. Specifically, relocate()/commitEdit()/promote() rebuild AssetSnapshot and silently drop parentCollectionId — collection membership lost, double-parenting possible.

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/data/data_manager.cpp:421-434, 662-673, 1359-1371` (DataManager::relocate / DataManager::commitEdit / DataManager::promote)

## User impact
- Broken catalog invariant, duplicated rows in the Data Manager panel, corrupted collection membership after an import dedups onto the affected source, and project-reload diagnostics/errors. Persistence itself survives (serializer writes collection->childAssetIds), so the corruption is silent until an adopt/reload path hits it.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (DATAPY-1)**: Any collection child that is relocated (missing-source relink), promoted from temporary, or whose vector edit is committed.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (DATAPY-1)**: The one-parent invariant documented at data_manager.cpp:1635-1645 ('A child has at most one parent collection') is preserved across snapshot rebuilds.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (DATAPY-1)**: Snapshot reports a standalone asset while the collection still lists it. DataManagerPanel then renders the asset twice (under the collection via collection->childAssetIds, data_manager_panel.cpp:695, and as a top-level row because parentCollectionId() is nullopt, data_manager_panel.cpp:705-710). Worse, CollectionImportService::commit (src/processing/framework/collection_import_service.cpp:281-296) keys its dedup decision on snapshot->parentCollectionId(): the orphaned-looking child is 'adopted' into a second collection, so childAssetIds now contains it in two collections; on save/reload the serializer's second addChildToCollection fails with collection.child_already_owned and the project read reports failure.

## Root cause
- **DATAPY-1**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `UI 重定位缺失源 (src/app/main_window_docks.cpp:487 dataManager.relocate(RelocateRequest{assetId, replacement})) → DataManager::relocate → snapshot rebuild → parentCollectionId==nullopt while CollectionRecord.childAssetIds still lists the asset (pruneChildFromCollections only runs on unload/reap). Promote path: main_window_docks.cpp:455 → DataManager::promote.`
  - *Code context*: `AssetSnapshot's constructor (src/data/data_asset.h:323-346) has no parentCollectionId parameter; the member (data_asset.h:358) is set only by addChildToCollection via direct member write (data_manager.cpp:1648 `assetIt->snapshot.m_parentCollectionId = collectionId;`). relocate() constructs `AssetSnapshot updated{ current.id(), newRevision, normalizedDescriptor, ..., current.acquisitionTime() };` then `recordIt->snapshot = std::move( updated );` (421-434) — m_parentCollectionId resets to nullopt. commitEdit (662-673) and promote (1359-1371) use the same rebuild pattern and drop it identically. unloadCollection's non-cascade path (1737-1742) clears the member explicitly, proving the member is only reachable by direct access.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: AssetSnapshot ctor (data_asset.h:323-346) has no parentCollectionId parameter; member is set only by addChildToCollection via friend direct write (data_manager.cpp:1648) and cleared by unloadCollection non-cascade (1741). All three rebuilds construct a fresh snapshot without the member, so m_parentCollectionId resets to nullopt while CollectionRecord.childAssetIds still lists the asset. Reachability verified: DataManagerPanel promoteRequested/relocateRequested -> main_window_docks.cpp:455/487, commitEdit via commitEditLease -> main_window_vector.cpp:435-445. Consequences verified in code: data_manager_panel.cpp:695 renders collection children by childAssetIds AND :707 skips top-level rows only when parentCollectionId has_value -> relocated child renders twice; collection_import_service.cpp:274-296 keys dedup/adoption on snapshot->parentCollectionId() so the orphaned-looking child gets adopted into a second collection (double-adoption).
- **Review note**: Line refs: snapshot rebuilds verified at data_manager.cpp:421-434 (relocate), 662-673 (commitEdit), 1351-1371 (promote); the cited 1359-1371 range is accurate.
- **Finding DATAPY-1**: `AssetSnapshot's constructor (src/data/data_asset.h:323-346) has no parentCollectionId parameter; the member (data_asset.h:358) is set only by addChildToCollection via direct member write (data_manager.cpp:1648 `assetIt->snapshot.m_parentCollectionId = collectionId;`). relocate() constructs `AssetSnapshot updated{ current.id(), newRevision, normalizedDescriptor, ..., current.acquisitionTime() };` then `recordIt->snapshot = std::move( updated );` (421-434) — m_parentCollectionId resets to nullopt. commitEdit (662-673) and promote (1359-1371) use the same rebuild pattern and drop it identically. unloadCollection's non-cascade path (1737-1742) clears the member explicitly, proving the member is only reachable by direct access.`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure proper synchronization, atomic state transitions, clean thread termination, and avoidance of use-after-free or race conditions on worker/GUI threads.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (DATAPY-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Summary
Workspace path policies bypassable: CLI validates before ${VAR} expansion; MCP accepts relative '..' paths. Specifically, Workspace path policies are bypassable: CLI validates params BEFORE ${VAR} env expansion; MCP allows relative '..' paths unchecked.

## Area
Security / Path Validation / Robustness

## Type
security/robustness

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/cli/rs_pipeline_runner.cpp:215 vs 339-344,635-644` (RsPipelineRunner::runFromJson/validatePipelineJson/expandEnvironmentPlaceholders + McpServer::absolutePathOutsideWorkspace (src/agent/mcp_server.cpp:105-148))

## User impact
- SICNU_MCP_WORKSPACE/SICNU_PIPELINE_WORKSPACE sandboxes do not actually confine reads/writes

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (AGMCP-5)**: Untrusted pipeline JSON with ${VAR} params, or an MCP agent passing relative parent-escaping paths

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (AGMCP-5)**: Containment enforced on the final resolved paths (post-expansion, CWD-resolved)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (AGMCP-5)**: Both documented workspace boundaries can be escaped deterministically

## Root cause
- **AGMCP-5**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `CLI: pipeline JSON -> validatePipelineJson(raw) OK -> cliJsonToWorkflowDefinition -> expandEnvironmentPlaceholders -> absolute path outside workspace dispatched. MCP: tools/call execute_algorithm {parameters:{input:"../../x"}} -> validateWorkspacePaths -> relative -> allowed`
  - *Code context*: `CLI: runFromJson calls validatePipelineJson (which runs jsonValueOutsideWorkspace on raw params, lines 635-644) BEFORE cliJsonToWorkflowDefinition expands ${VAR} into params (line 215) — a param "${SECRET_OUT}/x.tif" is the literal relative string during validation, then expands to an absolute path outside SICNU_PIPELINE_WORKSPACE. MCP: absolutePathOutsideWorkspace returns false for any non-absolute path (comment line 103: 'Relative paths are allowed without check') — input "../../etc/shadow" or "..\\.." passes validateWorkspacePaths and the operator resolves it against the process CWD, escaping SICNU_MCP_WORKSPACE whenever CWD is at/under the workspace root.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: CLI: runFromJson calls validatePipelineJson (raw JSON; jsonValueOutsideWorkspace at rs_pipeline_runner.cpp:635-644) BEFORE cliJsonToWorkflowDefinition which performs expandEnvironmentPlaceholders at :215 (regex $(VAR) -> getenv). SICNU_PIPELINE_WORKSPACE is read at :610-611; no post-expansion re-validation exists in TaskCenter/JobEngine (grep OutsideWorkspace in task_center.cpp/job_engine.cpp = 0). So '${SECRET_OUT}/x.tif' validates as a relative string then expands to an absolute path outside the workspace. MCP: absolutePathOutsideWorkspace (mcp_server.cpp:105-148) returns false for every non-absolute path (fi.isAbsolute() false -> return false), so '..\..\etc' passes; CWD resolution under the workspace root escapes SICNU_MCP_WORKSPACE. Both mechanisms verified at HEAD.
- **Review note**: None; note MCP half is semi-documented policy (source comment 'Relative paths are allowed without check'), weakening that half to a design-weakness rather than silent bug, but the CLI validate-before-expand ordering is an unambiguous bypass of an intended containment check.
- **Finding AGMCP-5**: `CLI: runFromJson calls validatePipelineJson (which runs jsonValueOutsideWorkspace on raw params, lines 635-644) BEFORE cliJsonToWorkflowDefinition expands ${VAR} into params (line 215) — a param "${SECRET_OUT}/x.tif" is the literal relative string during validation, then expands to an absolute path outside SICNU_PIPELINE_WORKSPACE. MCP: absolutePathOutsideWorkspace returns false for any non-absolute path (comment line 103: 'Relative paths are allowed without check') — input "../../etc/shadow" or "..\\.." passes validateWorkspacePaths and the operator resolves it against the process CWD, escaping SICNU_MCP_WORKSPACE whenever CWD is at/under the workspace root.`

## Suggested fix
- Enforce path normalization and access control policies after macro/variable expansion to prevent unauthorized filesystem access.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (AGMCP-5).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- No closed issue on workspace path containment. #223 (CLOSED) is about the ${VAR} grammar being misread as step references (unresolved DAG) — different defect, same placeholder feature. #221/#222/#240 unrelated.
- Finding AGMCP-5: grep of issues-closed: no prior issue on workspace-path bypass; #221/#222/#240 unrelated
title: [P2][security/robustness] Workspace path policies bypassable: CLI validates before ${VAR} expansion; MCP accepts relative '..' paths

## Summary
Advertised tool surface not executable: GUI copilot data:* tools unregistered; CLI cannot run gdal:/otb:/qgis: provider algorithms. This issue aggregates 2 related finding(s): AGMCP-3, AGMCP-4. Specifically, GUI copilot advertises data:list_layers/describe_dataset/get_lineage to the LLM but they are unexecutable — InteractionToolRegistry never registers data: tools and the failure is silent. Specifically, CLI pipeline runner cannot execute provider algorithms (gdal:/otb:/qgis:/native:) — no AlgorithmEngine init, no JobEngine fallback/prefix executors registered.

## Area
Agent Interface / Model Context Protocol (MCP)

## Type
agent/mcp

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/agent/agent_copilot_dock_widget.cpp:296-299,363-396` (AgentCopilotDockWidget::sendPrompt/onToolCallParsed + InteractionToolRegistry::registerBuiltinTools (src/agent/interaction_tool_registry.cpp:375-525))
- `src/cli/main_cli.cpp:18-118` (main (cli) vs JobEngine resolution (src/jobs/job_engine.cpp:613-648))

## User impact
- Headline copilot capability (list layers / describe dataset / lineage) silently dead in GUI; #186's 'route data: tools' fix covered only the MCP surface
- Pipelines are not portable across surfaces; users hit 'Operator not registered' for the ~40 provider algorithms the MCP catalog advertises

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (AGMCP-3)**: User asks the copilot anything that makes the model call a data: tool (they are in every exported tool list)
- **Trigger (AGMCP-4)**: Run any pipeline JSON containing a provider algorithm id via sicnu_geo_rs_cli (works fine via MCP execute_algorithm and GUI)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (AGMCP-3)**: data: tools execute against DataManager/QgsProject as MCP's explicit routing does (mcp_server.cpp:547-557)
- **Expected (AGMCP-4)**: Same catalog executes on all surfaces (Invariant A: GUI == CLI == MCP)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (AGMCP-3)**: '⚡ 准备执行工具: data_list_layers' card appears, then nothing — no result, no error
- **Actual (AGMCP-4)**: CLI is restricted to rs:/opencv: RSOperators; provider ids unconditionally fail

## Root cause
- **AGMCP-3**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `LLM tool_calls data_list_layers -> onToolCallParsed -> ToolCallDispatcher::submit -> InteractionToolRegistry::execute -> error payload dropped by empty lambda`
  - *Code context*: `sendPrompt exports AgentToolCatalog::exportOpenAiToolDefinitions() which includes DataToolProvider's data:list_layers/data:describe_dataset/data:get_lineage (tool_catalog/data_tool_provider.cpp:8-145). The LLM's call 'data_list_layers' -> classify -> isInteractionAction -> submit -> mInteractionActionHandler -> InteractionToolRegistry::execute -> findTool misses (registerBuiltinTools only registers view:/roi:/canvas:/raster:) -> returns {status:error, errorMessage:'Interaction tool not registered: data_list_layers'}; the completion callback is [](const Json::Value&){} so the error is discarded (line 391).`
- **AGMCP-4**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `--pipeline with gdal:/otb:/qgis: step -> TaskCenter::submitPipeline -> JobEngine -> no executor, no RSOperator, no fallback -> Failed`
  - *Code context*: `main_cli.cpp never calls AlgorithmEngine::instance().initialize() (only src/app/main.cpp:141 does), never registers JobEngine prefix executors, and never calls JobEngine::setFallbackExecutor (only src/app/main.cpp:148-163 wires the AtomicAlgorithmRegistry fallback that resolves gdal:/otb:/qgis: ids). JobEngine resolve order is per-job -> prefix -> RSOperator -> fallback; with none registered a 'gdal:translate' step fails 'Unknown algorithm' which rs_pipeline_runner.cpp:453-454 renames to 'Operator not registered: gdal:translate'.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: AGMCP-3: AgentToolCatalog registers DataToolProvider (agent_tool_catalog.cpp:162); exportOpenAiToolDefinitions therefore advertises data:list_layers/describe_dataset/get_lineage. ToolCallDispatcher::isInteractionAction includes data:/data_ prefixes; dock wires mInteractionActionHandler->InteractionToolRegistry::execute; registerBuiltinTools (interaction_tool_registry.cpp:375+) registers only view:/canvas:/roi:/raster: names; execute() returns {status:error,'Interaction tool not registered: data_list_layers'} and the dock's completion callback is the empty lambda at agent_copilot_dock_widget.cpp:391 — silent. AGMCP-4: main_cli.cpp never calls AlgorithmEngine::instance().initialize() (only src/app/main.cpp:141) and never registers setFallbackExecutor (only main.cpp:148) nor prefix executors; JobEngine resolution order is per-job -> prefix -> RSOperator -> fallback (comment, job_engine.cpp:~613-648) and with no fallback an unrecognized id fails 'Unknown algorithm'; rs_pipeline_runner.cpp:453-454 renames it to 'Operator not registered'. Verified: setFallbackExecutor call sites grep to exactly main.cpp:148; AlgorithmEngine initialize grep to main.cpp:141.
- **Review note**: None.
- **Finding AGMCP-3**: `sendPrompt exports AgentToolCatalog::exportOpenAiToolDefinitions() which includes DataToolProvider's data:list_layers/data:describe_dataset/data:get_lineage (tool_catalog/data_tool_provider.cpp:8-145). The LLM's call 'data_list_layers' -> classify -> isInteractionAction -> submit -> mInteractionActionHandler -> InteractionToolRegistry::execute -> findTool misses (registerBuiltinTools only registers view:/roi:/canvas:/raster:) -> returns {status:error, errorMessage:'Interaction tool not registered: data_list_layers'}; the completion callback is [](const Json::Value&){} so the error is discarded (line 391).`
- **Finding AGMCP-4**: `main_cli.cpp never calls AlgorithmEngine::instance().initialize() (only src/app/main.cpp:141 does), never registers JobEngine prefix executors, and never calls JobEngine::setFallbackExecutor (only src/app/main.cpp:148-163 wires the AtomicAlgorithmRegistry fallback that resolves gdal:/otb:/qgis: ids). JobEngine resolve order is per-job -> prefix -> RSOperator -> fallback; with none registered a 'gdal:translate' step fails 'Unknown algorithm' which rs_pipeline_runner.cpp:453-454 renames to 'Operator not registered: gdal:translate'.`

## Suggested fix
- Comply with MCP protocol specifications, raise proper JSON-RPC errors, and handle lifecycle/path policies securely.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (AGMCP-3, AGMCP-4).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

- #186 (CLOSED) 'dead data:* tools' was fixed on the MCP tools/call routing surface (cac5da9469 commit message: 'route data: tools in MCP'); the GUI copilot dock dispatcher path remains broken — incomplete-fix/new-site. #105 (CLI pipelines via TaskCenter) does not cover AlgorithmEngine/fallback init on the CLI binary; #115 covers MCP/headless, not CLI. No live dupe.

## Summary
MCP stdio server never exits on stdin EOF and performs no TaskCenter/JobEngine shutdown (zombie process). Specifically, MCP headless server never exits on stdin EOF (zombie process) and MCP path performs no TaskCenter/JobEngine shutdown.

## Area
Agent Interface / Model Context Protocol (MCP)

## Type
agent/mcp

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/main.cpp:187-198` (main (mcpMode branch) + StdinReader::run (src/agent/mcp_server.cpp:361-372))

## User impact
- Orphaned processes per client session; dirty shutdown crash path (variant of #177/#178 for the MCP surface)

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (AGMCP-2)**: MCP client terminates the connection (normal disconnect, crash, or timeout)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (AGMCP-2)**: Server process exits on stdin EOF and shuts down TaskCenter/JobEngine cleanly

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (AGMCP-2)**: Process hangs indefinitely as a zombie; if killed, ~StdinReader's wait(3000) can time out mid-getline -> QThread destroyed-while-running qFatal, and running tasks' threads outlive QgsApplication

## Root cause
- **AGMCP-2**: CONFIRMED
  - *Callchain*: `client disconnect -> stdin EOF -> StdinReader::run exits -> (no quit wired) QCoreApplication::exec loops forever holding stdout open`
  - *Code context*: `McpServer server; server.start(app); int result = app->exec(); — no connect(mReader,&QThread::finished,...) anywhere (mcp_server.cpp:398 only connects lineRead), so when the client closes stdin StdinReader::run returns but app->exec() keeps running forever. GUI path (main.cpp:509-511) calls TaskCenter::shutdown()/JobEngine::shutdown(); the MCP branch has neither, so even a forced exit tears down QgsApplication (delete app) while provider-job worker threads still run.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: src/app/main.cpp mcpMode branch (lines ~187-198) is exactly 'McpServer server; server.start(app); int result = app->exec(); delete app; return result;'. StdinReader::run (mcp_server.cpp:361-372) exits when std::getline hits EOF, but the only connections in start() are to lineRead; no QThread::finished -> app->quit() anywhere (grep quit/finished in mcp_server.cpp = 0 hits). So stdin EOF leaves app->exec() running forever (zombie holding stdout). GUI path at main.cpp:509-511 calls TaskCenter::shutdown()/JobEngine::shutdown(); the MCP branch does neither although McpServer ctor registers ProcessingJobAdapter (prefix executor) and execute_algorithm dispatches through ToolCallDispatcher->TaskCenter->JobEngine (mcp_server.h:50,122), so provider/py jobs can be created on the MCP surface. ~McpServer wait(3000) is the destructor path only.
- **Review note**: None.
- **Finding AGMCP-2**: `McpServer server; server.start(app); int result = app->exec(); — no connect(mReader,&QThread::finished,...) anywhere (mcp_server.cpp:398 only connects lineRead), so when the client closes stdin StdinReader::run returns but app->exec() keeps running forever. GUI path (main.cpp:509-511) calls TaskCenter::shutdown()/JobEngine::shutdown(); the MCP branch has neither, so even a forced exit tears down QgsApplication (delete app) while provider-job worker threads still run.`

## Suggested fix
- Comply with MCP protocol specifications, raise proper JSON-RPC errors, and handle lifecycle/path policies securely.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (AGMCP-2).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

- #177/#178 are GUI-path teardown (QgsApplication torn down while JobEngine workers run; shutdown joins forever) — different surface. #221/#222 lifecycle handshake commit did not add EOF/quit wiring. No closed issue covers MCP stdio-server exit-on-EOF.

## Summary
#246 incomplete: production .points save/load never passes sourceGeoTransform - map coordinates still land in pixel columns. Specifically, #246 incompletely fixed: production save/load never pass sourceGeoTransform, so .points v2 still writes map coordinates (mapY negated) into pixelX/pixelY columns and QGIS v1 pixel-coord files are still misread as map coords.

## Area
Core Remote Sensing / Georeferencing / Classification

## Type
correctness

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/georeferencer/qgsgeoref_shell_window.cpp:2030,2054,2083` (QgsGeorefShellWindow::loadPoints / savePoints / closeEvent save path)

## User impact
- .points files written by this app cannot be consumed by QGIS's georeferencer and vice versa; cross-session loads with a georeferenced raster silently corrupt GCP source coordinates.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (GEOREF-4)**: Any .points save with a georeferenced source raster; any load of an externally-written .points file while a georeferenced source is open.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (GEOREF-4)**: Shell reads the source raster geotransform (it already builds QgsRasterChangeCoords in updateGcpTableRasterPaths) and passes it to both save and load so files carry true pixel coordinates and loads re-derive map coords, per the codec's design.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (GEOREF-4)**: The codec's conversion parameter is dead code in production; the exact defect #246 described ('map coordinates in pixel columns', 'loader has no raster-state check') persists in every production round-trip involving a georeferenced source. In-app save/load round-trips only by symmetric accident (both sides skip conversion), but the negated mapY in the pixelY column also breaks QGIS interop.

## Root cause
- **GEOREF-4**: CONFIRMED (production call sites qgsgeoref_shell_window.cpp:2030 (closeEvent save), :2054 (loadPoints), :2083 (savePoints) all omit sourceGeoTransform - grep across src/ shows ONLY tests pass gt (test_gcp_points_file.cpp:109,127); codec qgsgcplist.cpp:38-49 converts map->pixel on save and :111-116 pixel->map on load ONLY when gt!=nullptr, so with gt=nullptr: georeferenced-source GCPs write mapX into pixelX and -mapY into pixelY (:55-56), and QGIS-written pixel-coord files load as sourcePoint pixels -> fit's getPixelCoords misreads; in-app round-trip survives only by symmetric accident (both sides skip conversion); #246 fix f8f79f717f touched qgsgcplist.cpp/.h + tests + classification files, NOT the shell (git show --stat verified); the shell already has the geotransform at hand - QgsRasterChangeCoords loaded in updateGcpTableRasterPaths (:771-772) - so wiring was trivially available)
  - *Callchain*: `User loads georeferenced source raster (I2I typical) -> GCP sourcePoints are canvas picks in source-layer map coords -> savePoints/closeEvent-save -> rsSaveGcpPointsFile with gt=nullptr writes mapX into 'pixelX' column and -mapY into 'pixelY' column (line 53-56). Load of a QGIS-written v1/v2 file (true pixel coords) with gt=nullptr keeps pixels as sourcePoint -> fit's getPixelCoords interprets pixels as map coords -> garbage fit.`
