## Summary
SIFT/template-match auto-GCP insertion stores raw SRC pixel coordinates where the session contract requires map coordinates - matched GCPs are garbage. Specifically, SIFT and template-match results insert raw SRC pixel coordinates as QgsGcpPoint::sourcePoint; the session contract requires source-layer MAP coordinates when the raster is georeferenced (and opposite Y convention vs canvas picks when not).

## Area
Core Remote Sensing / Georeferencing / Classification

## Type
correctness

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/georeferencer/qgsgeoreferencermainwindow.cpp:304-312,455-463` (QgsGeoreferencerMainWindow::runSiftMatch acceptance lambda / runTemplateMatch acceptance lambda)

## User impact
- Both auto-match features (SIFT, template NCC) silently produce garbage georeferencing whenever they succeed, on the very data they are designed for (georeferenced source for template match). Worst-case the user accepts 25 'good' matches and warps to a garbage output with no error.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (GEOREF-3)**: I2I window. Template match ALWAYS (rs_template_matcher.cpp:151-160 requireSrcGeo=true rejects non-georeferenced SRC): grid col/row (e.g. (300,400)) stored as sourcePoint; fit computes toColumnLine((300,400)) = ((300-UL_X)/resX, ...) -> wildly wrong pixels -> garbage transform and warp output, silently (fit 'succeeds'). SIFT with georeferenced SRC: same. SIFT with unreferenced SRC: canvas-picked GCPs store (col,-line) (provider gt {0,1,0,0,-1,0}) while SIFT stores (col,+line) -> mixing manual and SIFT GCPs mirrors the y axis of half the points; SIFT-only sets place markers at positive y, outside the canvas extent y in [-H,0].

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (GEOREF-3)**: Match srcPx converted to the source layer's map coordinates via the source geotransform (toXY) before insertion, or the session to accept pixel coords with an explicit convention conversion; ExistingSeeds mode converting session map-coord GCPs to pixels when feeding the matcher (currently rs_template_matcher treats g.sourcePoint() directly as col/row at line 212-216, so existing-seed mode with a georeferenced source puts huge map values into 'sc = lround(sx)' and every seed falls out of bounds -> '未找到满足阈值的匹配点').

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (GEOREF-3)**: Auto-matched GCPs are stored in a different coordinate space than every other GCP source (canvas picks, .points load, table edits). Fit, residuals, markers, .points export all consume the wrong values; template-match ExistingSeeds mode finds zero matches with a misleading threshold message.

## Root cause
- **GEOREF-3**: CONFIRMED (SIFT acceptance qgsgeoreferencermainwindow.cpp:309 QgsGcpPoint(m.srcPx, m.dstWorld, destCrs, true) with srcPx documented 'Pixel coords in source raster' (rs_sift_matcher.h:40) from rs_sift_matcher.cpp:168 (keypoint/srcScale) - raw pixel col/row; template acceptance :460 identical with rs_template_matcher.cpp:267 m.srcPx=QgsPointXY(sx,sy) grid col/row; session contract requires source-layer MAP coords when georeferenced (qgsgcppoint.h:46 + facade updateParametersFromGcps:184-187 routes through getPixelCoords when hasExistingGeoreference); appendGcps (rs_georeferencing_session.cpp:203-214) does zero conversion then refit()s immediately; template-match primary mode REQUIRES a georeferenced SRC (requireSrcGeo, rs_template_matcher.cpp:151-160) so the mismatch is on the designed-for path; ExistingSeeds mode confirmed broken: qgsgeoreferencermainwindow.cpp:363 feeds g.sourcePoint() (map coords) as col/row, rs_template_matcher.cpp:212-216 lround(sx) -> out-of-bounds -> zero matches with threshold message; SIFT-on-unreferenced mixes (col,-line) picks vs (col,+line) SIFT - provider gt[5]=-1 verified)
  - *Callchain*: `RsSiftTask/RsTemplateMatcher (Task Center worker) -> inliers/matches -> QMessageBox accept -> session.appendGcps(pairs) -> refit -> QgsGeorefTransform::fit -> getPixelCoords misinterprets pixel indices as map coords; markers QgsGeorefDataPoint::updateMarkers setWorldPos(sourcePoint) plot pixels on a map-unit canvas.`
  - *Code context*: `SIFT acceptance (309): 'pairs.append( QgsGcpPoint( m.srcPx, m.dstWorld, destCrs, true ) );' with RsSiftMatcher::Match::srcPx documented as 'Pixel coords in source raster' (rs_sift_matcher.h) produced at rs_sift_matcher.cpp:168 'mm.srcPx = QgsPointXY( srcPts[i].x / srcScale, srcPts[i].y / srcScale );'. Template acceptance (460) identical for rs_template_matcher.cpp:267 'm.srcPx = QgsPointXY( sx, sy );' (grid col/row). No conversion to source-layer map coordinates anywhere. The fit treats sourcePoint as MAP coords when georeferenced: QgsGeorefTransform::updateParametersFromGcps (qgsgeoreftransform.cpp:184-187) 'mRasterChangeCoords.getPixelCoords( sourceCoordinates )' and toColumnLine (qgsrasterchangecoords.cpp:70-78) divides (p-mUL)/res.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Searched for any conversion between matcher output and session insertion (session, window, matcher) - none exists. Considered 'maybe fit expects pixels when georeferenced' - refuted by getPixelCoords dividing (p-UL)/res, which maps map->pixel; feeding pixels produces (pixel-UL)/res garbage as claimed.
- **Review note**: None. Impact framing accurate: both auto-match features produce garbage exactly when they succeed on georeferenced sources, silently (fit succeeds).
- **Finding GEOREF-3**: `SIFT acceptance (309): 'pairs.append( QgsGcpPoint( m.srcPx, m.dstWorld, destCrs, true ) );' with RsSiftMatcher::Match::srcPx documented as 'Pixel coords in source raster' (rs_sift_matcher.h) produced at rs_sift_matcher.cpp:168 'mm.srcPx = QgsPointXY( srcPts[i].x / srcScale, srcPts[i].y / srcScale );'. Template acceptance (460) identical for rs_template_matcher.cpp:267 'm.srcPx = QgsPointXY( sx, sy );' (grid col/row). No conversion to source-layer map coordinates anywhere. The fit treats sourcePoint as MAP coords when georeferenced: QgsGeorefTransform::updateParametersFromGcps (qgsgeoreftransform.cpp:184-187) 'mRasterChangeCoords.getPixelCoords( sourceCoordinates )' and toColumnLine (qgsrasterchangecoords.cpp:70-78) divides (p-mUL)/res.`

## Suggested fix
- Address the root cause directly with minimal, surgical changes adhering to project coding standards.

## Acceptance criteria

- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

- Finding GEOREF-3: #34 only migrated matching to Task Center (infra). No closed issue covers matcher-to-session coordinate semantics. New root cause.

## Summary
fit() residual engine incompatible with RPC: panel-CRS-unit destinations fed to WGS84-degree inverse; Y-flip unpaired - residuals wrong on perfect models. Specifically, fit() residual engine is incompatible with RpcPhysical: destination points are fed in panel-CRS units to a WGS84-degree RPC inverse, and the facade Y-flip is unpaired (invertYAxis ignored by the RPC impl), so RPC residuals/RMS are garbage (residual.y ~ 2*row) or silently invalid.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/app/georeferencer/qgsgeoreftransform.cpp:52-92,216-229` (sourcePixelResiduals / QgsGeorefTransform::transformWorldToRaster)

## User impact
- RPC mode's entire quality-feedback loop (RMS label, per-point residual table, scatter plot, marker residual arrows, 精化前/后 RMS diagnostic added by #286) shows garbage or nothing. Users cannot judge an RPC fit; refinement 'improvement' display is meaningless even though the underlying bias decision (computed inside updateParametersFromGcps with raw GDAL calls) is correct.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (GEOREF-2)**: RPC mode in the I2M window with any GCPs. Case A (projected panel CRS, the default): UTM meters are passed as lon/lat degrees to GDALRPCTransform inverse -> failure or nonsense -> residuals become the NaN sentinel, 'RMS: —', refinement diagnostic cleared, no error. Case B (EPSG:4326 panel CRS): predicted.y = -line vs observed.y = +line (canvas picks store (col,-line) because the QGIS provider forces gt[5]=-1 for unreferenced rasters, src/core/providers/gdal/qgsgdalprovider.cpp:673-678; georeferenced sources get (col,line) y-down and mirror identically) -> residual.y = ~2*row even for a perfect RPC model; RMS ~ image height in pixels.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (GEOREF-2)**: Residuals computed by converting dst into the RPC model's WGS84 output space (the setDestinationCrs seam added for #286) and comparing in a consistent y convention with the stored source points, as done for linear/helmert where the test comment says 'invertY bookends cancel' (test_georeferencing_session.cpp:229).

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (GEOREF-2)**: For RpcPhysical the bookends do not cancel: residual y is mirrored (perfect model reports residuals of order 2*pixel row, e.g. hundreds of px on a 1000-row image) or all residuals are invalid. test_georeferencing_session.cpp:348-358 only asserts fit.rms >= 0 and fit.rms < fit.refinementRmsBefore - both hold equally for the mirrored values, so tests stay green; test_rpc_gcp_refine.cpp exercises the raw transformer only.

## Root cause
- **GEOREF-2**: CONFIRMED (both sub-claims hold at HEAD). Case A CRS: fit() collects dst homogenized to targetCrs = first enabled GCP's dest CRS = panel CRS, default EPSG:32650 (rs_georef_params_panel.cpp:339-343); makeConfiguredTransform does call impl->setDestinationCrs (qgsgeoreftransform.cpp:42) but QgsRpcGcpTransformer uses mDestinationCrs ONLY inside the refinement-bias block (qgsrpcgcptransformer.cpp:190-206, the #286 fix) - transform()/rpcTransformWithBias never converts, so UTM meters hit GDALRPCTransform bDstToSrc as if lon/lat -> fail/garbage -> rsGeorefInvalidResidual. Case B Y-flip: QgsRpcGcpTransformer::updateParametersFromGcps declares 'bool /*invertYAxis*/' (:121-123) so the facade's unconditional raster.setY(-raster.y()) (qgsgeoreftransform.cpp:227) is unpaired for RPC: GDALRPCTransform inverse already returns y-down line, predicted=(col,-line) vs observed=toSourcePixel=toColumnLine=(col,line) (qgsrasterchangecoords.cpp:70-78) -> residual.y ~ -2*row on a perfect model; test_georeferencing_session.cpp:348-358 only asserts rms>=0 and rms<refinementRmsBefore so garbage passes (verified assertions at :355-357)
  - *Callchain*: `RsGeoreferencingSession::refit -> QgsGeorefTransform::fit -> sourcePixelResiduals -> QgsGeorefTransform::transformWorldToRaster -> QgsGcpTransformerInterface::transform -> rpcTransformWithBias(dst->src) -> GDALRPCTransform. Then shell onSessionFitChanged (qgsgeoref_shell_window.cpp:1303-1376) shows fit.rms/residuals in panel, GCP table, scatter, marker arrows, refinement before/after labels.`
  - *Code context*: `sourcePixelResiduals (line 65): 'if ( !xf.transformWorldToRaster( dst.at( i ), predicted ) )' - dst comes from collectEnabledGcps homogenized to targetCrs (line 374), typically the panel CRS (default EPSG:32650, rs_georef_params_panel.cpp:339-341). transformWorldToRaster (line 227) unconditionally 'raster.setY( -raster.y() )', which pairs with impls that honor invertYAxis (linear/helmert/GDAL flip internally); QgsRpcGcpTransformer::updateParametersFromGcps declares 'bool /*invertYAxis*/' (qgsrpcgcptransformer.cpp:123) - GDAL's RPC natively consumes y-down pixel/line, so the facade flip is unpaired.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Primary refutation hypothesis was that setDestinationCrs (added for #286) also covers the residual path - refuted by reading qgsrpcgcptransformer.cpp: mDestinationCrs appears only in the wgsDst lambda. Second hypothesis: GDALRPCTransform might accept projected coords - refuted: GDAL RPC transformer works strictly in WGS84 lon/lat on the destination side (rpcTransformWithBias subtracts degree-unit biases confirming the contract). Unreferenced-canvas gt[5]=-1 claim verified at qgsgdalprovider.cpp:673-677.
- **Review note**: Line refs all accurate at HEAD. Sign of Case B residual is -2*row (finding says ~2*row - magnitude claim correct). The bias decision inside updateParametersFromGcps IS correct (#286), as the finding concedes - defect is strictly the residual/RMS feedback path.
- **Finding GEOREF-2**: `sourcePixelResiduals (line 65): 'if ( !xf.transformWorldToRaster( dst.at( i ), predicted ) )' - dst comes from collectEnabledGcps homogenized to targetCrs (line 374), typically the panel CRS (default EPSG:32650, rs_georef_params_panel.cpp:339-341). transformWorldToRaster (line 227) unconditionally 'raster.setY( -raster.y() )', which pairs with impls that honor invertYAxis (linear/helmert/GDAL flip internally); QgsRpcGcpTransformer::updateParametersFromGcps declares 'bool /*invertYAxis*/' (qgsrpcgcptransformer.cpp:123) - GDAL's RPC natively consumes y-down pixel/line, so the facade flip is unpaired.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (GEOREF-2).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #286 (line 3) fixed bias units/median/improvement inside the transformer; no closed issue covers the residual engine's CRS-space or Y-convention mismatch. Adjacent root cause, distinct fix surface - not a dupe.
- Finding GEOREF-2: #286 fixed bias units/median/improvement-check inside QgsRpcGcpTransformer; no closed issue covers the residual engine's CRS-space or Y-convention mismatch with RPC. Adjacent-but-distinct root cause in the same feature area.

## Summary
TaskCenter terminal-state regression: racing progress/log records regress Completed/Failed tasks to permanent Running zombies. Specifically, updateTaskProgress/markTaskRunning only guard Canceled - a terminal (Completed/Failed) task is regressed back to Running by a racing progress/log record, leaving a permanent zombie that consumes a concurrency slot.

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/framework/task_center.cpp:549-582, 817-829, 843-854` (TaskCenter::processJobRecord / TaskCenter::updateTaskProgress / TaskCenter::markTaskRunning)

## User impact
- Each occurrence permanently burns one slot in processNextQueuedTasks' runningByProfile/totalRunning/runningTotalMb accounting (L627-634), so repeated occurrences shrink effective parallelism to zero; UI (task_center_dock refreshTaskList) shows the task running forever; retry/cancel UX degrades (cancelTask still works but waitForTask callers already returned Completed).

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (CONC-2)**: Concrete interleaving: (a) T calls JobEngine::submit, gets jobId; (b) worker W picks it up and reports progress 0.5; (c) T registers m_taskByJobId[jobId] (L511 or L792), snapshots a RUNNING record and enters processJobRecord, passing the L551 terminality check; (d) T is preempted between L553 and L824; (e) W finishes the job and its terminal notify is processed: task becomes Completed and the dedup/dispatch keys are erased; (f) T resumes, finds m_lastForwardedProgress erased (-2.0 != 0.5) and calls updateTaskProgress -> L821 guard sees Completed (not Canceled) -> L824 writes status=Running. No further job records exist (job terminal, mapping erased), so nothing ever repairs the state.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (CONC-2)**: Terminal status is final: a stale progress/log record arriving after the terminal transition is dropped (the L551 check's intent).

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (CONC-2)**: The check and the write are in different critical sections; updateTaskProgress/markTaskRunning resurrect the task to Running with progress 0.5 and duplicate every log line into logBuffer. The task is a permanent zombie Running.

## Root cause
- **CONC-2**: CONFIRMED (processJobRecord :549-553 terminality check in its own critical section, mutations in later separate sections; updateTaskProgress :817-824 guards ONLY status==Canceled then writes status=Running - regresses Completed/Failed; markTaskRunning :843-849 same; ADR 0051 line 22 'terminal mark* methods treat terminal as final' - invariant deliberately enforced only on mark*, matching the finding; the demanded interleaving is concrete and valid: T (main thread, flushPendingLaunches :804-806 catch-up or submitJobImpl :519-520) passes check, W (worker) terminal notify erases m_taskByJobId/m_lastForwardedProgress/m_forwardedLogCounts (:609-613), T resumes: value(taskId,-2.0)!=0.5 -> updateTaskProgress flips Completed->Running and the log loop re-appends every line from forwarded=0 - permanent zombie, no further records exist (mapping erased) to repair it)
  - *Callchain*: `Thread T (GUI thread in submitJobImpl L519-520, or the flushing thread in flushPendingLaunches L804-806): JobEngine::snapshot -> onJobRecord(runningRecord) -> processJobRecord [check passes] -> preempted -> Thread W (JobEngine worker): notify(terminal) -> onJobRecord -> markTaskCompleted -> Completed + m_taskByJobId.remove/m_forwardedLogCounts.remove/m_lastForwardedProgress.remove (L609-613) -> T resumes: updateTaskProgress(0.5) flips Completed->Running; log loop re-appends every log line (dedup counter was erased)`
  - *Code context*: `processJobRecord validates terminality once, in a SEPARATE critical section from the mutations it then performs:
  { QMutexLocker locker(&m_mutex);
    if ( !m_tasks.contains(taskId) || isTerminalStatus(m_tasks[taskId].status) ) return; }   // L549-553
  ... progress handling ...
  if ( changed ) updateTaskProgress( taskId, record.progress );                              // L568
updateTaskProgress then does:
  if ( !m_tasks.contains(taskId) || m_tasks[taskId].status == TaskStatus::Canceled ) return;  // L821 - Canceled ONLY
  m_tasks[taskId].progressPercentage = progress;
  m_tasks[taskId].status = TaskStatus::Running;                                              // L823-824 regresses Completed/Failed -> Running
markTaskRunning has the same Canceled-only guard (L847) and sets Running at L849. The ADR 0051 invariant 'terminal mark* methods treat terminal as final' (docs/adr/0051 L21-22) is thus only enforced on the mark* methods, not on the progress/running writers.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Checked lock scopes at HEAD: the gap between :553 and :824 spans three lock/unlock cycles - real TOCTOU window. Checked whether flushPendingLaunches re-checks terminality before applying the record: it delegates to onJobRecord->processJobRecord which has the same split. No catch-up re-snapshot of terminal jobs exists (mapping erased), so nothing repairs the zombie.
- **Review note**: None.
- **Finding CONC-2**: `processJobRecord validates terminality once, in a SEPARATE critical section from the mutations it then performs:
  { QMutexLocker locker(&m_mutex);
    if ( !m_tasks.contains(taskId) || isTerminalStatus(m_tasks[taskId].status) ) return; }   // L549-553
  ... progress handling ...
  if ( changed ) updateTaskProgress( taskId, record.progress );                              // L568
updateTaskProgress then does:
  if ( !m_tasks.contains(taskId) || m_tasks[taskId].status == TaskStatus::Canceled ) return;  // L821 - Canceled ONLY
  m_tasks[taskId].progressPercentage = progress;
  m_tasks[taskId].status = TaskStatus::Running;                                              // L823-824 regresses Completed/Failed -> Running
markTaskRunning has the same Canceled-only guard (L847) and sets Running at L849. The ADR 0051 invariant 'terminal mark* methods treat terminal as final' (docs/adr/0051 L21-22) is thus only enforced on the mark* methods, not on the progress/running writers.`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure proper synchronization, atomic state transitions, clean thread termination, and avoidance of use-after-free or race conditions on worker/GUI threads.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (CONC-2).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- No closed issue covers status regression via progress/log writers (#205-#213, #220, #233, batch-21 verified in issues-closed.txt). Clean; distinct from C57's #207 residual-watcher teardown race.
- Finding CONC-2: Not a dupe: ADR 0051 (closed) established the single-listener + catch-up design and claimed 'terminal is final'; the delta logic dedups terminal marks but not the progress/log writers. No closed issue (#205-#213, #220, #233, #237, batch-21) covers status regression.

## Summary
#209 RSS retry timer is created on JobEngine worker threads (no event dispatcher) so it never fires - queued-task starvation persists on the worker path. Specifically, TaskCenter #209 RSS retry timer is created on JobEngine worker threads (std::thread, no event dispatcher) so it never fires - worker-path starvation persists.

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/framework/task_center.cpp:689-703` (TaskCenter::processNextQueuedTasks)

## User impact
- Silent scheduler deadlock under memory pressure: pipelines stall, waitForTask/waitForPipeline block to their 30/60-min timeouts, MCP/agent tool calls time out. Recovery only via a new main-thread submit.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (CONC-1)**: 1) One or more tasks run and finish while process RSS is at/above the 75% watermark (plausible right after a big raster task frees memory - VmRSS decays asynchronously). 2) The LAST running task's terminal record is processed by its JobEngine worker (the common path). 3) Queued tasks exist. Thread A (worker) executes the singleShot at task_center.cpp:693; thread B does not exist - nobody ever runs the event loop for A's thread, so the retry never fires and no other terminal transition is pending (totalRunning==0).

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (CONC-1)**: The #209 re-arm retries scheduling after 250ms so queued tasks are launched once RSS drops, regardless of which thread processed the terminal transition.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (CONC-1)**: On the worker-thread path the retry lambda is never scheduled; queued tasks stay Queued indefinitely (until the user happens to submit/mark another task from the main thread). The exact starvation #209 was filed for still reproduces whenever the terminal transition lands on a worker.

## Root cause
- **CONC-1**: CONFIRMED (task_center.cpp:688-703 QTimer::singleShot(250,...) with NO context object - Qt docs: timer created in calling thread, and QTimer requires a thread with an event loop; JobEngine workers are raw std::thread (job_engine.cpp:442 m_workers.emplace_back) with no dispatcher -> QObject::startTimer fails ('Timers can only be used with threads started with QThread') and the callback never runs; chain verified: workerLoop:474 -> runOperatorJob terminal notify(:546 invokes listener synchronously on worker) -> onJobRecord(task_center.cpp:529) -> markTaskCompleted:893 processNextQueuedTasks under m_mutex on the worker; grep shows the singleShot at :693 is the ONLY auto re-arm in task_center.cpp - no periodic scheduler self-heals; remaining processNextQueuedTasks callers (:462 submit, :1033 cancel, :1269 submitPipeline) are main-thread user actions exactly as the finding's recovery path states; #209 fix 763966246f added exactly this line and works only when the transition lands on the main thread)
  - *Callchain*: `JobEngine workerLoop -> runOperatorJob -> notify(terminal record) -> TaskCenter::onJobRecord -> processJobRecord -> markTaskCompleted -> processNextQueuedTasks (m_mutex held, worker thread) -> memoryPressureHigh()==true && totalRunning==0 -> QTimer::singleShot(250, ...) on std::thread`
  - *Code context*: `processNextQueuedTasks() runs with m_mutex held on whatever thread performed the terminal transition. Terminal transitions for JobEngine-submitted tasks execute on the worker: JobEngine worker -> notify(rec) (job_engine.cpp:546-564, invoked from runOperatorJob finish lambdas on the worker) -> TaskCenter::onJobRecord (task_center.cpp:532) -> processJobRecord -> markTaskCompleted/Failed/Canceled -> processNextQueuedTasks. The #209 re-arm is:
  if ( m_resourceMonitor.memoryPressureHigh() ) {
      if ( totalRunning == 0 && QCoreApplication::instance() ) {
          QTimer::singleShot( 250, [this]() { ... processNextQueuedTasks(); flushPendingLaunches(); flushPendingSignals(); } );
      }
      break;
  }
QTimer::singleShot with no context object starts the timer in the CALLING thread. A JobEngine worker is a raw std::thread with no QEventLoop/event dispatcher; per Qt docs (Threads and QObjects): 'Event driven objects may only be used in a single thread. Specifically, this applies to the timer mechanism' and 'If no event loop is running ... the QTimer will never emit its timeout() signal'. QObject::startTimer fails with 'Timers can only be used with threads started with QThread' and returns -1; the 250ms callback is never invoked.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Checked ADR 0051/0052 and batch-21 #177/#178 (8cc594609a touched task_center.cpp 15 lines - the terminal-final guard, not the timer path); no alternative wake mechanism exists (no QThread polling of RSS, no worker-side condition-variable re-check after 250ms).
- **Review note**: None material. Trigger plausibility note: after glibc frees a large raster buffer RSS usually drops promptly, so the starved state needs lingering residency (allocator retention, page cache accounting in same-process RSS) - real but narrower than 'every big task'.
- **Finding CONC-1**: `processNextQueuedTasks() runs with m_mutex held on whatever thread performed the terminal transition. Terminal transitions for JobEngine-submitted tasks execute on the worker: JobEngine worker -> notify(rec) (job_engine.cpp:546-564, invoked from runOperatorJob finish lambdas on the worker) -> TaskCenter::onJobRecord (task_center.cpp:532) -> processJobRecord -> markTaskCompleted/Failed/Canceled -> processNextQueuedTasks. The #209 re-arm is:
  if ( m_resourceMonitor.memoryPressureHigh() ) {
      if ( totalRunning == 0 && QCoreApplication::instance() ) {
          QTimer::singleShot( 250, [this]() { ... processNextQueuedTasks(); flushPendingLaunches(); flushPendingSignals(); } );
      }
      break;
  }
QTimer::singleShot with no context object starts the timer in the CALLING thread. A JobEngine worker is a raw std::thread with no QEventLoop/event dispatcher; per Qt docs (Threads and QObjects): 'Event driven objects may only be used in a single thread. Specifically, this applies to the timer mechanism' and 'If no event loop is running ... the QTimer will never emit its timeout() signal'. QObject::startTimer fails with 'Timers can only be used with threads started with QThread' and returns -1; the 250ms callback is never invoked.`

## Suggested fix
- Ensure proper synchronization, atomic state transitions, clean thread termination, and avoidance of use-after-free or race conditions on worker/GUI threads.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (CONC-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #209 (line 57) closed by adding this timer; the fix is incomplete on the worker-transition path - incomplete-fix angle verified by git show 763966246f (+30 lines task_center.cpp, the singleShot). Not a dupe of #208/#110.
- Finding CONC-1: #209 CLOSED via commit 763966246f ('RSS retry timer') which added exactly this QTimer::singleShot. Fix works only for the main-thread path (enqueueTask/submitPipeline callers); the primary terminal-transition path (ADR 0051 listener on JobEngine workers) is unfixed. Not a dupe of #208 (zero-step pipeline) or #110.
title: [P2][concurrency/lifecycle] #209 RSS retry timer is created on JobEngine worker threads (no event dispatcher) so it never fires - queued-task starvation persists on the worker path

Vector overlay adapters combine geometries across different CRSs with no transform (#194 fixed only clip). Specifically, Vector overlay adapters silently combine geometries across different CRSs - #194 fix only patched clip; difference/intersection/union/spatial-query family still unguarded.

## Area
Concurrency / Job Engine / Lifecycle

## Type
concurrency/lifecycle

P2

## Summary
gdal tool wrappers construct always-failing or precision-truncating CLI invocations (grid -a_nodata, gdalmanage default action, proximity -targetvalue, reproject/dstnodata 6-decimal formatting). This issue aggregates 4 related finding(s): PROVG-1, PROVG-2, PROVG-3, OPS-6. Specifically, gdal:grid passes nonexistent -a_nodata flag — the tool always errors whenever NODATA is present (dialog default -9999); -tr without -txe/-tye also fails. Specifically, gdalmanage wrapper's default ACTION 'info' is not a valid gdalmanage mode (copy|delete|identify|rename) — the default action always fails. Specifically, gdal_proximity wrapper maps TARGET_VALUE to nonexistent -targetvalue flag (valid flag is -values).

## Area
Processing Framework / GDAL & OTB Providers

## Type
processing/provider

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/providers/gdal_tools/algorithms/gdal_grid.cpp:67-70, 82-87` (GdalGridAlgorithm::buildArgs)
- `src/processing/providers/gdal_tools/algorithms/gdalmanage.cpp:11-13, 26-30` (GdalManageAlgorithm::initAlgorithm / buildArgs)
- `src/processing/providers/gdal_tools/algorithms/gdal_proximity.cpp:43-45` (GdalProximityAlgorithm::buildArgs)
- `src/operators/gdal/gdal_reproject_operator.cpp:162-171` (GdalReprojectOperator::run)

## User impact
- gdal:grid is unusable in the default dialog flow and in the respecified-pixel-size flow — always-failing tool with a cryptic downstream error
- The default and most common gdal:manage action never runs; user gets a generic failure
- Proximity restricted to a target value can never run; only the whole-raster distance mode works
- Grid-alignment precision defect in the primary reprojection entry point; downstream same-grid operators (change detection, apply_mask) then reject or misplace the result.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (PROVG-1)**: Run gdal:grid from the toolbox with the default NODATA (-9999), or set PIXEL_SIZE without EXTENT
- **Trigger (PROVG-2)**: Run gdal:manage without changing ACTION (default 'info')
- **Trigger (PROVG-3)**: Run gdal:proximity with TARGET_VALUE set
- **Trigger (OPS-6)**: gdal:reproject with targetResolution in degrees, e.g. 2.69495e-5 (~3 m) or 8.98315e-5 (~10 m): to_string yields '0.000027'/'0.000090', rounding the pixel size by up to ~2%; nodata like -3.4e38 serializes as a 39-digit fixed string.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (PROVG-1)**: Wrapper emits only flags gdal_grid supports (drop -a_nodata or use a supported mechanism); -tr accompanied by extent or translated to -outsize
- **Expected (PROVG-2)**: args << "identify" maps to a real mode and the tool reports dataset info
- **Expected (PROVG-3)**: -values <n> (possibly comma-separated list) is emitted
- **Expected (OPS-6)**: util::fmtDouble(targetResolution)/fmtDouble(nodata) as used by the reference path and gdal:clip.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (PROVG-1)**: gdal_grid aborts with 'Unknown argument: -a_nodata' (or ERROR 5 for -tr-only); algorithm throws 'GDAL tool gdal_grid.py failed'
- **Actual (PROVG-2)**: gdalmanage rejects 'info' as an unknown mode; algorithm throws 'GDAL tool gdalmanage failed'
- **Actual (PROVG-3)**: Unknown option -targetvalue -> tool exits non-zero -> 'GDAL tool gdal_proximity failed'
- **Actual (OPS-6)**: Rounded 6-decimal values are passed to GDALWarp; output pixel size deviates from the requested resolution, accumulating to tens of pixels of misalignment across a large scene and breaking exact grid alignment with co-registered products.

## Root cause
- **PROVG-1**: CONFIRMED empirically on system GDAL 3.13.2 (= linked version): 'gdal_grid -a_nodata -9999 ...' -> 'ERROR 1: Unknown argument: -a_nodata' (flag absent from --help); '-tr without -txe/-tye' -> 'ERROR 5: -txe ad -tye arguments must be provided when resolution is provided'. Wrapper code gdal_grid.cpp:67-70,82-87 as cited; NODATA declared with default -9999 (:24-26) so dialog flow always trips
  - *Callchain*: `Toolbox dialog / pipeline JSON -> TaskCenter -> ProviderAlgorithmAdapter::execute -> GdalToolWrapper::processAlgorithm -> GdalGridAlgorithm::buildArgs -> gdal_grid subprocess (exit 1)`
  - *Code context*: `if (parameters.contains("NODATA") && !parameters.value("NODATA").toString().isEmpty()) { double nodata = parameters.value("NODATA").toDouble(); args << "-a_nodata" << QString::number(nodata); } — NODATA is declared with default -9999 (initAlgorithm line 24-26) so any dialog-built parameter map carries it. Verified on the linked GDAL 3.13.2: `gdal_grid -a_nodata -9999 ...` -> 'ERROR 1: Unknown argument: -a_nodata' (gdal_grid --help has no nodata option at all; -a_nodata belongs to gdal_edit). Additionally line 82-87 emits -tr without -txe/-tye whenever PIXEL_SIZE is set but EXTENT is empty -> 'ERROR 5: -txe ad -tye arguments must be provided when resolution is provided'.`
- **PROVG-2**: CONFIRMED empirically: gdalmanage modes are {copy,delete,identify,rename}; 'gdalmanage info <file>' -> 'Error: Zero positional arguments expected'. Wrapper gdalmanage.cpp:11-13,26-30 keeps invalid 'info' as index 0/default
  - *Callchain*: `Toolbox dialog / pipeline -> TaskCenter -> ProviderAlgorithmAdapter::execute -> GdalToolWrapper::processAlgorithm -> GdalManageAlgorithm::buildArgs -> gdalmanage subprocess (argparse error)`
  - *Code context*: `QStringList actions; actions << "info" << "copy" << "rename" << "delete"; ... QString action = actions.value(actionIndex, "info"); args << action; — default enum index 0 selects 'info'. Verified on GDAL 3.13.2: `gdalmanage --help` shows '{copy,delete,identify,rename}'; `gdalmanage info <file>` -> 'Error: Zero positional arguments expected' + usage (exit != 0). The intended mode is 'identify'.`
- **PROVG-3**: CONFIRMED empirically: gdal_proximity --help lists '-values <n>,<n>,<n>'; 'gdal_proximity src dst -targetvalue 6' -> 'Unrecognized option : -targetvalue'. Wrapper gdal_proximity.cpp:43-45 as cited
  - *Callchain*: `Toolbox dialog / pipeline -> TaskCenter -> ProviderAlgorithmAdapter::execute -> GdalToolWrapper::processAlgorithm -> GdalProximityAlgorithm::buildArgs -> gdal_proximity subprocess`
  - *Code context*: `if (parameters.contains("TARGET_VALUE") && !parameters.value("TARGET_VALUE").toString().isEmpty()) { args << "-targetvalue" << parameters.value("TARGET_VALUE").toString(); } — verified on GDAL 3.13.2: gdal_proximity --help lists '-values <n>,<n>,<n>' (no -targetvalue in any GDAL version); `gdal_proximity src dst -targetvalue 6` prints usage and exits non-zero.`
- **OPS-6**: CONFIRMED (gdal_reproject_operator.cpp:162-165 targetResolution branch uses std::to_string (=%f 6 decimals: 2.69495e-5 -> '0.000027'); :167-170 -dstnodata same; reference branch :151-161 correctly uses fmtDouble (%.17g) - the #230 asymmetry is visible in one function)
  - *Callchain*: `MCP/CLI execute_algorithm -> RsOperatorAdapter::execute -> GdalReprojectOperator::run -> runGdalWarp (gdal_operator_utils.cpp:123).`
  - *Code context*: ``} else if (targetResolution > 0.0) { options.emplace_back("-tr"); options.emplace_back(std::to_string(targetResolution)); ...` and `options.emplace_back("-dstnodata"); options.emplace_back(std::to_string(nodata));` — std::to_string is %f with 6 decimals. The reference-alignment branch above (153-161) was fixed to use util::fmtDouble (%.17g) and gdal:clip was fixed the same way, but this branch was left on to_string.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Re-derived every CLI claim by executing the actual system gdal binaries (read-only --help plus tiny WS-local runs); all four reproduce exactly as the finder claimed. No wrapper-level pre-validation intercepts these flags (buildArgs emits them verbatim).
- **Review note**: None. All three tools registered (provider.cpp:52,68,71 addAlgorithm). OPS-6's -3.4e38 nodata case mostly round-trips through %f (39 digits > double precision); the sharp edge is small resolutions/magnitudes - impact statement slightly overstated for huge sentinels, correct for sub-arcsecond -tr.
- **Finding PROVG-1**: `if (parameters.contains("NODATA") && !parameters.value("NODATA").toString().isEmpty()) { double nodata = parameters.value("NODATA").toDouble(); args << "-a_nodata" << QString::number(nodata); } — NODATA is declared with default -9999 (initAlgorithm line 24-26) so any dialog-built parameter map carries it. Verified on the linked GDAL 3.13.2: `gdal_grid -a_nodata -9999 ...` -> 'ERROR 1: Unknown argument: -a_nodata' (gdal_grid --help has no nodata option at all; -a_nodata belongs to gdal_edit). Additionally line 82-87 emits -tr without -txe/-tye whenever PIXEL_SIZE is set but EXTENT is empty -> 'ERROR 5: -txe ad -tye arguments must be provided when resolution is provided'.`
- **Finding PROVG-2**: `QStringList actions; actions << "info" << "copy" << "rename" << "delete"; ... QString action = actions.value(actionIndex, "info"); args << action; — default enum index 0 selects 'info'. Verified on GDAL 3.13.2: `gdalmanage --help` shows '{copy,delete,identify,rename}'; `gdalmanage info <file>` -> 'Error: Zero positional arguments expected' + usage (exit != 0). The intended mode is 'identify'.`
- **Finding PROVG-3**: `if (parameters.contains("TARGET_VALUE") && !parameters.value("TARGET_VALUE").toString().isEmpty()) { args << "-targetvalue" << parameters.value("TARGET_VALUE").toString(); } — verified on GDAL 3.13.2: gdal_proximity --help lists '-values <n>,<n>,<n>' (no -targetvalue in any GDAL version); `gdal_proximity src dst -targetvalue 6` prints usage and exits non-zero.`
- **Finding OPS-6**: ``} else if (targetResolution > 0.0) { options.emplace_back("-tr"); options.emplace_back(std::to_string(targetResolution)); ...` and `options.emplace_back("-dstnodata"); options.emplace_back(std::to_string(nodata));` — std::to_string is %f with 6 decimals. The reference-alignment branch above (153-161) was fixed to use util::fmtDouble (%.17g) and gdal:clip was fixed the same way, but this branch was left on to_string.`

## Suggested fix
- Align parameter definitions, argument builders, and result harvesting with the QGIS/GDAL/OTB provider execution contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (PROVG-1, PROVG-2, PROVG-3, OPS-6).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #169 (line 97) fixed -of/-ts/-te/-outsize (8cc594609a touched gdal_grid.cpp 2 lines); #228 (line 38) fixed gdalmanage NEWNAME + others (646d3ea112 +9 lines, kept 'info'); #230 (line 36) fixed clip + reproject reference branch (646d3ea112 touched gdal_reproject_operator.cpp but left the -tr/-dstnodata branch). All three findings are genuine incomplete-fix residuals, not dupes.
- Finding PROVG-1: #169 (commit 8cc594609a) fixed -of/-ts/-te/-outsize in these wrappers but left -a_nodata; #228 batch fixed contour/gdalmanage validation, not gdal_grid. Verified present at HEAD d9c59e5b.
- Finding PROVG-2: #228 (commit 646d3ea112) added the NEWNAME validation in this file but kept the invalid 'info' mode word. Verified at HEAD.
- Finding PROVG-3: #169 fixed -of/-ts/-te/-outsize flags (commit 8cc594609a), #228 fixed zMin/zMax/gdaltransform/stats/contour/gdalmanage — -targetvalue untouched. Verified at HEAD.
- Finding OPS-6: #230 'gdal:clip truncates -te/-dstnodata floats to 6 decimals' — commit 646d3ea112 fixed clip and reproject's reference branch only; the targetResolution/dstnodata branch still uses std::to_string at HEAD. Prior fix incomplete.
title: [P2][processing/provider] gdal tool wrappers construct always-failing or precision-truncating CLI invocations (grid -a_nodata, gdalmanage default action, proximity -targetvalue, reproject/dstnodata 6-decimal formatting)

## Summary
Generic GDAL-metadata TOA reflectance inverts scale semantics (phys = DN*scale+offset, not (DN+offset)/scale). Specifically, Generic (GDAL-metadata) TOA reflectance inverts scale semantics: rho = (DN+offset)/scale instead of GDAL's phys = DN*scale + offset.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/radiometric_calibration.cpp:296-307, 403-409` (RadiometricCalibration::loadGdalMetadata / toToaReflectance)

## User impact
- Silently wrong reflectances by up to 8 orders of magnitude on the generic sensor path; downstream indices, change detection and the SICNU_RADIOMETRIC_STATE=comparable check all operate on garbage values.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSALGO-2)**: Radiometric calibration to TOA reflectance on a raster without MTL/MTD whose bands expose GDAL SCALE/OFFSET (MODIS HDF4/HDF5/NetCDF, scaled GeoTIFFs) - e.g. MOD09 with scale_factor 0.0001

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSALGO-2)**: phys = DN * scale + offset (GDAL convention) -> MODIS DN 5000 with scale 1e-4 -> 0.5 reflectance

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSALGO-2)**: (DN + offset)/scale -> 5000/1e-4 = 5e7

## Root cause
- **RSALGO-2**: CONFIRMED (toToaReflectance generic branch radiometric_calibration.cpp:403-409 computes (dn+offset)*invScale; S2 loader sets c.scale=QUANTIFICATION_VALUE (~10000) at :250 so divide is correct for S2; loadGdalMetadata :296-297 sets c.scale=GDALGetRasterScale which per current official GDAL docs means 'Units value = (raw value * scale) + offset' (verified against gdal.org API docs; system GDAL 3.13.2) - for MODIS scale 1e-4 the code yields DN*1e4 instead of DN*1e-4, off by 1/scale^2=1e8; offset also applied before scaling instead of after; reachable: loadMetadata falls back to loadGdalMetadata when no MTL/MTD sibling, operator auto-detect returns empty and processFile still loads via fallback)
  - *Callchain*: `rs_radiometric_calibration operator (method=toa_reflectance, no MTL/MTD present) -> RadiometricCalibration::processFile:534-548 -> toToaReflectance generic branch; coefficients from loadGdalMetadata (auto-fallback when loadMetadata has empty metadataPath)`
  - *Code context*: `loadGdalMetadata stores GDAL band scale into c.scale: `c.scale = GDALGetRasterScale(band, &hasScale)`; toToaReflectance generic branch computes `reflectance[i] = (dn[i] + offset) * invScale;` with `invScale = 1.0 / c.scale`. The Sentinel-2 quantification convention (DN/10000, scale=10000) was generalized to GDAL scale_factor, but GDAL SCALE/OFFSET semantics are physical = raw * scale + offset (multiplicative scale, offset added after). For a MODIS HDF (scale_factor=1e-4, header comment says 'Generic/MODIS fallback'): computed = DN/1e-4 = DN*10000, correct = DN*1e-4 -> output inflated by 1/(scale^2) = 1e8. Additive offset is also applied before division instead of after multiplication.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Checked historical GDAL doc formula variants ('value=(raw+offset)*scale' in old docs) - even that reading contradicts the code's division; the current documented formula (raw*scale+offset, matching CF scale_factor/add_offset conventions used by MODIS/NetCDF drivers) is authoritative for the vendored/linked 3.13.2.
- **Review note**: None. Note the fix must keep the S2 divisor convention while multiplying for GDAL-loaded scale (or normalize GDAL scale to 1/scale at load time).
- **Finding RSALGO-2**: `loadGdalMetadata stores GDAL band scale into c.scale: `c.scale = GDALGetRasterScale(band, &hasScale)`; toToaReflectance generic branch computes `reflectance[i] = (dn[i] + offset) * invScale;` with `invScale = 1.0 / c.scale`. The Sentinel-2 quantification convention (DN/10000, scale=10000) was generalized to GDAL scale_factor, but GDAL SCALE/OFFSET semantics are physical = raw * scale + offset (multiplicative scale, offset added after). For a MODIS HDF (scale_factor=1e-4, header comment says 'Generic/MODIS fallback'): computed = DN/1e-4 = DN*10000, correct = DN*1e-4 -> output inflated by 1/(scale^2) = 1e8. Additive offset is also applied before division instead of after multiplication.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (RSALGO-2).

## Summary
Radiometric operators silently fall back to identity gain/bias when calibration metadata is absent and stamp output as radiance/reflectance. This issue aggregates 2 related finding(s): OPS-2, OPS-3. Specifically, rs:radiometric_calibration unit=radiance silently emits DN (gain=1/bias=0 defaults) when RADIANCE_MULT/ADD are absent and stamps the output as radiance. Specifically, rs:atmospheric_correction / rs:dn_to_radiance silently fall back to gain=1.0/bias=0.0 when metadata cannot be resolved.

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/operators/rs/rs_radiometric_calibration_operator.cpp:114-142; src/processing/algorithms/radiometric_calibration.cpp:88-121,377-382,498-511` (RsRadiometricCalibrationOperator::run / RadiometricCalibration::toRadiance / loadLandsatMtl)
- `src/operators/rs/rs_atmospheric_correction_operator.cpp:148-151, 199-229, 236-269` (atmospheric_detail::runAtmosphericCorrectionCore)

## User impact
- Quantitatively wrong radiance products enter the calibration -> atmospheric-correction -> change-detection chain with a trusted radiometric-state stamp, defeating the ADR-0114 comparability guard itself.
- Users get DN labeled as radiance/surface-reflectance without any signal; downstream radiometric-state checks are poisoned the same way as OPS-2.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (OPS-2)**: rs:radiometric_calibration with unit='radiance' on a Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 SR stack (no RADIANCE_MULT_BAND_x in MTL) or on any generic product carrying only GDAL SCALE/OFFSET metadata.
- **Trigger (OPS-3)**: rs:dn_to_radiance (or atmospheric_correction method=dn_to_radiance/dos1/dos2) on a stacked raster whose MTL/MTD is not a sibling of the input and where the caller omitted gain/bias.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (OPS-2)**: Deterministic failure ('no radiance coefficients for band N') mirroring the reflectance-path guard, before any output is created.
- **Expected (OPS-3)**: A typed error or at least a warning ('radiance gain/bias unresolved; pass gain/bias or metadata_path') — the schema advertises 'resolved from product metadata when omitted' as if it always succeeds.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (OPS-2)**: Output is an identity copy of DN labeled and stamped as radiance; run returns success.
- **Actual (OPS-3)**: Silent identity transform; output stamped as radiance (or used as-is for DOS scaling).

## Root cause
- **OPS-2**: CONFIRMED (BandCoefficients defaults gain=1/bias=0 radiometric_calibration.h:46-53; loadLandsatMtl :113-116 inserts band on ANY coefficient match so L2-SR MTL (REFLECTANCE_MULT only) yields identity radiance; toRadiance :377-382 is an unguarded linearScale; toToaReflectance Landsat branch guards at :393-394 - the codebase's own standard; up-front validation :500-511 checks only band presence; operator stamps state=radiance unconditionally rs_radiometric_calibration_operator.cpp:150-158)
  - *Callchain*: `MCP/CLI execute_algorithm -> RsOperatorAdapter::execute -> RsRadiometricCalibrationOperator::run -> RadiometricCalibration::processFile -> toRadiance; output state then consumed by rs:change_detection's radiometric comparability check (rs_change_detection_operator.cpp:244-256), which now trusts the wrong state.`
  - *Code context*: `BandCoefficients defaults radianceGain=1.0/radianceBias=0.0 (radiometric_calibration.h:66-68). loadLandsatMtl inserts a band when ANY coefficient matched (radiometric_calibration.cpp:113-116), so a Landsat C2 L2 SR MTL (REFLECTANCE_MULT only, no RADIANCE_MULT_BAND_x) yields gain=1/bias=0. toRadiance() (377-382) is MathUtils::linearScale with no 'coefficients missing' guard, unlike toToaReflectance's Landsat branch which does guard (393-394: `if (c.reflMult == 1.0 && c.reflAdd == 0.0) return false;`). loadGdalMetadata (265-312) sets only scale/offset, which toRadiance ignores entirely. The up-front validation (500-511) checks only meta.bands.contains(b), not unit-specific coefficients. The operator then stamps SICNU_RADIOMETRIC_STATE=radiance on the output (operator lines 150-158).`
- **OPS-3**: CONFIRMED (rs_atmospheric_correction_operator.cpp:148-151 defaults; :199-229 resolution chain silently falls through on every failure (no metadata, parse fail, band missing) with no warning; :263-269 stamps radiance/surface-reflectance; schema text at :45-46/:69 literally advertises 'when omitted, resolved from product metadata' - contract violation is user-visible)
  - *Callchain*: `MCP/CLI execute_algorithm -> RsOperatorAdapter::execute -> runAtmosphericCorrectionCore -> AtmosphericCorrection::processFile`
  - *Code context*: `gain/bias default to 1.0/0.0 (150-151). The metadata resolution block (199-229) only overwrites them when a metadata file is found, loads, and contains the band; every failure path (no MTL/MTD sibling, XML parse failure, band not in coefficients) falls through silently with no warning or error. processFile then runs `out[i] = gain * v + bias` (atmospheric_correction.cpp pass 3), i.e. DN passthrough for dn_to_radiance, and the operator stamps SICNU_RADIOMETRIC_STATE=radiance (263-269).`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Design-intent angle tried: no code comment or doc claims identity passthrough is intended; the reflectance-path guard demonstrates intent to fail closed on missing coefficients. QUAC path is unaffected (needs no gain/bias) - finding correctly scopes to dn_to_radiance/dos.
- **Review note**: None.
- **Finding OPS-2**: `BandCoefficients defaults radianceGain=1.0/radianceBias=0.0 (radiometric_calibration.h:66-68). loadLandsatMtl inserts a band when ANY coefficient matched (radiometric_calibration.cpp:113-116), so a Landsat C2 L2 SR MTL (REFLECTANCE_MULT only, no RADIANCE_MULT_BAND_x) yields gain=1/bias=0. toRadiance() (377-382) is MathUtils::linearScale with no 'coefficients missing' guard, unlike toToaReflectance's Landsat branch which does guard (393-394: `if (c.reflMult == 1.0 && c.reflAdd == 0.0) return false;`). loadGdalMetadata (265-312) sets only scale/offset, which toRadiance ignores entirely. The up-front validation (500-511) checks only meta.bands.contains(b), not unit-specific coefficients. The operator then stamps SICNU_RADIOMETRIC_STATE=radiance on the output (operator lines 150-158).`
- **Finding OPS-3**: `gain/bias default to 1.0/0.0 (150-151). The metadata resolution block (199-229) only overwrites them when a metadata file is found, loads, and contains the band; every failure path (no MTL/MTD sibling, XML parse failure, band not in coefficients) falls through silently with no warning or error. processFile then runs `out[i] = gain * v + bias` (atmospheric_correction.cpp pass 3), i.e. DN passthrough for dn_to_radiance, and the operator stamps SICNU_RADIOMETRIC_STATE=radiance (263-269).`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (OPS-2, OPS-3).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #127/#128/#129 (lines 105-107) built the features; no closed issue covers the identity fallback or unresolved gain/bias. Clean.
- Finding OPS-2: #127/#125 built this operator; no closed issue covers the radiance identity-passthrough (grep of issues-closed.txt: nothing on radiance defaults). Verified at HEAD.
- Finding OPS-3: No closed issue covers unresolved atmospheric gain/bias defaults (#129 added QUAC, #127 the operator). Verified at HEAD: no error branch exists when the metadata block fails.
title: [P2][algorithm/numerics] Radiometric operators silently fall back to identity gain/bias when calibration metadata is absent and stamp output as radiance/reflectance

## Summary
Radiometric calibration processFile treats NoData-unset bands as NoData=0 and NaNs every valid DN=0 pixel (deterministic, test-proven). Specifically, Radiometric calibration processFile treats NoData-unset as NoData=0 and NaNs out every valid DN=0 pixel (baseline failure a is a real product defect).

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/processing/algorithms/radiometric_calibration.cpp:530,554-558` (RadiometricCalibration::processFile)

## User impact
- Silent data corruption in the core DN->radiance/reflectance/brightness-temperature path; all three OutputUnit modes share the same clause. Fix: use the hasNodata out-param (only match bandNoData when hasNodata==true).

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (TESTS-1)**: Any input raster whose band declares no NoData value (typical for raw Landsat/Sentinel stacks produced by third-party tools or by createOutputTiff itself) and contains DN==0 pixels. Deterministic: ~1/256 pixels of uniformly distributed 8-bit data.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (TESTS-1)**: With NoData unset, DN==0 is valid data: result = gain*0 + bias = 0.0 (what the test asserts).

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (TESTS-1)**: Result pixel = NaN; output band NoData is declared NaN (line 524), so downstream stats/mosaics silently drop ~0.4% of valid pixels per 8-bit band.

## Root cause
- **TESTS-1**: CONFIRMED with live reproduction: ran audit-build tests/test_radiometric_calibration with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen -> 'processFile streams a multi-tile raster to radiance' (test_radiometric_calibration.cpp:519) FAILS at :561 'nanf is within 0.001 of 0.0'; 19/20 pass, deterministic. Root cause exactly as filed: radiometric_calibration.cpp:530 calls 1-arg bandNoDataValue(b) (hasNodata out-param dropped, wrapper gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:385-402 returns GDALGetRasterNoDataValue verbatim = 0.0 when unset); :556 clause |v-bandNoData|<1e-4 NaNs every DN==0 pixel; fixture band=(x+3y)%256 has band[0]==0 at (0,0); createOutputTiff sets no NoData so input is unset; contrast readBandWindow :219-226 uses hasNodata correctly with a comment stating the violated invariant.
  - *Callchain*: `processFile -> GdalDatasetWrapper::bandNoDataValue(b) [ignores hasNodata] -> tile loop converts v==0 to NaN -> outDataset.writeBandWindow`
  - *Code context*: `Line 530: const double bandNoData = srcDataset.bandNoDataValue(b); — the 1-arg call ignores the hasNodata out-param. GdalDatasetWrapper::bandNoDataValue (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:385-402) returns GDALGetRasterNoDataValue verbatim: 0.0 with hasNodataInt=0 when the band declares no NoData. Line 556 then applies: if (!std::isfinite(v) || (!std::isnan(bandNoData) && std::abs(v - bandNoData) < 1e-4f)) out[i] = quiet_NaN(); — with bandNoData==0.0, every pixel with |v|<1e-4 (i.e. every DN==0 pixel) is written as NaN. The failing test test_radiometric_calibration.cpp:519 'processFile streams a multi-tile raster to radiance' writes DN=(x+3y)%256 (band[0]==0 at pixel (0,0)) and asserts result[i]==0.01*band[i]; rerun of the audit-build binary fails deterministically at i=0: 'nanf is within 0.001 of 0.0' (20 test cases, 1 failed, reproducible). Tiling is NOT the trigger — the same bug fires on any raster with a 0-valued DN pixel and unset NoData; the sibling single-tile test (test_radiometric_calibration.cpp:354) only passes because its fixture DNs are 100/200/50/80 (no zeros). The wrapper's own readBandWindow (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:219-226) uses the hasNodata flag correctly and its comment states the violated invariant: 'zero is a real pixel value for DN imagery and silently corrupts downstream statistics'. The test suite never pins this contract: test_gdal_wrapper.cpp:245-256 'reads band no-data value' does (void)nodata; (void)hasNodata; REQUIRE(true) — a tautology that let the misuse through.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Could not refute: deterministic failing baseline test is direct evidence; tiling NOT the trigger (single-tile sibling passes only because fixture DNs 100/200/50/80 contain no zero); test_gdal_wrapper tautology (REQUIRE(true)) verified as filed.
- **Review note**: Add sibling site: atmospheric_correction.cpp:406 has the identical 1-arg misuse with the same :426 clause (DN==0 -> NaN when NoData unset) - same fix needed there. Output band IS declared NaN-NoData (:524) so the corruption is silent drop of ~1/256 uniformly-distributed 8-bit pixels, as filed.
- **Finding TESTS-1**: `Line 530: const double bandNoData = srcDataset.bandNoDataValue(b); — the 1-arg call ignores the hasNodata out-param. GdalDatasetWrapper::bandNoDataValue (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:385-402) returns GDALGetRasterNoDataValue verbatim: 0.0 with hasNodataInt=0 when the band declares no NoData. Line 556 then applies: if (!std::isfinite(v) || (!std::isnan(bandNoData) && std::abs(v - bandNoData) < 1e-4f)) out[i] = quiet_NaN(); — with bandNoData==0.0, every pixel with |v|<1e-4 (i.e. every DN==0 pixel) is written as NaN. The failing test test_radiometric_calibration.cpp:519 'processFile streams a multi-tile raster to radiance' writes DN=(x+3y)%256 (band[0]==0 at pixel (0,0)) and asserts result[i]==0.01*band[i]; rerun of the audit-build binary fails deterministically at i=0: 'nanf is within 0.001 of 0.0' (20 test cases, 1 failed, reproducible). Tiling is NOT the trigger — the same bug fires on any raster with a 0-valued DN pixel and unset NoData; the sibling single-tile test (test_radiometric_calibration.cpp:354) only passes because its fixture DNs are 100/200/50/80 (no zeros). The wrapper's own readBandWindow (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:219-226) uses the hasNodata flag correctly and its comment states the violated invariant: 'zero is a real pixel value for DN imagery and silently corrupts downstream statistics'. The test suite never pins this contract: test_gdal_wrapper.cpp:245-256 'reads band no-data value' does (void)nodata; (void)hasNodata; REQUIRE(true) — a tautology that let the misuse through.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (TESTS-1).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #193 (line 73) is the opposite direction (ignoring DECLARED NoData); #192/#190 unrelated; no closed issue covers unset-NoData-as-0. Not a dupe.
- Finding TESTS-1: Not a dup: #193 covered atomic processors IGNORING declared NoData (opposite direction); #192/#190 covered missing masking in index/bandmath; none covered treating UNSET NoData as 0 in radiometric calibration.
title: [P2][algorithm/numerics] Radiometric calibration processFile treats NoData-unset bands as NoData=0 and NaNs every valid DN=0 pixel (deterministic, test-proven)

## Summary
Class-map writers still destructively overwrite outputs before validation and delete them on failure (#285 temp+rename fix not propagated to pipeline/class raster writers). This issue aggregates 2 related finding(s): RSCLS-3, RSHYP-2. Specifically, RsClassificationPipeline::run Create-overwrites the existing output raster and deletes it on failure — a failed re-run destroys the user's previous classification (#285 defect class, unfixed in this path). Specifically, RsClassRaster::paint/polygonize GDALCreate the output BEFORE validating the reference and before writes can fail - late failure destroys the user's previous result (#285 sibling, fix never applied here).

## Area
Algorithms / Image Processing / Numerics

## Type
algorithm/numerics

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/analysis/classification/rs_classification_pipeline.cpp:596-621 (Create on target path), 699-712 (failWithPartialOutput removes it)` (RsClassificationPipeline::run)
- `src/analysis/segmentation/rs_class_raster.cpp:paint 87-89 (GDALCreate), 98-115 (reference opened/validated AFTER create), 113/183/218 (removeIncompleteOutput); polygonize 265-266 (GDALCreate of vector), 308-364 (mask build can fail after create), 311/321/332/348/361/376 (removeIncompleteOutput)` (RsClassRaster::paint / RsClassRaster::polygonize)

## User impact
- User loses the prior classification result of a long-running whole-scene job; same data-loss class as closed issue #285 which was only fixed in rs_post_process.cpp.
- Destroys the user's previous class raster/vector on a failed re-run - the exact defect class of #285, still live in the OBIA writeback path.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (RSCLS-3)**: Re-run classification to the same output path and have any late step fail: read error at a tile, prediction exception, scaler band mismatch, or user cancel mid-predict.
- **Trigger (RSHYP-2)**: Re-run an OBIA classify/export to the same outputPath as a previous good result and hit any post-Create failure: reference grid mismatch (segment map from a different raster), disk full during row writes, or an unreadable class raster row in polygonize.

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (RSCLS-3)**: Write to a sibling temp dataset and rename on success (the exact pattern commit 26f4566474 implemented for RsPostProcess::saveLabelRaster/polygonize).
- **Expected (RSHYP-2)**: Output written atomically (temp file + rename, as implemented for #285 in classification) or at least validated before the existing file is truncated; failure leaves the previous result intact.

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (RSCLS-3)**: Previous output is truncated at Create and then QFile::remove'd by the failure handler; nothing left on disk.
- **Actual (RSHYP-2)**: GDALCreate truncates the previous output first; every late failure path then deletes it, so the user loses both the old and the new result (polygonize additionally leaves orphaned .dbf/.shx sidecars).

## Root cause
- **RSCLS-3**: CONFIRMED (rs_classification_pipeline.cpp:596-614 GTiff Create truncates existing output; failWithPartialOutput :699-712 QFile::remove's output AND probability output; reachability: rs_supervised_classification_operator.cpp:247-268 + qgsclassificationmainwindow + rs_kmeans_operator)
  - *Callchain*: `GUI Apply (module:classify:apply) and rs:supervised_classification operator -> RsClassificationPipeline::run; also the .tmp~ preview path is safe but Apply writes straight to the user-chosen output`
  - *Code context*: `GDALDataset *dstDs = drv->Create( config.outputRaster.toUtf8().constData(), outW, outH, 1, outType, papsz ); ... failWithPartialOutput: QFile::remove( config.outputRaster ); — GTiff Create truncates the existing file in place before any tile is written.`
- **RSHYP-2**: CONFIRMED (rs_class_raster.cpp paint: GDALCreate at :87 before GDALOpen(reference) at :98, grid-mismatch removeIncompleteOutput at :113; polygonize GDALCreate :265 before mask build, 6 removeIncompleteOutput sites; contrast RsSegmentMap::toGeoTIFF validates reference BEFORE create; callers rs_obia_task.cpp:183, rs_obia_main_window.cpp:1362/1642, rs_obia_hierarchy_operator.cpp:229)
  - *Callchain*: `OBIA GUI tasks: src/app/obia/rs_obia_task.cpp:183 and src/app/obia/rs_obia_main_window.cpp:1362; operators: src/operators/rs/rs_obia_hierarchy_operator.cpp:229 (and the obia_classify paint path) -> RsClassRaster::paint(segMap, segmentClasses, referenceRasterPath, outputPath, classColors) -> RsClassRaster::polygonize`
  - *Code context*: `paint: 'GDALDatasetH dstDs = GDALCreate( driver, outputPath.toUtf8().constData(), w, h, 1, outType, papszOptions );' (line 87) truncates any existing file at outputPath; only afterwards 'GDALDatasetH srcDs = GDALOpen( referenceRasterPath... )' (line 98) and on grid mismatch 'removeIncompleteOutput( outputPath ); return result;' (line 113). GTiff Create opens the file for writing immediately, so the previous output is already gone at that point; mid-write RasterIO failures likewise 'removeIncompleteOutput( outputPath )' (183, 218). polygonize creates the shapefile at line 265 before the per-row class-raster mask build (339-365) which fails closed on the first unreadable row and then deletes the .shp - leaving stale .dbf/.shx sidecars beside a deleted .shp. Contrast RsSegmentMap::toGeoTIFF (rs_segment_map.cpp:99-131) which correctly validates the reference BEFORE GDALCreate.`

## Evidence
- **Skeptic verification**: Attempted refutation 'preview path writes .tmp~ so production is safe': preview is safe but Apply and the rs: operator write straight to the user-chosen path - destructive path reachable. GTiff GDALCreate opens O_CREAT|O_TRUNC semantics so prior file is gone before first write - standard GDAL behavior, no need for empirical run.
- **Review note**: None material. Note polygonize leaves orphaned .dbf/.shx beside deleted .shp (ESRI shapefile driver sidecars) - correct as filed.
- **Finding RSCLS-3**: `GDALDataset *dstDs = drv->Create( config.outputRaster.toUtf8().constData(), outW, outH, 1, outType, papsz ); ... failWithPartialOutput: QFile::remove( config.outputRaster ); — GTiff Create truncates the existing file in place before any tile is written.`
- **Finding RSHYP-2**: `paint: 'GDALDatasetH dstDs = GDALCreate( driver, outputPath.toUtf8().constData(), w, h, 1, outType, papszOptions );' (line 87) truncates any existing file at outputPath; only afterwards 'GDALDatasetH srcDs = GDALOpen( referenceRasterPath... )' (line 98) and on grid mismatch 'removeIncompleteOutput( outputPath ); return result;' (line 113). GTiff Create opens the file for writing immediately, so the previous output is already gone at that point; mid-write RasterIO failures likewise 'removeIncompleteOutput( outputPath )' (183, 218). polygonize creates the shapefile at line 265 before the per-row class-raster mask build (339-365) which fails closed on the first unreadable row and then deletes the .shp - leaving stale .dbf/.shx sidecars beside a deleted .shp. Contrast RsSegmentMap::toGeoTIFF (rs_segment_map.cpp:99-131) which correctly validates the reference BEFORE GDALCreate.`

## Suggested fix
- Correct the mathematical formulas, coordinate system transforms, and NoData boundary conditions to align with standard GIS conventions (Horn 1981, GDAL, IEEE-754).

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (RSCLS-3, RSHYP-2).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe
- #285 (line 4) fix 26f4566474 touched ONLY rs_post_process.cpp + tests (git show --stat verified) - both members are genuine incomplete-fix siblings, not dupes.
- Finding RSCLS-3: #285 closed by 26f4566474 — git show --stat: only rs_post_process.cpp + tests touched; pipeline path still destructive at HEAD.
- Finding RSHYP-2: #285 was fixed in commit 26f4566474 which touched ONLY src/analysis/classification/rs_post_process.cpp (verified via git show --stat); git log shows rs_class_raster.cpp untouched since creation (1444e71885). Genuinely incomplete fix of #285.

## Summary
Headless rs: spectral-index/band-math/terrain operators still read raw DN without NoData masking (#192 fixed only the QGIS provider path). This issue aggregates 2 related finding(s): OPS-1, RSALGO-8. Specifically, Headless rs:spectral_index / rs:*_index / rs:band_math / rs:terrain_analysis read raw DN without NoData masking and write outputs with undeclared NoData. Specifically, rs:band_math operator path still reads raw DN with no NoData masking and writes no NoData - #192 fix covered only the QGIS provider path.

## Area
Data Model / Raster Grids / NoData & CRS

## Type
data/crs-nodata-metadata

## Severity
P2

## Baseline
- Repository: WindWang2/exp-rs
- Branch: master
- Commit: d9c59e5b8290a74cbfe6c8c9f3c7209c6cdab7dc

## Affected code
- `src/operators/rs/rs_spectral_index_operator.cpp:208-281 (spectral index); src/processing/algorithms/band_math.cpp:608-651; src/operators/rs/rs_terrain_analysis_operator.cpp:130-172; src/processing/gdal/gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:507-547` (spectral_index_detail::runSpectralIndexCore / BandMath::processFile / RsTerrainAnalysisOperator::run / writeGdalOutput)
- `src/processing/algorithms/band_math.cpp:608-651` (BandMath::processFile)

## User impact
- Silent science corruption of the flagship NDVI/indices path on every masked scene: clouds/fill turn into plausible index values; downstream operators that honor declared NoData (kmeans, rx_anomaly, apply_mask) and QGIS display treat sentinel pixels as valid data.
- rs:* operator/pipeline users (the agent/MCP surface) get different, wrong results from the identical expression run through the QGIS provider surface - same class as #192, incompletely fixed.

## Reproduction
- **Trigger (OPS-1)**: Any rs:spectral_index/rs:ndvi/rs:band_math/rs:terrain_analysis run on a raster that declares a numeric band NoData (e.g. MODIS -3000 fill, Landsat fill 0, or any -9999 product) or that contains NaN/edge NoData pixels.
- **Trigger (RSALGO-8)**: rs:band_math on a raster with any declared NoData sentinel (e.g. expression '(b1-b2)/(b1+b2)' over a scene with nodata=0)

## Expected behavior
- **Expected (OPS-1)**: Input NoData pixels propagate to the output as a declared sentinel (band NoData set on the written GeoTIFF), matching what the #192/#202 fixes did for the QGIS provider path and for SAM/RX/mosaic outputs.
- **Expected (RSALGO-8)**: NoData pixels masked to NoData in inputs and output (as the provider algorithm now does)

## Actual behavior
- **Actual (OPS-1)**: NoData DNs are fed into the index formulas (fill becomes a computed index value, e.g. -9999/-9999 -> 0) and the output Float32 bands carry NaN or the raw sentinel with no GDAL band NoData declaration.

  - *Callchain*: `MCP execute_algorithm / CLI -> JobEngine 'processing:' executor (src/app/shell/processing_job_adapter.cpp:64 adapter->execute) -> AtomicAlgorithmRegistry -> RsOperatorAdapter::execute (atomic_algorithm_adapter.cpp:302) -> RSOperator::run -> runSpectralIndexCore / BandMath::processFile; also asset_index_pipeline.cpp:112 op->execute for the GUI asset path`
  - *Code context*: `readBand() calls ds.readBandData() which is a plain GDALRasterIO float conversion (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:186-200, no NoData->NaN). Output goes through writeGdalOutput() (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:507-547) which never calls GDALSetRasterNoDataValue. Spectral indices emit NaN via MathUtils::safeDiv on 0/0 but leave the sentinel undeclared; a -9999 NoData pair gives NDVI = 0/(-19998) = 0.0 (a valid-looking value). Terrain kernels write the input `nodata` sentinel (default -9999) at image borders into the Float32 output, also undeclared. BandMath::processFile reads every band via readBandData (band_math.cpp:624-632) with the same masking gap and writes via writeGdalOutput (641-648).`
- **RSALGO-8**: CONFIRMED (band_math.cpp:608-651: readBandData raw DN for every band, evaluate, writeGdalOutput; zero NoData handling in file; rs_band_math_operator.cpp:89 calls processFile; provider contrast band_math_algorithm.cpp:100/133 masks and declares - #192 asymmetry real)
  - *Callchain*: `rs:band_math (rs_band_math_operator.cpp:89) -> BandMath::processFile:608 -> readBandData (raw DN) -> evaluate -> writeGdalOutput (no NoData declared)`
  - *Code context*: `processFile: `srcDataset.readBandData(i, buffer.data(), ...)` for every band, evaluate(), then `writeGdalOutput(...)` - zero NoData handling anywhere in the file (grep: 8 NaN matches, all expression-eval NaN semantics). The #192 fix commit 0169bd7eac added masking to the QGIS provider algorithms (band_math_algorithm.cpp:100-101 converts isNoData->NaN, :133 declares output NoData) but not to BandMath::processFile used by the rs: operator. rs_band_math_operator.cpp:89 calls processFile directly.`

## Evidence

Verified provider paths mask (spectral_index_algorithm.cpp:61-62 isNoData->NaN, :229-241 declare output NoData).
- **Review note**: OPS-1 title/scope overstates terrain: move the terrain raw-DN claim to C08's output-declaration defect. OPS-1 cited lines for terrain (130-172) show kernels receiving resolved nodata, contradicting the 'reads raw DN without NoData masking' framing for that member.
- **Finding OPS-1**: `readBand() calls ds.readBandData() which is a plain GDALRasterIO float conversion (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:186-200, no NoData->NaN). Output goes through writeGdalOutput() (gdal_dataset_wrapper.cpp:507-547) which never calls GDALSetRasterNoDataValue. Spectral indices emit NaN via MathUtils::safeDiv on 0/0 but leave the sentinel undeclared; a -9999 NoData pair gives NDVI = 0/(-19998) = 0.0 (a valid-looking value). Terrain kernels write the input `nodata` sentinel (default -9999) at image borders into the Float32 output, also undeclared. BandMath::processFile reads every band via readBandData (band_math.cpp:624-632) with the same masking gap and writes via writeGdalOutput (641-648).`
- **Finding RSALGO-8**: `processFile: `srcDataset.readBandData(i, buffer.data(), ...)` for every band, evaluate(), then `writeGdalOutput(...)` - zero NoData handling anywhere in the file (grep: 8 NaN matches, all expression-eval NaN semantics). ## Suggested fix
- Validate grid compatibility rigorously, propagate NoData masks across all processing steps, and preserve CRS/metadata on output datasets.

## Acceptance criteria
- Defect resolved for all members (OPS-1, RSALGO-8).
- CMake build and Catch2 unit test suite pass with 100% success.
- No regression in existing functionality or contracts.

## Regression tests
- Add targeted unit/integration tests covering the affected code path(s).

## Risk / compatibility
- Low risk when applying surgical, isolated fixes matching existing conventions.

## References / Dedupe

Verified at HEAD d9c59e5b: headless path still unmasked/undeclared.
- Finding RSALGO-8: #192 closed by 0169bd7eac but only in providers (verified by git show --stat); rs operator path verified defective at HEAD.
title: [P2][data/crs-nodata-metadata] Headless rs: spectral-index/band-math/terrain operators still read raw DN without NoData masking (#192 fixed only the QGIS provider path)
